# https://modryos.com/docs/

# Modryos documentation

You build the whole mod - models, animations, textures, recipes, logic and code - in one studio. AI is an optional helper.

Modryos is a desktop studio for making Minecraft Java mods. It runs on Windows. It is in closed beta, so these pages grow as the studio does.



## Find your way

Pick a section below, or use the search box at the top of the page.

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/getting-started

# Getting started

Modryos is a studio for making Minecraft mods. You build the whole mod - models, animations, textures, recipes, logic and code - in one studio. AI is an optional helper.

You do not need to know how to code. If you know Minecraft, you can start.

## The five steps

1. [Install Modryos](install.md): download it, start it, sign in.
2. [Your first mod in 10 minutes](first-mod.md): pick a sample, change one thing.
3. [Play](play.md): see your mod in the real game.
4. [Export](export.md): make the mod file you can share.
5. [Publish](publishing.md): put it on Modrinth or CurseForge.

## Good to know

- Your projects stay on your computer.
- One project can make a mod for NeoForge and Fabric. See [Versions and loaders](versions-and-loaders.md).
- Stuck? Read [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md), the [FAQ](faq.md) or [Help and community](help-and-community.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/install

# Install Modryos

## What you need

- Windows 10 or Windows 11.
- An internet connection for the first start.
- About 1.7 GB of free disk space for the game tools. The studio downloads them the first time you press [Play](glossary.md#play).
- A Minecraft Java Edition account to play your mod in the real game.

## Download

Get `Modryos-Install-<version>.exe` from the [download page](/download.html). Save it anywhere, for example in Downloads.

## Windows may warn you

For now the installer is not signed, so Windows does not know who made it yet. That is expected. If Windows stops it:

1. Press **More info** on the "Windows protected your PC" window.
2. Check that the file name is the one you downloaded.
3. Press **Run anyway**.

If the window shows **Run** at once, press it.

> **Note** On some new Windows 11 computers, Smart App Control blocks every unsigned app and shows no Run button. Turning it off cannot be undone without reinstalling Windows, so you may prefer to wait for the signed version.

## Check the file (optional)

The download page shows a SHA256 checksum for each file. To check yours, open PowerShell (the blue command window that comes with Windows: press Start, type PowerShell, press Enter) in the folder with the file and run one command. A checksum is a long code made from every byte of the file; if one byte changed, the code changes ([what is SHA256?](glossary.md#sha256)):

```
Get-FileHash .\Modryos-Install-<version>.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

Use your file's real name. The long number it prints must be the same as the one on the download page. If it is not, do not run the file. Write to support@modryos.com.

## Install

1. Run the file and press **Install**. **Options** lets you pick the folder and who it is for. The default is only for you and needs no administrator password.
2. It takes under a minute. Modryos opens when it is done.
3. Installing over an older Modryos? The button says **Update**. Your projects and sign-in stay.

## Sign in

The beta is open to invited people.

1. Type your email, tick **I am 15 or older** and the terms, and press **Send me a code**.
2. Type the 6-digit code from the email. There is no password.
3. Type the invite code from your invite email and press **Redeem**.

No invite yet? Press **Join the waiting list** on that screen.

## First start

1. Accept the terms and the Minecraft [EULA](glossary.md#eula) once. Pick how much you have made mods before. None is fine, and you can change it in Settings.
2. The studio then gets Java and the game files it needs, by itself. You install nothing else. It takes several minutes, and a bar shows how far it is. You can look around while it works.

Next: [your first mod](first-mod.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/first-mod

# Your first mod in 10 minutes

Keep this page open beside Modryos.

## 1. Start a mod

On the start screen, **What are you making today?**, start a new mod. Pick **From a sample** and then **Ruby Gear**, the first one in the list, so there is already something in it (see [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)). Press **Make my copy**. When you start a new mod yourself, keep both [loaders](glossary.md#loader) ticked under **Works with**.

![The start screen](/media/start-welcome.webp)

## 2. Follow First steps

Modryos shows a small **First steps** card with four steps: **Look**, **Change**, **Play** and **In the game**. You can open it again any time with **Help > Getting started**.

- **Look.** Click one of your things in the Project list on the left. Blocks, items and creatures open so you can see how they are made.
- **Change.** Change its name or any number you see. You can always undo it, so try anything.
- **Play.** Press **Play** at the top. Modryos builds your mod and opens Minecraft with it. The first time takes a few minutes. Keep the window open.
- **In the game.** Find your thing in the creative inventory, in your mod's own tab. The card says "Your mod is in the game. Well done!" when it sees it.

## 3. Add something of your own

Press **New thing**, pick a category such as **Blocks and items** and then **Block**. Give it a name and press **Play** again. More: [A block with your own picture](block-with-your-own-picture.md) and [Make a fire sword](make-a-fire-sword.md).

## 4. Change it again

Change a colour or a name, then press **Reload in the game**. The change shows up without restarting. Press **Stop** when you are done.

## 5. Make the mod file

Use **File > Export > Make the mod file (.jar)**. See [Export](export.md).

Next: read more about [Play](play.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/play

# Play and Stop

**Play** builds your mod and starts Minecraft with it. **Stop** closes the game again.

## Which version and loader

[Play](glossary.md#play) starts the version and [loader](glossary.md#loader) you pick in **Play on**. A project can have more than one. Pick another one there and press Play again. See [Versions and loaders](versions-and-loaders.md).

## The first start

The first time, Modryos downloads the game and its tools (about 1.7 GB) and builds your mod. That takes a few minutes. Later starts are much faster. You are asked to accept the Minecraft [EULA](glossary.md#eula) once, with **Accept and Play**.

## In the game

- Open the creative inventory and find your mod's own tab.
- Place your block and break it to see what drops.
- Open the mod list and look for your mod's name.

Change something in Modryos and press **Reload in the game**. Most changes show up without a restart. **Leave and rejoin the world** helps when one does not.

## The Cook window

[Cooking](glossary.md#cook) is how Modryos makes the mod file. Play does it for you. You can also open it with **File > Export > Make the mod file (.jar)**. It shows four steps:

1. **Write the project**
2. **Resolve what the game needs**
3. **Compile**
4. **Pack the file**

When it is done it tells you how many mod files it made. If something fails, the first red line says why. Fix it and press **Make again**.

![The Cook window with its targets](/media/cook-targets.webp)

If Play does not work, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/export

# Export your mod

The mod file is a `.jar`. It is what people put in their Minecraft `mods` folder.

## Make it

1. Choose **File > Export > Make the mod file (.jar)**. The [Cook](glossary.md#cook) window opens.
2. Press **Cook**.
3. When it is done, each file shows its full path. **Show the file** opens its folder, and **Open the folder** opens the folder with all of them.

## One jar for each version and loader

Modryos makes one [jar](glossary.md#jar) for every version and [loader](glossary.md#loader) your project [targets](glossary.md#target). A project for NeoForge and Fabric on two versions makes four jars. Each one only works on its own version and loader, so check the name before you share it. Ask your friend which loader (NeoForge or Fabric) and which Minecraft version they use, and send the jar for that pair. See [Versions and loaders](versions-and-loaders.md).

## Where they land

In your project folder, in `release`, in a folder named for the mod version. Your project's own files are never changed by this.

## Play one

Put the jar in the `mods` folder of a Minecraft with the same loader and version. Fabric mods also need [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) in the same folder.

Next: [Publish your mod](publishing.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/help-and-community

# Help and community

## The Help menu

- **Getting started** walks you through your first mod.
- **Documentation** opens these guides in your browser.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** lists every key you can press, and lets you search.
- **Help for this editor** opens the guide page for the editor you are in.
- **What's new** shows what changed in this version.
- **Contact support** writes an email to the Modryos team. It starts with the version you use.
- **The Modryos community** opens the place where makers help each other.
- **Report a problem** shows what would go in a report first, and saves nothing until you say yes.

## Report a problem

Press **F6** or choose **Help > Report a problem**. Write one line about what you expected. You see everything that goes in the report before it is saved.

## Contact support

Write to support@modryos.com. A person reads it.

## The Modryos community

Join other makers on Discord: https://discord.com/invite/ccWxeu8BVh

Also see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) and the [FAQ](faq.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/make-a-fire-sword

# Make a fire sword

Two ways. The first is the quickest.

## Way 1: the setting

1. Press **New thing**.
2. Open **Blocks and items** and pick **Weapon**.
3. Give it a **Name**, for example Flame Blade.
4. Find **Sets alight for** and type a number of seconds, for example 5. Nought sets nothing alight.
5. Press **Play**. In the game, find the sword in your mod's creative tab and hit a cow.

## Way 2: a rule

Use this when you want more than fire, such as a sound too.

1. Open your sword in the Project list on the left and click its **Behavior** tab.
2. Under **Or start with an example**, press **Set on fire** ("Whatever it hits catches fire.").
3. Or build it yourself: press **Add a moment** and pick **When (this) hits something**. Then press **Add a line** and pick **Set (who) on fire for (seconds) seconds**.
4. Change the seconds, then press **Play**.

More: [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Behavior](thing-behaviour.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/block-with-your-own-picture

# A block with your own picture

1. Press **New thing**, open **Blocks and items** and pick **Block**. Give it a **Name**.
2. Press **New thing** again, open **Mobs and models** and pick **Texture**. This is the picture, and its page is the painter: it opens by itself when you make it, and again when you click the texture in the project list. Give it a name.
3. Pick the size under **How big to start**: **16 by 16**, **32 by 32** or **64 by 64**. Minecraft's own blocks are 16 by 16, so choose that to match the game. Bigger sizes show finer detail.
4. Either draw it, or bring one in:
   - **Draw:** pick a colour, press **Fill**, then paint pixel by pixel with the painter's tools.
   - **Bring one in:** press **Import a PNG** and choose the file.
5. Press **Apply** to keep the picture.
6. Open your block. In **Texture**, choose your picture.
7. Press **Play** and place the block.

More on pictures: [Pictures and textures](pictures-and-textures.md). A texture is just a PNG.

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/make-a-creature

# Make a creature

1. Press **New thing**, open **Mobs and models** and pick **Mob**.
2. Give it a **Name**.
3. In **Made from the game's**, write the game's creature it behaves like, for example zombie or cow. Empty makes a creature of your own.
4. Set **Health** (a player has 20) and **Temperament**: Passive, Neutral or Hostile.
5. Optional: choose **Its own picture** so it wears a new look. Make the picture as in [Pictures and textures](pictures-and-textures.md).
6. Press **Play**. A spawn egg for it is in your mod's creative tab.

More: [Mob editor](editor-creature.md).

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/pictures-and-textures

# Pictures and textures

A texture is the picture a block, item or creature wears. It is a PNG file.

## Draw one

1. **New thing > Mobs and models > Texture**.
2. Under **How big to start**, pick **16 by 16**, **32 by 32** or **64 by 64**.
3. Pick a colour and press **Fill**, then paint with the tools.
4. Press **Apply**.

## Bring one in

In the Texture editor press **Import a PNG** and choose the file. To bring in many, use **Import pictures** or **Import a folder**. To use a picture you already have, press **Choose a texture**.

## Sizes

16 by 16 matches Minecraft's blocks and items. 32 by 32 and 64 by 64 give finer detail. You can change it later with **Resize the picture**.

## A strip of frames

A picture made of squares one above the other, like a film strip. The game shows the squares one after another, so the picture moves, like water. Turn it on with the **Plays as frames** setting of the block or item.

## Replaces

The **Replaces** setting is only for taking the place of a picture the game already has, for example `minecraft:block/stone`. Leave it empty for your own.

See the [Texture editor](editor-texture.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editors

# Editors

Each editor is where you set one kind of thing. Pick one to see its settings.

## Blocks and items

- [Area value](editor-areaValue.md): A number the world keeps by place, not by player or item: an aura in each chunk, an oil reservoir under it, radiation, a corruption that spreads, a pollution.
- [Banner pattern](editor-bannerPattern.md): A pattern woven on a banner in the loom, and shown on a shield.
- [Block](editor-block.md): Something placed in the world: ore, stone, a crate.
- [Boat](editor-boat.md): A boat or a raft a player rows on water, with a chest or not.
- [Forms for every material](editor-formSet.md): Makes a dust, a plate, a gear or any other form for every metal and gem the game has when it starts, other mods too.
- [Gene](editor-gene.md): A trait any thing can carry and pass to its young: a number such as Growth, or one of a few choices such as Coat colour.
- [Item](editor-item.md): Something held in the hand or kept in a chest.
- [Material](editor-material.md): What parts are cut from, any item the game's iron ingot among them: its color, and the numbers and abilities it gives a part.
- [Satellite](editor-satellite.md): A launched thing that watches a place and reports back.
- [Space station](editor-spaceStation.md): A built place in a dimension of its own that anyone or any vehicle docks with, orbiting a world at a height that rules move.
- [Species](editor-species.md): A kind of bee, plant or animal: the gene values it starts with, what it looks like as a block, an item or a mob, and which two species bred give it.
- [Spell](editor-spell.md): A spell of its own: what it does as rules (when it is cast, when it reaches a mob or a block, every tick it is kept up), what it costs (mana or any value), its cooldown and charge-up, and how it reaches: on the caster, along a ray, as a missile or all around.
- [Value](editor-value.md): A number or a list kept by an item, the player, a team or the world: Energy, XP, Kills, the foods a player has eaten.
- [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md): Something to ride that is not alive, beyond the boat: a cart, a motor boat, a broom or an airship, a minecart of its own, a ride along a path.
- [World event](editor-worldEvent.md): Something that happens to a whole dimension for a while: a blood sky, a fog bank, an aurora, a rift.

## Crafting and loot

- [Armor trim](editor-armourTrim.md): A trim put on armor at the smithing table, in any of the game's materials.
- [Condition](editor-condition.md): A test in plain words, like half of the time, only in a biome, only at night.
- [Drop](editor-drop.md): What falls out when a block breaks or a mob dies.
- [Effect](editor-effect.md): Something that happens to a mob for a while.
- [Enchantment](editor-enchantment.md): A power added to a tool or weapon.
- [Extras for an item](editor-itemExtras.md): What any item, the game's or yours, also does: composts, burns in a furnace, or what a dispenser does with it.
- [Game thing changed](editor-gameChange.md): One of the game's own blocks, items or mobs given new values, such as a block's hardness, an item's stack size or a mob's health, a structure the game makes no more, or a limit the game sets, such as the anvil's most cost.
- [Item change](editor-itemChange.md): What happens to an item after it is made: its count, its wear, a name, a lore line, a random enchantment.
- [Loot changed](editor-lootChange.md): What the game's own blocks, mobs and chests drop, changed in place: things taken out, or one thing given in place of another.
- [Loot table](editor-lootTable.md): A weighted list of what can come out, rolled by a quest, a crate, a mob's or a block's drop, or a rule.
- [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md): What one machine of yours turns into something else, and what it costs.
- [Other mod's recipe](editor-modRecipe.md): A recipe for a machine from a mod yours builds on, filled in by clicks.
- [Potion](editor-potion.md): A drink that gives an effect.
- [Recipe](editor-recipe.md): Make something in a crafting table, furnace, stonecutter or smithing table.
- [Recipe change](editor-recipeChange.md): Change a recipe the game or another mod already has.
- [Recipes taken away](editor-recipesRemoved.md): Take recipes the game has out of the game.
- [Ritual](editor-ritual.md): Offerings on pedestals around an altar, a catalyst on the altar, the conditions it asks, and the result it leaves on the altar.
- [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md): A recipe done on a station's own screen, with cells, tanks and energy.
- [Villager trade](editor-villagerTrade.md): What a villager offers and asks for.

## Machines and networks

- [Custom kind](editor-matter.md): A matter of your own beside energy and fluid: a chemical, mana, heat, whatever your mod calls it.
- [Fluid](editor-fluid.md): A liquid that flows in the world and fills a bucket, as water does.
- [When fluids meet](editor-fluidReactions.md): What happens where a fluid meets another fluid or a block: lava meeting water makes obsidian, your own fluid meeting lava makes a block or drops an item.

## Mobs and models

- [Animation](editor-animation.md): How a model moves over time.
- [Attribute](editor-attribute.md): A number every living thing has, as luck and armor are.
- [Damage change](editor-damageChange.md): A hurt a living thing takes, changed or cancelled by who takes it, who deals it and what it is, on every game version, without code of yours inside the game's own.
- [Mob](editor-creature.md): A living thing with a model, animations and behavior.
- [Mob behaviour](editor-mobBehaviour.md): A piece of your own code that joins one activity of a mob's brain, the game's or another mod's.
- [Model](editor-model.md): The shape of a block, item or mob, made from boxes.
- [Movement](editor-movement.md): How a living thing moves, the player or a mob: its speed and its jump, and a class of yours run as it moves.
- [Painting](editor-painting.md): A picture hung on a wall.
- [Particle](editor-particle.md): Sparks, smoke, dust and the like.
- [Projectile](editor-projectile.md): A thing that flies, drawn by a model: a spell, a dart, a boomerang, a homing missile.
- [Sound](editor-sound.md): A sound the game plays.
- [Texture](editor-texture.md): The pixels a block, item or mob wears.
- [The player](editor-player.md): The game's own player: its body, and rules for its moments, such as when it eats, is hurt or joins.
- [Thing](editor-thing.md): Something in the world that is not a mob and does not fly: a spell's ward, a frame on a wall, a floating orb, a balloon on a string, a trap.
- [Villager job](editor-villagerProfession.md): A job a villager takes at its workstation, with its coat and its trades.
- [Worn slots](editor-wornSlots.md): Slots you name on any mob, the game's own or yours: a hat on a cow, boots on its four legs, a saddle on a pig, armor on a wolf.

## Logic and code

- [Another mod](editor-dependency.md): A mod this one uses or works with, such as a recipe viewer: built against, in the test game, and named in both manifests.
- [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md): What happens when something happens: when this sword hits, set the target on fire.
- [Code](editor-code.md): A Java class of your own, kept safe when the mod is rebuilt.
- [Command](editor-command.md): A command typed in chat with a slash, whose rules run when a player types it.
- [Commands to run](editor-function.md): A list of the game's commands run together by name, when a world loads, or every tick.
- [Damage type](editor-damageType.md): A way of getting hurt, with its own message.
- [File of your own](editor-ownFile.md): Any file the mod ships as it is, under resources/: data, assets, anything the game reads.
- [Game rule](editor-gameRule.md): A rule of the world, set with the gamerule command.
- [Locks](editor-locks.md): What a player may not use, wear, break, place, hit, enter or ride until they reach a skill level, a value or an advancement.
- [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md): A setting players can change after the mod is built, in its settings file: a number, on or off, one word out of a list, or a list of entries they edit.
- [Tag](editor-tag.md): A named group of blocks or items other rules can point at.
- [Translation](editor-translation.md): The names of your things in another language.
- [Word of your own](editor-ownWord.md): A few lines you name once and use in any rule as one line: it is given as many things as it needs, and it can give back an answer.

## The world

- [Biome](editor-biome.md): A region of the world with its own look and life.
- [Caves](editor-carver.md): Caves, ravines or Nether tunnels the world cuts into its ground.
- [Dimension](editor-dimension.md): A whole other world reached through a portal.
- [Feature](editor-feature.md): Something the world grows as it is made: a patch of flowers, a tree, a boulder, a lake, a vein of a block.
- [Structure](editor-structure.md): A building or ruin placed in the world.
- [World type](editor-worldType.md): A choice on the game's Create New World screen.

## Screens and guides

- [Advancement](editor-advancement.md): One of the game's own advancements: a goal with a toast, reached by an item, a kill or a rule.
- [Chest menu](editor-chestMenu.md): A chest's screen of items, one to six rows of nine, opened by a rule for one player; each item runs its own lines when clicked, and nothing can be taken from it.
- [Creative tab](editor-creativeTab.md): A tab of the creative inventory with the things you put in it, or your things added to one of the game's tabs.
- [Drawing in the world](editor-worldDraw.md): Drawn in the world from what the player looks at: an outline, the vein a key will break, a beam from the hand.
- [Guide book](editor-guideBook.md): A book of pages about the mod: words, pictures, items and recipes.
- [HUD drawing in code](editor-hudDraw.md): Your own code that draws on the HUD every frame, in a box you place on the screen.
- [HUD number bar](editor-hud.md): One number of the player shown over the game as a bar or words, like saturation above the hunger bar.
- [Key binding](editor-keyBinding.md): A key players press to do something of yours.
- [Quests](editor-questBook.md): Chapters of quests a player finishes for rewards, read in a book of the mod's own, each quest placed on its chapter's page.
- [Screen](editor-screen.md): A screen of the mod's own, laid out by dragging: opened by a rule, or shown always over the game.
- [Skill](editor-skill.md): A skill with levels, like Mining or Farming: XP comes from any moment, each level reached runs its rewards, and locks may wait for a level.
- [Skill tree](editor-skillTree.md): Skills a player buys with points, each after the ones it needs.
- [Tooltip lines](editor-tooltip.md): Lines added to the tooltip of any item or block, the mod's or the game's, or of every item, each filled in from the item's numbers and values and shown by its own condition.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-advancement

# Advancement editor

One of the game's own advancements: a goal with a toast, reached by an item, a kill or a rule.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Advancement

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The title the game shows in its toast and its advancements screen. |
| Game name | The name the mod knows it by. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Words | The line under the title. |
| Picture | The item drawn beside its title. |
| Reached by | Having an item, killing a mob, a rule that grants it, or any of the things the game watches for. Choose one of: Having an item, Killing a mob, A rule, Anything the game watches for. |
| Item | The item a player must have. |
| Mob | The mob a player must kill, chosen from the list. |
| Needs | Whether a player must do all of these things, or any one of them. Choose one of: All of them, Any one of them. |
| Things to do | What the player does to reach this, each from the game's own list. |
| Only when | A condition the player must pass for this to count. |
| After | The advancement it follows in the advancements screen. With none, it starts a tab of its own. |
| Frame | How its picture is framed: a task, a goal or a challenge. Choose one of: Task, Goal, Challenge. |
| Experience | The experience a player is given on reaching it. From 0 to 100000. |
| Said in chat | Whether the chat says who reached it. |
| Hidden until reached | Whether it stays out of the advancements screen until a player reaches it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Condition](editor-condition.md).

## Picture

![Advancement editor](/media/docs/editor-advancement.webp)

## Related pages

- [Advancement](thing-advancement.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-animation

# Animation editor

How a model moves over time.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Animation
- New thing > Mobs and models > Player animation

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you, shown in the project and on a mob's Animations tab. Players never see it. |
| Model | The model whose parts this animation moves. It has to be one made for a mob, because the animation is kept by that model's parts. |
| Keys | How each part turns, moves and grows over time. Edited on the Animate tab. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

These point at it: [Projectile](editor-projectile.md), [Thing](editor-thing.md), [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md).

## Picture

![Animation editor](/media/docs/editor-animation.webp)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-dependency

# Another mod editor

A mod this one uses or works with, such as a recipe viewer: built against, in the test game, and named in both manifests.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Another mod

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The mod's name, as players know it. |
| Store name | The name this mod has on the store, kept when you add it from there so it can be fetched again for other versions. |
| Mod id on NeoForge | Its id on NeoForge, written into this mod's manifest. Leave it empty when it is not on NeoForge. |
| Mod id on Fabric | Its id on Fabric, written into this mod's manifest. Leave it empty when it is not on Fabric. |
| Its NeoForge jar | The other mod's jar for NeoForge, picked from disk. Its things join every picker; your code compiles against it. |
| Its Fabric jar | The other mod's jar for Fabric, picked from disk. Its things join every picker; your code compiles against it. |
| Its jars | The other mod's jars, one for NeoForge and one for Fabric on each game version this mod is made for, picked from disk or fetched from the mod store. Its things join every picker; your code compiles against them; the test game runs with them. Each row has: Jar, Made for, Game version, Is. |
| This mod adds to it | This mod is an add-on of it. Its area values, kinds of energy, genes, species and studies show in your lists by their names, and your species join its genes. |
| Needed | Required: a player must install it. Optional: this mod works with it when it is there. Choose one of: Required, Optional. |
| From version | The lowest version of it this mod works with. |
| NeoForge jar is for | The game version its NeoForge jar is made for, read from the jar. Only that version compiles against it. |
| Fabric jar is for | The game version its Fabric jar is made for, read from the jar. Only that version compiles against it. |
| Published at | The Maven repository it is published in, when it is not Maven Central or one NeoForge and Fabric already know. |
| Compiled against | Coordinates both targets compile against, such as its common API; several separated by spaces. Each is group:name:version, as the mod's page for developers lists it, such as com.example:examplemod-common-api:1.0.0. |
| NeoForge: compiled against | Coordinates NeoForge alone compiles against; several separated by spaces. Each is group:name:version, as the mod's page for developers lists it, such as com.example:examplemod-common-api:1.0.0. |
| NeoForge: in the test game | Coordinates of the mod itself, loaded in NeoForge's test game. |
| Fabric: compiled against | Coordinates Fabric alone compiles against; several separated by spaces. Each is group:name:version, as the mod's page for developers lists it, such as com.example:examplemod-common-api:1.0.0. |
| Fabric: in the test game | Coordinates of the mod itself, loaded in Fabric's test game. |
| Carried inside | This mod's jar carries it, so a player installs nothing more: for a library, never for a mod players install on their own. |
| Finds your classes as | On Fabric, the entry points it looks up, each name=class, such as examplemod_plugin=mod.mymod.MyPlugin. NeoForge finds a plugin by its annotation. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Another mod editor](/media/docs/editor-dependency.webp)

## Related pages

- [Another mod](thing-dependency.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-areaValue

# Area value editor

A number the world keeps by place, not by player or item: an aura in each chunk, an oil reservoir under it, radiation, a corruption that spreads, a pollution. Where it is kept, how it starts, spreads and comes back, and what happens as it rises or falls are its own; rules read, add, take and set it at any place.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Area value

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the value is called in the game, such as Aura or Oil. |
| Game name | The value's game name in the game; the world saves it by this, and rules of another mod read it by it. |
| Kept by another mod | Another mod's area value this one stands for, such as its aura. Your rules read and change that mod's amount, hear when it rises or falls, and your HUD shows it. |
| Kept for each | The area that holds one number: each chunk (16 by 16 blocks, all the way down), each square of chunks, each biome, or each dimension. Choose one of: Chunk, Square of chunks, Biome, Dimension, Block, Sealed room. |
| Square size | How many chunks across one square is. From 2 to 64 chunks. |
| Starts as | What a place has the first time it is asked of: the number below, a random number between the two (the same in the same world), or a smooth noise between them so nearby places are alike. Choose one of: The number, Random in a range, Smooth noise. |
| Starts at | What a place starts with, or the low end of its range. A formula of the place may stand in, such as its height. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Up to | The high end of the range a place starts in. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Noise size | How many areas across one hill of the noise is: more makes wider patches. From 1 to 256. |
| Chance of any | How many places in a hundred start with any at all; the rest start at the least, as most chunks hold no oil. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Starts elsewhere | Other numbers where a place is in a biome, a group of biomes (#) or a dimension, the first that holds: more oil under deserts, no aura in the Nether. Each row has: Where, From, To. |
| Least | It never goes below this. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Most | It never goes above this; a HUD bar is full at it. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Comes back | How much it moves back by itself each second, as an aura recovers or radiation fades. Nought leaves it to the rules. A place far from everyone is caught up when next asked. From 0 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Comes back by | So much a second, or so many in a hundred of the way left a second (fast at first, slow near the end). Choose one of: An amount, A share of the way. |
| Comes back to | Where it settles: where the place started, its least, or its most. Choose one of: Where it started, Its least, Its most. |
| Spreads | How much of the difference with each area beside it moves across each second, in a hundred. Nought keeps each area to itself. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Spreads how | Evens out, more flowing to less as an aura does; or grows outward from the areas at or above a level without them losing any, as a corruption does. Choose one of: Evens out, Grows outward. |
| Grows from | Only areas at or above this number grow into the areas beside them. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Swings through the day | How far the number rises at noon and falls at midnight, as a temperature does. Nought leaves the day out of it. A place reads its kept number plus this swing plus the blocks that push it. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Swings through the year | How far the number rises, then falls, once in a year of the days below. Nought leaves the seasons out. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| A year is | How many game days one swing through the year takes. From 2 to 1000 days. |
| Blocks that push it | A block that raises or lowers the number round it, within a radius: a heater, a climatiser, a vent. Every such block near a place counts. The number is read at the place, not kept. Each row has: Block, Pushes by, Within, Reaches. |
| Blocks it turns | Where the number is high enough, blocks of a kind turn into another kind: grass into a dead grass, stone into a rot. A turn can need a block of another kind beside it, which makes it spread block to block. Each row has: Block that turns, Becomes, Only beside, Chance each try, Where it is at least, Each turn adds. |
| Blocks that hold it back | Where one of these blocks stands within its reach, nothing turns: a ward, a purifier. Each row has: Block, Holds within. |
| Tries a second | How many random places round each player the game tries to turn each second. More tries spread faster and cost more. From 1 to 2000 perSecond. |
| Tries out to | How many blocks from each player the tries reach. From 4 to 64 blocks. |
| Vent blocks | A closed space with one of these blocks touching it keeps a number of its own, found by a fill from the place: air, pressure, heat. Open to the outside, too big, or with no vent, a place reads the outside number (the dimension's). Each row has: Block, Gives a second. |
| A new room starts at | What a room holds the first time it is sealed. Outside, the number starts as the settings above say, so an airless world can start at nought. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Biggest room | How many blocks of open space count as one room. A bigger space, or one with a hole to the outside, is not sealed. From 8 to 4000 blocks. |
| A step every | How often the blocks that hold it make, burn, cool, lose and pass it on: 20 ticks is a second. From 1 to 1200 ticks. |
| Found within | How far around each player blocks that hold it are found by themselves; blocks touching ones already found are found too, at any distance. From 0 to 32 blocks. |
| Blocks that hold it | Each kind of block that holds the number, such as a reactor's fuel cells, its casing and a heat sink, and how each passes it on, makes it, loses it and what happens at its limit. Each row has: Block, Passes on, Makes, Loses, Limit, At the limit, Turns into, Blast power, Lights at, Fuel let in, Lights when it holds, Uses up, Fuel let in by. |
| Makes more beside | A block makes more for each touching block of a kind, as a fuel cell beside a moderator does. Each touching block counts once. Each row has: Block, For each touching, More each step. |
| Burns fuel | A block makes it only while it burns fuel from its own slots or tank, as a reactor cell burns fuel rods or a burner burns oil. Each row has: Block, Fuel, Burns each step, Gives, Leaves, How many left. |
| Cooled by | A block that turns a fluid in its tank into another by the number it holds, as water boils into steam: the number falls, the hot fluid goes into a touching block that takes it. Each row has: Block, Takes fluid, Makes fluid, Most each step, Takes each mB. |
| Made from a fluid | A block makes it by turning a fluid in its tank into another, as a turbine turns steam or a hot loop gives its heat. The new fluid goes into a touching block that takes it. Each row has: Block, Uses fluid, Makes fluid, Most each step, Gives each mB. |
| Made from another value | A block makes it each step from another value it holds, as neutron flux makes heat in a reactor's cells. Each row has: Block, Other value, Times. |
| Turns into energy | A block turns what it holds above its start into energy in its own store, as a generator turns rotation into power. Each row has: Block, Most each step, Energy each. |
| Only in a formed build | Blocks hold it only while they are part of a formed build, and each formed build counts as one, so a reactor works only once it is complete. |
| Redstone stops it | While a block of a build gets a redstone signal, the blocks joined to it make and burn nothing, as a reactor's shutdown lever does. Coolant and losing go on. |
| Starts again below | A build stopped by a limit starts again once its highest block falls below this. Nought or less keeps it stopped until it is rebuilt. From -1000000000 to 1000000000. |
| Kept going within | How many chunks around each player spread and run the value's every-second moment; places further out wait until they are asked. From 0 to 16 chunks. |
| Shown to players | Each player's game is told the value where the player stands, so a HUD element can draw it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [World event](editor-worldEvent.md), [Recipe](editor-recipe.md), [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md), [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md), [Ritual](editor-ritual.md), [HUD number bar](editor-hud.md), [Species](editor-species.md).

## Picture

![Area value editor](/media/docs/editor-areaValue.webp)

## Related pages

- [Area value](thing-areaValue.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-armourTrim

# Armor trim editor

A trim put on armor at the smithing table, in any of the game's materials.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Armor trim

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The trim's name; the game says it as the name and Armor Trim. |
| Game name | The trim's name in the game, as a command or a data pack names it. |
| On armor | The trim on a helmet, chestplate and boots, in the game's eight greys: each material colours them. |
| On leggings | The trim on leggings, in the same greys. |
| Template picture | The smithing template's picture, which puts the trim on armor. |
| Drawn over dye | Whether the trim is drawn as it is over dyed leather, as the game's own decal trims are. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Armor trim editor](/media/docs/editor-armourTrim.webp)

## Related pages

- [Armor trim](thing-armourTrim.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-attribute

# Attribute editor

A number every living thing has, as luck and armor are.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Attribute

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The attribute's name, as an item's tooltip shows it. |
| Game name | The attribute's name in the game, as the attribute command and a rule's words name it. |
| Starts at | What every living thing has until an item, an effect or a rule changes it. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Lowest | The lowest and the highest it can be, however much is added. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Highest | The lowest and the highest it can be, however much is added. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Sent to players | Whether a player's game hears it, so the player's side can read it. |
| Given by | Items that give some of it while held or worn, as a sword gives attack damage. Each row has: Item, Gives, While. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Attribute editor](/media/docs/editor-attribute.webp)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-bannerPattern

# Banner pattern editor

A pattern woven on a banner in the loom, and shown on a shield.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Banner pattern

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The pattern's name, as the loom and a banner's tooltip show it after the colour. |
| Game name | The pattern's name in the game, as a command or a data pack names it. |
| On a banner | The pattern on the banner's cloth, white where it shows: the loom dyes it. |
| On a shield | The pattern on a shield's face, white where it shows. |
| Needs its item | Whether the loom offers it only with its pattern item, as the globe. Off, it is always offered. |
| Item picture | The pattern item's picture, held and in the loom's slot. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-behaviour

# Behavior editor

What happens when something happens: when this sword hits, set the target on fire.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Behavior

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What to call this behaviour in the tree. |
| Belongs to | The block or item that does this. |
| Rules | What happens, and when. Edited on the thing's Behavior tab. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Projectile](editor-projectile.md), [Thing](editor-thing.md), [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md), [Spell](editor-spell.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [World event](editor-worldEvent.md), [Satellite](editor-satellite.md), [Space station](editor-spaceStation.md), [When fluids meet](editor-fluidReactions.md), [The player](editor-player.md), [Screen](editor-screen.md), [Command](editor-command.md), [Key binding](editor-keyBinding.md), [Skill tree](editor-skillTree.md), [Quests](editor-questBook.md), [Guide book](editor-guideBook.md), [Word of your own](editor-ownWord.md), [Chest menu](editor-chestMenu.md).

## An example

To make a sword set things on fire, see [Make a fire sword](make-a-fire-sword.md). It uses one rule, step by step.

## Picture

![Behavior editor](/media/docs/editor-behaviour.webp)

## Related pages

- [Behavior](thing-behaviour.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-biome

# Biome editor

A region of the world with its own look and life.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Biome

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Its name, which the game shows where it names the biome a player stands in. |
| Game name | The biome's name in the game, as a command finds it: /locate biome. |
| Grass | The colour of its grass. |
| Leaves | The colour of the leaves of its trees and vines. |
| Water | The colour of its water. |
| Sky | The colour of its sky by day. |
| Fog | The colour of the haze in the distance. |
| Under water | The colour of the haze a swimmer sees under its water. |
| In the air | Specks that drift in its air, as the ash of the nether. |
| How many | How thick the specks are. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Music | What plays while a player is there. Left empty, the game's own music plays. |
| Always heard | A sound that plays over and over while a player is there, as the nether's hum. |
| Now and then | A sound heard now and then, as the nether's distant groans. |
| Mobs | What lives there. Each is as likely as its weight beside the others of its group. Each row has: Mob, Group, Weight, At least, At most. |
| Ores and caves | The game's own ores, geodes, dungeons, springs and lava lakes, as under its plains. |
| Grass and flowers | The game's own grass, flowers, oaks, mushrooms, pumpkins and sugar cane, as on its plains. |
| Caves in it | Your own caves, or the game's, that are cut into this biome, besides the usual ones. |
| Caves and ravines | Whether caves and ravines are cut into its ground. |
| Ground on top | The block on top of its ground in a dimension of yours with hills or shaped land. In the overworld, lay blocks with Its ground. |
| Ground below | The blocks just under the top in a dimension of yours with hills. |
| Its ground | Blocks laid in its ground by where they are: on top, under the top, on steep slopes, under water, on cave ceilings, below or above a height. The first row that fits a block wins; the top and under blocks lie beneath them all. Each row has: Block, Where, Depth, Height, Patches. |
| Appears | Where the world makes it. A dimension of yours lists its own biomes too. Choose one of: In the overworld, In the nether, Only in a dimension of yours. |
| Placed | Beside one of the game's biomes, in a share of its places; or by its land, in a share of every place of the warmth, wetness and land you choose, so it stands on land of that height and roughness. Choose one of: Beside one of the game's, By its land. |
| In place of | One of the game's biomes: yours appears where it would, in a share of its places. |
| Land | The shape of the land it takes. Its height and roughness come from there: lowlands are flat, mountains steep, valleys low beside rivers, caves under the ground. Choose one of: Any land, Ocean, Coast, Lowlands, Hills, Mountains, Peaks, Valleys, Caves underground. |
| Warmth | How warm the places it takes are, in the game's five bands. Choose one of: Any, Frozen, Cold, Mild, Warm, Hot. |
| Wetness | How wet the places it takes are, from desert dry to jungle wet. Choose one of: Any, Arid, Dry, Middling, Wet, Very wet. |
| Share | How much of that biome's land becomes yours. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| Land height | How far above or below its dimension's land height its ground stands, in a dimension with a shaped land. From -48 to 96 blocks. |
| Roughness | How rough its ground is: nought is flat, a hundred is steep hills and cliffs. Its dimension's hilliness scales it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Weather | What falls from its sky. Choose one of: Rain, Snow, Nothing, dry as a desert. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Caves](editor-carver.md), [Block](editor-block.md).

These point at it: [Feature](editor-feature.md), [Structure](editor-structure.md), [Dimension](editor-dimension.md).

## Picture

![Biome editor](/media/docs/editor-biome.webp)

## Related pages

- [Biome](thing-biome.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-block

# Block editor

Something placed in the world: ore, stone, a crate.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Block
- New thing > Machines and networks > Machine
- New thing > Machines and networks > Generator
- New thing > Machines and networks > Cable
- New thing > Machines and networks > Pipe
- New thing > Machines and networks > Item pipe
- New thing > Machines and networks > Tank
- New thing > Machines and networks > Transmitter
- New thing > Machines and networks > Receiver
- New thing > Machines and networks > Wireless energy node
- New thing > Machines and networks > Shared chest
- New thing > Machines and networks > Shared tank
- New thing > Machines and networks > Chest
- New thing > Machines and networks > Drawer
- New thing > Machines and networks > Storage crate
- New thing > Machines and networks > Mailbox
- New thing > Machines and networks > Trade station
- New thing > Machines and networks > Asking chest
- New thing > Machines and networks > Terminal
- New thing > Machines and networks > Storage cell
- New thing > Machines and networks > Storage cable
- New thing > Machines and networks > Drive
- New thing > Machines and networks > Network heart
- New thing > Machines and networks > Dense cable
- New thing > Machines and networks > Link
- New thing > Machines and networks > Access point
- New thing > Machines and networks > Crafter
- New thing > Machines and networks > Pattern table
- New thing > Machines and networks > Matter tank
- New thing > Machines and networks > Altar
- New thing > Machines and networks > Pedestal
- New thing > Machines and networks > Formed machine
- New thing > Machines and networks > Machine casing
- New thing > The world > Waypoint
- New thing > Machines and networks > Aiming block
- New thing > The world > Berry bush
- New thing > Machines and networks > Matter pipe
- New thing > Blocks and items > Assembly station
- New thing > Blocks and items > Carved block
- New thing > Blocks and items > Ore
- New thing > Blocks and items > Crop
- New thing > Blocks and items > Plant

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players read in the game, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. You can change it any time. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Texture | The picture on every face of the block. |
| Shape | A shape of your own for this block to wear instead of a plain cube. Leave it empty and the block stays a cube. |
| Light (0 to 15) | How much light the block gives off, from 0 to 15. A torch is 14. From 0 to 15. |
| Time to break | How hard the block is; stone is 1.5, dirt 0.5. Higher is slower; obsidian is 50. The overview shows the seconds by hand. From 0 to 3600. |
| Tooltip lines | Extra lines under its Name when a player points at it, such as "Tastes like thunder.". The Name itself is set above. Each row has: Words, Color. |
| Plays as frames | Which of the block's pictures play as a strip of frames, and how fast. It is set on the picture itself. |
| Blocks across | How many blocks wide its front is, from 1 to 5. From 1 to 5. |
| Blocks up | How many blocks tall it is, from 1 to 5. From 1 to 5. |
| Blocks back | How many blocks deep it is, away from whoever places it, from 1 to 5. From 1 to 5. |
| Sounds like | The game's own sounds of a sort of block, for breaking it, walking on it and placing it. Choose one of: Stone, Wood, Gravel, Grass, Metal, Glass, Wool, Sand, Snow, Amethyst, Copper, Deepslate, Netherite, Bone, Honey, Slime, Mud, Bamboo, Cherry wood, Chain, Lantern. |
| Breaking sound | A sound, the game's or your own, played when it is broken, in place of its sort's. |
| Step sound | A sound, the game's or your own, played when something walks on it, in place of its sort's. |
| Placing sound | A sound, the game's or your own, played when it is placed, in place of its sort's. |
| Gives off | A particle, the game's or your own, it gives off now and then from its top, as a torch gives off smoke. |
| Made from the game's | The game's own thing this one behaves like; its behaviour stays the game's. A block kind from the game, such as grass or ice, written with its game name. Empty: a plain block. |
| Form | The game's own shapes, each drawn from this block's picture and working as the game's own does: stairs you walk up, a slab that doubles, a fence and a wall that join their neighbours, a door and a trapdoor that open, a button and a pressure plate that give a redstone signal, a pane, a carpet, leaves that fall away when no log is near, a pillar that lies the way it is placed, and a rail the game's carts ride. Choose one of: A full block, Stairs, A slab, A wall, A fence, A fence gate, A door, A trapdoor, A pressure plate, A button, A pane, as glass and bars, A carpet, Leaves, A pillar, as a log, A rail, A slope, A slope, outer corner, A slope, inner corner, A ridge, as a roof top, A quarter round, as an arch, A round pillar, A window frame. |
| Wears the block used on it | Off, the shape shows this block's own picture. On, a player can use any full block on it, from this mod, the game or another mod, and the shape then shows that block's pictures instead, grass and leaves colours included. Using nothing while sneaking gives the block back, and breaking the shape gives it back too. The slope, corners, ridge, quarter round, round pillar and window frame turn to face you and hang upside down when placed on a ceiling or on the top half of a side, like stairs. |
| Turns carts | Whether a cart rolling onto it goes off to one side instead of straight on: never, while redstone powers it, or by the cart, when the cart matches the list below. Lay track on three sides of it, like a T. Choose one of: Never, While powered, By the cart. |
| Turns to | The side a turned cart goes off to, as the cart sees it coming in: its left or its right. Choose one of: Left, Right. |
| Which carts turn | The carts that turn, any one of these: a kind of cart (a chest minecart), an item it carries (coal), a tag of items (all ores), or the fluid in its tank (water), each by its game name. Empty: every cart turns. |
| Gives a signal | A redstone signal while a cart is on it: for any cart, only a full cart, only an empty cart, or stronger the fuller the cart is. Full counts its chest, its tank and its battery together. Choose one of: Never, For any cart, For a full cart, For an empty cart, By how full. |
| Which carts count | Only these carts give the signal, any one of them: a kind of cart, an item or a tag it carries, or the fluid in its tank. Empty: every cart. |
| Picture of its ends | The picture on its two ends, as a log shows its rings; its sides wear the block's own picture. With none, the ends wear that too. |
| Picture of the top half | The door's upper half; its lower half and the item in the hand wear the block's own picture. With none, both halves wear that. |
| Works like | Wood: a door or trapdoor opens by hand, a button stays pressed longer and an arrow presses it, a pressure plate feels anything on it, a fence joins the game's wooden fences. Metal or stone: only redstone opens a door or trapdoor, and only a player or a mob presses a plate. Choose one of: Wood, Metal or stone. |
| Turns | Whether it turns to face whoever places it, as a furnace does, or any way at all, up and down too, as a dispenser does. A picture for its front shows which way it faces. Choose one of: Never, To face whoever places it, Any way, up and down too. |
| Picture of its front | The face that looks at whoever placed it, as a furnace's front; every other face wears the block's own picture. |
| See through | Solid hides what is behind it. Holes shows through the see-through pixels of its picture, as leaves and bars do. Tinted glass mixes what is behind with the colour of each half-see-through pixel, as stained glass does. Choose one of: Solid, Holes, Tinted glass. |
| Holds water | Water can stand in it, as in a slab or a lantern: placed in water it keeps the water, and a bucket fills it. |
| Box from, across | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| Box from, up | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| Box from, back | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| Box to, across | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| Box to, up | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| Box to, back | The box it takes, in sixteenths of a block, from 0 to 16 on each side: what a player bumps into, what the cursor outlines and, with its own picture, what is drawn. 0 0 0 to 16 16 16 is a whole block; 0 0 0 to 16 8 16 is its lower half. A block that turns turns its box too. From 0 to 16 pixels. |
| States of its own | What the block can be besides itself, as a lamp is lit or not and a crop is at a stage: each a switch that is on or off, or a number from 0 up to its most. Placed, each is off or 0; a rule turns it with Turn the ... of the block, and finds it with Find the ... of the block, by its name. Each row has: Name, Holds, Up to. |
| Looks by state | How it looks and how much light it gives while a state is set so: the first that fits wins, and with none it looks as itself. Each row has: While, Is, Picture, Light. |
| Its own numbers | Numbers each placed block keeps, such as its heat. Rules set them; moving parts follow them. Each row has: Name, Most. |
| Animations | The animations it plays, chosen by what it is doing. |
| Selection outline | One frame (default): a single box round everything the block draws, as machines in other mods are outlined, never a box for each part. Detailed shape: each part of the model, the moving ones as the box they sweep. None: no outline. A block whose model draws nothing has no outline unless set otherwise. Choose one of: One frame round everything it draws, Detailed shape (each part), None. |
| Shape (hit and bump) | What the cursor outlines and what a player bumps into. From the model uses the boxes of the block's model (or the game's shape). Full block makes it the whole block. Your own boxes lets you list boxes, in sixteenths of a block. Choose one of: From the model, Full block, My own boxes. |
| Boxes | Each box goes from one corner to the other, in sixteenths of a block (0 to 16). The shape is all the boxes together. Each row has: From, across, From, up, From, back, To, across, To, up, To, back. |
| No collision | Players, mobs and arrows pass through it, but the cursor can still point at its shape. |
| Walk through it | Nothing bumps into it: players, mobs and arrows pass through, as through tall grass or a cobweb. |
| Falls | With nothing under it, it falls, as sand and gravel do, and lands on whatever stops it. |
| Stands up to explosions | Higher holds out better. Stone is 6, obsidian is 1200; a creeper's explosion breaks what is under about 4 near it. From 0 to 3600000. |
| Best broken with | The tool that breaks it fast, as a pickaxe breaks stone. Any tool: every tool breaks it at the speed of a hand. Choose one of: Any tool, A pickaxe, An axe, A shovel, A hoe. |
| At least | How good that tool has to be, as iron ore needs a stone pickaxe and diamond ore an iron one. Choose one of: Any, Stone, Iron, Diamond. |
| Drops only with that tool | Broken with anything else it gives nothing, as stone gives nothing to a hand. |
| Slippery | How much it keeps things sliding: 0.6 is most blocks, 0.8 slime, 0.98 ice, 0.989 blue ice. From 0.1 to 1.1. |
| Walking speed on it | 1 is normal; soul sand is 0.4, honey 0.4; above 1 it hurries whoever walks on it. From 0.1 to 3 times. |
| Jump on it | 1 is normal; honey is 0.5; above 1 it sends whoever jumps from it higher. From 0.1 to 3 times. |
| When a piston pushes it | What a piston does to it: moves it as stone, breaks it as a torch or pumpkin, cannot move it as obsidian, or pushes it but never pulls it back as glazed terracotta. Choose one of: It moves, It breaks and drops, It stays put, Pushed, never pulled. |
| Catches fire | How readily fire nearby sets it alight, from 0 (never) to 300: planks are 5, wool and leaves 30, hay 60. From 0 to 300. |
| Burns away | How fast it burns away once alight, from 0 (never) to 300: planks are 20, wool and leaves 60, hay 20. From 0 to 300. |
| Lava sets it alight | Lava beside it can start a fire on it, as on wood. |
| Gives way to a placed block | A block placed where it stands takes its place, as over tall grass or snow. |
| A dispenser places it | A dispenser facing an empty space puts this block down there, as it does with a shulker box. Off, the dispenser shoots it out as an item. |
| Keeps contents when broken | Broken, it drops as one item that still holds everything that was inside, with its settings. Put it down again and it is just as it was. |
| A wrench turns it | Use a wrench on it and it turns to the next way round. Any item in the wrench tag is a wrench, from this mod or another. |
| Wrench picks it up | Sneak and use a wrench on it and it comes off as an item that keeps everything inside it. No loot roll. |
| Wrench tag | The item tag that counts as a wrench for this block. Leave it as it is to work with the wrenches of other mods. |
| Muffles vibrations | A sculk sensor does not hear what happens on it and no vibration passes through it, as with wool. |
| Cannot be broken | Nothing breaks it, not by hand and not with a blast, as with bedrock. How hard it is no longer matters. |
| Glows in the dark | Its picture stays bright even in a dark cave. This only changes how it looks, it gives off no light. |
| Name colour | The colour of its name when you hold it: common is white, rare is blue, epic is purple. Choose one of: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic. |
| Chooses light blocked | Off, the game decides: a full block stops all light, glass stops none. On, you choose the number. |
| Light it blocks | From 0 (all light passes) to 15 (none passes). Light loses this much going through the block. From 0 to 15. |
| Experience dropped (least) | The fewest experience points it drops when it is mined. Leave both at 0 for none. From 0 to 1000. |
| Experience dropped (most) | The most experience points it drops when it is mined. It picks a number between the least and this. A tool with Silk Touch gets none. From 0 to 1000. |
| Pick-block item | What you get when you point at it and press the pick-block key (middle click). Leave it empty to get the block itself. |
| Runs every tick | A piece of your own code that the game runs twenty times a second for every one of these blocks placed in a world, for what the settings here cannot say: dig a block every few ticks, form a pattern, keep a count. Leave it empty and the block runs nothing. |
| Drawn every frame by | A piece of your own code that draws on this block every frame it is seen, after the moving parts of its shape, for anything the shape cannot say. Leave it empty and the shape is all that is drawn. |
| Joins look with neighbours | With edges, a face hides its border next to a block that joins it, so a wall of glass or framed stone reads as one big pane. You give one picture; the game does the rest. Choose one of: Off, Hide edges. |
| Border width | How many pixels of the picture's edge are the border that gets hidden, from 1 to 4. From 1 to 4 pixels. |
| Joins with | Other blocks it joins its look with, besides blocks like itself. A block of the game, one of yours, or a #tag. Each row has: Block. |
| Random looks | More pictures for the same block. Each placed block picks one by where it stands, so a floor of it does not repeat. A bigger weight is picked more often. Each row has: Picture, Weight. |
| Turns randomly | Each placed block is also turned a quarter, half or three quarters round by where it stands. Not used when the block joins its look with neighbours. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

These point at it: [Recipe](editor-recipe.md), [Drop](editor-drop.md), [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md), [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md), [Ritual](editor-ritual.md), [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md), [Villager job](editor-villagerProfession.md), [Feature](editor-feature.md), [Caves](editor-carver.md), [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Structure](editor-structure.md), [Dimension](editor-dimension.md), [Creative tab](editor-creativeTab.md), [Game thing changed](editor-gameChange.md), [Gene](editor-gene.md), [Species](editor-species.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-boat

# Boat editor

A boat or a raft a player rows on water, with a chest or not.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Boat

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The boat's name, as its item and the game say it. |
| Game name | The boat's name in the game, as a command names it; its chest kind adds chest. |
| Shape | A boat as the game's woods have, or a flat raft as bamboo's. Choose one of: Boat, Raft. |
| Picture | The boat's wood, laid out as the game's own boat pictures are. |
| Item picture | The boat's item, held and in the inventory. |
| With a chest too | Whether it also comes with a chest in it, a boat and item of their own. |
| Chest picture | The boat with its chest, laid out as the game's chest boats are. |
| Chest item picture | The item of the boat with a chest. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# Caves editor

Caves, ravines or Nether tunnels the world cuts into its ground. Give them to your biomes.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Caves

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. The game never shows it. |
| Game name | The cave's name in the game, as a biome finds it. |
| Shape | Round tunnels, one long deep crack, or tunnels like the Nether's. Choose one of: Tunnels, A long crack, Nether tunnels. |
| How often | The chance, in each part of the world, that this cave starts there. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| How wide | How wide it is, as a multiple of the game's own. 1 is the usual width. From 0.2 to 5. |
| How tall | How tall it is, as a multiple of the game's own. 1 is the usual height. From 0.2 to 5. |
| From height | The lowest height it starts at. Sea level is 63. From -64 to 320 blocks. |
| To height | The highest height it starts at. From -64 to 320 blocks. |
| Lava below | Under this height the empty space is filled with lava instead of air. From -64 to 320 blocks. |
| Also cuts through | Blocks it can cut besides what the game's caves cut (stone, dirt, sand and the like). |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

| How trusted they must be | As the game counts it: 1 may pass spawn protection, 2 may use cheats and command blocks, 3 may kick and ban, 4 may stop the server. The server console is 4. From 1 to 4. |
| Short name is fine | Turn on to stop the warning that another mod may use the same first word. Players can always type /<your mod's game name> <command> instead. |
| May be run from the console | Typed in the server's own window, where nobody ran it: lines that need the player who ran it are left out then, and say so. |
| Typed after it | What a player types after the command, in order, each with a name the game shows and suggests it by. A rule of the command uses each by its name. Each row has: Called, Which is, Its choices. |

# Condition editor

A test in plain words, like half of the time, only in a biome, only at night. A loot row or an advancement can say Only when and name it.

| Passes | What the game checks. Pick none to only join other conditions. Choose one of: Some of the time, Only in a biome, Only with a tool, Only at night, Only when sneaking, Only the joined ones. |
| Chance | How often it passes, out of a hundred. 50 is half of the time. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Biome | The biome it must be in. |
| Tool | The item held in the hand. Start with # for a group of items. |
| Joined ones must pass | All of them, any one of them, or none of them. It joins this condition's own test and the ones below. Choose one of: All of them, Any of them, None of them. |
| Tests | The tests this condition asks, beside its first one and the conditions joined to it. The tests are written in the game's own words. |
| Joined conditions | Other conditions of yours to join with this one. Do not join a condition to itself. |

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-matter

# Custom kind editor

A matter of your own beside energy and fluid: a chemical, mana, heat, whatever your mod calls it. Blocks hold it in tanks, pipes and channels carry it, rules move it and moving parts show it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Custom kind
- New thing > Machines and networks > Chemicals

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players call it, as it is shown. |
| Key | The name blocks keep it under, as the game keeps it with your mod's game name in front. |
| Counted in | The word for one of it, shown after its amount: mana, units, degrees. |
| Colour | The colour it is drawn in where it shows. |
| Types | The types of it, each with a name and a colour: oxygen and hydrogen of a gas, fire and water of a magic essence. A tank of it takes any one type at a time, unless it names one. Each row has: Name, Key, Colour, Made of. |
| Held by things | How much of each type things hold: an item, a block or a mob by its name or by a tag. A thing's own line wins over its tags' lines; a 0 takes a type away. Each row has: Thing, Type, Amount. |
| Kept by another mod | The name of another mod made here whose kind this is, the same game name and types. Your pipes then fill and empty that mod's blocks of it, and its pipes yours. |
| Kept by its handler | Use another mod's real tanks and machines for this kind. Write the name that mod gives its handler, with the mod's name in front, or pick the ready-made entry. Leave it empty to not use one. Nothing is built against that mod: when it is not installed, nothing happens. |
| Handler type | The full Java type of that handler, as the mod's page or code shows it. Needed to find it by name; the mod's page or code shows it. |
| Call that puts in | The name of the handler's call that puts stock in. The ready-made entry shows one. It is given the thing, how much, and whether to only try. |
| Putting in answers with | What that call gives back: how much went in (accepted), or how much did not fit (left over). Choose one of: How much went in, How much did not fit. |
| Call that takes out | The name of the handler's call that takes stock out. The ready-made entry shows one. It must give back how much came out. |
| Call that reads | Optional. The name of a call that tells how full the handler is: a number from 0 to 1, or any amount for something in it. Empty counts it as full. |
| Where their things are | Only when the calls want the other mod's own stack of a thing. The class and field of the list to find it in, written class#FIELD, as the Mekanism entry shows. A type key without a mod name gets the handler's mod name. |
| Theirs to one of ours | How many of their units make one of yours. 1 means one for one. From 1 to 1000000. |
| On the tooltip | When an item's tooltip lists what it holds of these types. Choose one of: Never, Always, While the player crouches, While holding or wearing an item. |
| Item that shows it | The item in either hand or on the head that lets a player see what things hold, like goggles. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md), [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-damageChange

# Damage change editor

A hurt a living thing takes, changed or cancelled by who takes it, who deals it and what it is, on every game version, without code of yours inside the game's own.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Damage change

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it in the project. |
| Taken by | What is hurt: choose a mob, or a group of them such as skeletons. Empty means any living thing. |
| Dealt by | What deals the hurt: choose a mob (a skeleton for its arrow), or a group of them. Empty means anything or nothing. |
| Damage type | What the hurt is, such as falling or fire, chosen from the list. Empty means any. |
| Change | What happens to the hurt. Changes run in the order of their elements; a hurt brought to 0 or less is not dealt. Choose one of: Multiply it, Add to it, Set it, Cancel it, Your class decides. |
| Amount | What it is multiplied by, added to it or set to, in health points (a heart is two). From -1000 to 1000. |
| Change class | Your class's full name. It implements the mod's Damages.Change: handed what is hurt, the damage source and the amount, it answers the amount dealt. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-damageType

# Damage type editor

A way of getting hurt, with its own message.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Damage type

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players read the death messages, not this. |
| Game name | The damage type's name in the game, as a command, a data pack or another mod names it. |
| Death message | What the chat says when it kills a player on its own. (player) is the player's name. |
| Killed by someone | What the chat says when someone dealt it. (attacker) is who dealt it. |
| Killed with an item | What the chat says when the one who dealt it held an item with a name of its own. (item) is that name. |
| Harder on hard | Whether it hurts more on Hard and less on Easy, as a zombie's bite does. Choose one of: Never, When a mob deals it, Always. |
| Hunger it costs | How much hunger a hit takes from a player, as swimming or sprinting does. Most hits take 0.1. From 0 to 10. |
| How it sounds | The game's own hurt sound the victim makes: an ordinary hurt, thorns, drowning, burning, a sweet berry's poke or freezing. Choose one of: Hurt, Thorns, Drowning, Burning, Poking, Freezing. |
| Also plays | Any sound, one of the game's or of your own, played where it lands when a rule deals it. |
| Goes through armour | Armour does not soften it, as starving and falling into the void are not. |
| Goes past a shield | A raised shield does not stop it. |
| Goes past Protection | Protection and the other enchantments that soften a hit do not soften this one. |
| Goes past Resistance | The Resistance effect does not soften it. |
| Is fire | Fire Resistance stops it and Fire Protection softens it, and a thing immune to fire is immune to it. |
| Is a projectile | Projectile Protection softens it, as it softens an arrow. |
| Is an explosion | Blast Protection softens it, as it softens a creeper. |
| Is freezing | What cannot freeze, a snow golem or a stray, takes none of it. |
| Is lightning | It turns a pig to a zombified piglin and a villager to a witch, as lightning does. |
| Is drowning | What breathes water takes none of it. |
| Is a fall | Feather Falling softens it, and what never takes a fall takes none of it. |
| No knockback | The victim is not pushed back when it lands. |
| Angers no one | A mob hurt by it does not turn on whoever dealt it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Sound](editor-sound.md).

These point at it: [Mob](editor-creature.md).

![Damage type editor](/media/docs/editor-damageType.webp)

- [Glossary](glossary.md)
