# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-dimension

# Dimension editor

A whole other world reached through a portal.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Dimension

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| Game name | The dimension's name in the game, as a command goes there: /execute in. |
| Its land | What its ground is like. Choose one of: Hills and valleys, as the overworld's, Shaped land, each biome its own, Islands floating in the sky, Caves under a ceiling of rock, Flat, in layers, Empty, nothing at all. |
| Biomes | The biomes it is made of, yours and the game's, each taking a share of its land. |
| Rock | The block its hills are made of, under each biome's own ground. |
| Sea | What fills its low places. Choose one of: Water, Lava, Nothing. |
| Sea level | How high its sea comes. From -64 to 256. |
| Land height | The height its land stands at; each biome stands above or below it by its own land height. From -32 to 256 blocks. |
| Hilliness | How hilly the whole dimension is; each biome's roughness is a share of it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Biome size | About how wide each biome's land is, in blocks. From 64 to 2048 blocks. |
| Caves | The caves cut into its ground: none, winding tunnels, or tunnels and great caverns as the overworld's. Choose one of: None, Tunnels, Tunnels and caverns. |
| Water underground | Pockets of water and lava underground at their own levels, as the overworld's; off, every cave below the sea is flooded. |
| Great ore veins | The overworld's large veins of copper and iron winding deep underground. |
| Layers | Its ground from the bottom up, each layer a block and how thick it is. Each row has: Block, Thick. |
| Time | Whether day turns to night there. Choose one of: Day and night, as the overworld, Always day, Always night. |
| Sky | What is over it. The colours of its sky and fog are its biomes'. Choose one of: A sky with the sun and the moon, No sky, a thick haze, A dark sky, as the end's. |
| Clouds | Whether clouds drift over it, under a sky with the sun and the moon. |
| Cloud height | How high its clouds drift. Before Minecraft 1.21.11 the game keeps them at its own height. From -64 to 320 blocks. |
| Light in the dark | How bright its darkest places are: none is as the overworld at night. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Sunlight | Whether light comes down from its sky. |
| Beds work | Whether a player may sleep there. Off, a bed explodes as in the nether. |
| Distance | How far one step there carries a player elsewhere: eight is the nether's. From 0.00001 to 30000000. |
| Portal | A way in, as the nether's: a frame of a block, lit by an item. Its inside becomes a portal; standing in it takes a player there and back. |
| Frame | The block its frame is built of, two to twenty one wide and three to twenty one high inside. |
| Lit by | The item a player uses on the frame to open it. |
| Portal colour | The colour of the swirl inside the frame. |
| Settings of a made one | Numbers each dimension made from this one keeps: each starts at random between its least and its most (the same for a fixed one), and a rule may set it. Each row has: Setting, Least, Most. |
| Ore of a made one | A block scattered in veins through each made dimension's ground. None picked means none. |
| Ore veins a chunk | How many veins of the ore each chunk gets; a formula may read a setting, as ores. From 0 to 64. |
| Ore from height | The lowest the veins are. From -64 to 320. |
| Ore to height | The highest the veins are. From -64 to 320. |
| Gravity | How hard everything falls in it: 100 is the game's own, 50 half, as on a moon. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Monsters' strength | Monsters in it have this much of their health and their hit: 200 is twice. From 1 to 10000 percent. |
| Hurt in the dark | Hurt a second a player takes in the dark in it; 0 for none. From 0 to 1000. |
| Dark at light | The light this low or lower counts as dark: 0 is pitch black, 15 full day. From 0 to 15. |
| Air | How much air there is: 100 is the game's own; below it a player's breath runs out and they drown. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Gives air when worn | Who wears this breathes as at home: a space helmet, a mask. |
| Gives air from | The fluid the worn item holds and breathes from. Empty: it gives air for ever. |
| Uses a second | How many millibuckets of that fluid the worn item uses each second in this dimension. When it runs out the air goes. From 0 to 100000 millibuckets. |
| Start island | Where the first one arrives in the empty, a small island is made for them. |
| Island top | The block on top of the island. |
| Island size | How far the island reaches from its middle. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Island height | How high the top of the island stands. 0: as before, the arrival height (64 in the overworld). Any other number is the height you choose. From -2032 to 2031 blocks. |
| Island at | Where the island is built: where the world begins (spawn), or at a place you choose. Choose one of: Where the world begins, At a place I choose. |
| Island east-west place | The x place of the island's middle. From -30000000 to 30000000. |
| Island north-south place | The z place of the island's middle. From -30000000 to 30000000. |
| Holds pocket rooms | Walled rooms, one for each name (a player, a placed block, an item), far apart in it. |
| Room walls | The block a room's six walls are made of. |
| Room's middle block | A block put in the middle of a new room's floor, as a way out. None picked means none. |
| Rooms apart | How far apart rooms are, middle to middle. From 80 to 4096 blocks. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Block](editor-block.md).

These point at it: [World type](editor-worldType.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-drop

# Drop editor

What falls out when a block breaks or a mob dies.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Drop

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The file name inside the mod. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. |
| From | The block broken or the mob killed that gives it. |
| Or the game's | Blocks and mobs of the game or another mod that drop it too, each one or a tag of them; another mod's is typed. What they drop already stays. |
| Gives | One item, or a roll of a loot table: a crate, or a handful of anything. Choose one of: An item, A loot table. |
| Drops | What it gives. Pick one of your things or one of the game's. |
| At least | The fewest that can drop. From 0 to 64. |
| At most | The most that can drop. From 1 to 64. |
| Loot table | The loot table rolled when it drops. |
| Chance | How often it drops, out of a hundred. From 0.1 to 100 percent. |
| Only when broken with | What the block must be broken with for this to drop: shears, as grass and leaves give themselves; a Silk Touch tool, as glass does; or anything but Silk Touch, so Silk Touch takes the block itself instead. Choose one of: Anything, Shears, A Silk Touch tool, Anything but Silk Touch. |
| More with Fortune or Looting | A block broken with a Fortune pickaxe drops more, the way ores do; a creature killed with a Looting sword drops more, the way the game's mobs do. |
| Every mob of a kind | Every monster, every animal, or every mob of the water, the game's and other mods' alike. Choose one of: None, Monsters, Animals, Water mobs, Any mob. |
| Never from | Mobs it never drops from, each one or a tag of them, such as the wither or the raiders. |

# Enchantment editor

A power added to a tool or weapon.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Enchantment

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The enchantment's name, as its tooltip line shows it. |
| Game name | The enchantment's name in the game, as /enchant and a data pack name it. |
| Goes on | What an anvil puts it on: the game's own groups of tools, weapons and armour, which a mod's own join when they are of the same sort. Choose one of: Swords, Swords and axes, Weapons, Mining tools, Mining tools, for loot, Armour, Helmets, Chestplates, Leggings, Boots, Bows, Crossbows, Tridents, Maces, Fishing rods, Anything that wears out, Anything worn, Anything at all. |
| Offered on | What the enchanting table offers it for; an anvil still puts it on everything it goes on. Choose one of: What it goes on, Swords, Swords and axes, Weapons, Mining tools, Mining tools, for loot, Armour, Helmets, Chestplates, Leggings, Boots, Bows, Crossbows, Tridents, Maces, Fishing rods, Anything that wears out, Anything worn, Anything at all. |
| Highest level | The strongest it comes: Sharpness goes to V, Knockback to II. From 1 to 255. |
| How common | How often the table and loot pick it against the others: Sharpness and Protection are 10, Fire Aspect 2, Mending and Thorns 1. From 1 to 1024. |
| What it does | Each a thing the game does for it with no code, stronger each level. Each row has: Does, At level I, Each level more, Changes, Effect, For. |
| Works when | Where the enchanted thing must be for it to work. Choose one of: Held in the main hand, Held in the off hand, Held in either hand, Worn on the head, Worn on the chest, Worn on the legs, Worn on the feet, Worn anywhere, Anywhere. |
| Not with | The game's own set it cannot share a thing with, as Sharpness cannot share one with Smite. Choose one of: Goes with any, Sharpness, Smite, Bane, The Protections, Frost Walker, Depth Strider, Infinity, Mending, Multishot, Piercing, Fortune, Silk Touch, Riptide's others. |
| From | The enchanting table's levels it is offered at: from the first number, a second number more each level, over a span of the third. From 0 to 255. |
| Each level | The enchanting table's levels it is offered at: from the first number, a second number more each level, over a span of the third. From 0 to 255. |
| Span | The enchanting table's levels it is offered at: from the first number, a second number more each level, over a span of the third. From 0 to 255. |
| Anvil cost | Levels an anvil asks to put it on from a book, each level of it: Sharpness 1, Fire Aspect 4. From 0 to 255. |
| At the table | The enchanting table can offer it. |
| Sold by librarians | A librarian may sell a book of it. |
| In loot | Chests and fishing may give it on an enchanted thing. |
| On mobs' gear | A mob's own gear, and what villagers sell, may come with it. |
| Treasure | Rare, as Mending is: never at the table, and a librarian asks twice as much for it. |
| Curse | A curse, as Binding is: its line is red and a grindstone cannot take it away. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-feature

# Feature editor

Something the world grows as it is made: a patch of flowers, a tree, a boulder, a lake, a vein of a block.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Feature

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. The game never shows it. |
| Game name | The feature's name in the game, as a command places it: /place feature. |
| Shape | What the world makes each time it places one. Choose one of: A patch of plants, A tree, A boulder, A lake, A vein under the ground, A round patch in the ground, A spring in a cave wall, A geode, A huge mushroom, A pile, A column, An iceberg, Basalt columns, A patch of ground, A fossil, A dripstone cluster, A desert well, A delta, Blobs in the ground, Kelp, Seagrass, Sea pickles, Bamboo, A mix of your features, A growth on cave walls, Nether plants, Nether vines, A huge fungus, A sculk patch, Magma under the sea, A dungeon, Vines, Glowstone, A basalt pillar, Blue ice, Coral, A chorus plant, An island in the End, One block, A replaced block, A filled layer, Frozen water and snow, An ice spike, An End spike, An End gateway, A great dripstone, A pointed dripstone, A tree with roots, Scattered ore, A ground patch under water, One of two features, A bonus chest, A patch of flowers (the game's flower type), A patch of bushes or plants (the game's random patch), One of several features, evenly, The End's obsidian platform, A starting platform in the void, Deposits from a list. |
| Plants | What the patch is made of. Each is as likely as its weight: two poppies for every dandelion. Each row has: Plant, Weight. |
| Plants a patch | How many times it tries to plant one in a patch. Some land where nothing grows. From 1 to 128. |
| Spread | How far from the middle of the patch a plant may land. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Trunk | The block the trunk is made of: a log of the game's or a block of yours. |
| Leaves | The block the leaves are made of. |
| Tree shape | How its leaves sit on the trunk, as the game's own trees. Choose one of: Round, as an oak, Pointed, as a spruce, Tall with branches, as a big oak, A low bush. |
| Trunk height | How tall the trunk grows, before a few blocks more by chance. From 1 to 32 blocks. |
| Made of | The block it is made of. |
| Found in | The ground the vein replaces. Choose one of: Stone, Deepslate, Netherrack, End stone. |
| Vein size | About how many blocks a vein holds. From 1 to 64. |
| Lowest | The lowest and highest height a vein is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| Highest | The lowest and highest height a vein is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| How many per chunk | How many veins it tries to place in each chunk. From 1 to 64. |
| Filled with | What the lake holds, or what the spring pours. Choose one of: Water, Lava. |
| Rim | The block around the lake where it meets the ground. |
| Across | How far the patch reaches from its middle. From 1 to 8 blocks. |
| Outer shell | The block of its outside, as the game's smooth basalt. |
| Middle shell | The block between, as the game's calcite. |
| Inside | The block that lines its hollow, as the game's amethyst. |
| Crystals | What grows on the inside. Left empty, nothing does. |
| Scattered | Whether its ores lie apart, one here and one there, as ancient debris does. |
| Only buried | Whether ores that would touch air are left out, as diamonds are. |
| Cap shape | The red mushroom's dome or the brown one's flat cap. Choose one of: Dome, Flat. |
| Cap | The block its cap is made of. |
| Stem | The block its stem is made of. |
| Cap width | How far the cap reaches from the stem. From 1 to 6 blocks. |
| Made of | The block the pile is made of, as hay bales in a village. |
| Made of | The block stacked up into a column, as sugar cane grows. |
| Up to | How tall it is, at most. From 1 to 32 blocks. |
| Made of | The block the iceberg is made of. It floats at the sea's level in an ocean. |
| Spread | How far its columns spread, as the Nether's basalt deltas. From 0 to 3 blocks. |
| Up to | How tall its columns of basalt rise at most. From 1 to 10 blocks. |
| Ground | The block laid over the ground, as moss in a lush cave. |
| Grows on it | The plant on most of the ground. Left empty, the ground is bare. |
| Across | How far the ground reaches from its middle. From 1 to 12 blocks. |
| Tree | One of your tree features. The roots grow round it and under it. |
| Roots | The block the roots are made of, as rooted dirt under an azalea. |
| Either | One of your features. It is placed half the time. |
| Or | Another of your features, placed the other half. A feature here grows only through this one, not on its own. |
| Bones | Which of the game's own fossils it leaves underground. Choose one of: Spines, Skulls, Spines and skulls. |
| Across | How far its stalactites and stalagmites reach in a cave. From 2 to 8 blocks. |
| Rim | The block around each pool, as magma round the Nether's lava deltas. |
| Across | How far its pools spread at most. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| In | The block the blobs replace where they find it. |
| Made of | The block each blob is made of, as blackstone in netherrack. |
| Across | How far a blob reaches from its middle. From 1 to 12 blocks. |
| Tall | How much of it grows two blocks tall. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| How many | How many sea pickles it tries to place. From 1 to 64. |
| On podzol | How often the ground under it turns to podzol, as in a bamboo jungle. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Picks one of | Your other features, one of them at each place, each as likely as its weight, as a forest mixes its trees. A feature here grows only through the mix, not on its own. Each row has: Feature, Weight. |
| Growth | What grows over the stone of caves. Choose one of: Glow lichen, on walls and ceilings, Sculk veins, on every side. |
| Reach | How far from where it starts it looks for stone to cover. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Plants | What spreads over the ground, each as likely as its weight. It grows only on nylium, as in a crimson forest. Each row has: Plant, Weight. |
| Grows | Which way the vines grow, as the Nether's own. Choose one of: Up from the ground, twisting, Down from the ceiling, weeping. |
| Grows on | The ground it grows from, as crimson nylium. |
| Stem | The block its stem is made of, as a crimson stem. |
| Cap | The block its cap is made of, as nether wart. |
| Lights | The block dotted through its cap, as shroomlight. Left empty, the cap is whole. |
| Spread | How far the sculk spreads from its middle. From 1 to 32. |
| With a catalyst | How often a sculk catalyst stands in the middle of it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Coral shape | Which of the warm ocean's corals grows, of the game's coral colours. Choose one of: A tree of branches, A claw, A mushroom. |
| List | The list of entries the player edits that says each deposit: its block, size, how rare and how deep. |
| Block field | The list's field that holds each deposit's block. |
| Size field | The list's field that holds each deposit's size, in blocks. |
| Rarity field | The list's field that holds how rare each deposit is: one chunk in this many. Missing, it is every chunk. |
| Lowest field | The list's field that holds the lowest height a deposit lies at. |
| Highest field | The list's field that holds the highest height a deposit lies at. |
| How often | How many the world places in each chunk, a square of sixteen blocks. Choose one of: Everywhere, eight a chunk, Often, three a chunk, Sometimes, one a chunk, Rarely, one in eight chunks, Very rarely, one in thirty two chunks, In clumps, thick in some places and thin in others, Just so many. |
| In each chunk | How many it places in a chunk where it places any. From 1 to 256. |
| Once in | It places any in one chunk of this many; one is every chunk. From 1 to 1000 chunks. |
| Where | At what height it is placed. Choose one of: Where it belongs: on the ground, or under it, On the ground, Between two heights, Most in the middle of two heights, On the top of the world, water too, On the ground, under the sea too, On cave floors, On cave ceilings. |
| Lowest | The lowest height it is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| Highest | The highest height it is placed at. The sea is at sixty three. From -64 to 320. |
| Only on these blocks | It is placed only on top of one of these blocks. Empty means any block. |
| Only in | Keep it to places full of water, or to open air. Choose one of: Anywhere, Only in water, Only in air. |
| Not near the surface | It stays at least this many blocks below the ground. Zero means no limit. From 0 to 128 blocks. |
| Only in its biomes | On, as the game does: it is placed only in the biomes above. Off lets other things that place it decide. |
| In biomes | Where it grows: the game's biomes, a group of them such as every overworld biome, or biomes of yours. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md), [Biome](editor-biome.md).

# Forms for every material editor

Makes a dust, a plate, a gear or any other form for every metal and gem the game has when it starts, other mods too. One grey picture per form is tinted in each material's colour.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Forms for every material

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for this set, only for you. |
| Forms | Each row is one thing made for every material, like a dust or a plate. Each row has: Form, Item name in the game, Tag, Picture. |
| Materials found by | A material is found for every item that fits one of these. A star stands for any text. Each row has: Item name. |
| Also these items | Items to make forms for even when no pattern finds them. Each row has: Item. |
| Skip | Materials or mods to never make forms for. Each row has: Material or mod. |
| Recipes | Recipes made for every material found when the game starts. Write one once with (material) and form names like (ingot), (nugget) or (dust); a recipe is skipped for a material when an item it needs is missing. Each row has: Recipe type, Recipe (JSON), Only if this mod is loaded. |
| Only if not made yet | On: a form is not made when an item with the same name already exists, so you never get two copper dusts. Mods that load after yours are not seen. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-gameChange

# Game thing changed editor

One of the game's own blocks, items or mobs given new values, such as a block's hardness, an item's stack size or a mob's health, a structure the game makes no more, or a limit the game sets, such as the anvil's most cost.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Game thing changed

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What it is called here. |
| Game name | Its name inside the mod, in small letters. |
| Changes | What kind of the game's things this changes: a block, an item, a mob, structures, or limits the game sets. Choose one of: A block, An item, A mob, Structures, Limits. |
| Item | The item to change, the game's, another mod's or yours: how many stack, and how many uses it lasts. |
| Stacks to | How many fit in one stack, up to 99, such as ender pearls 64; 0 keeps the game's. Items that wear out stack to 1. From 0 to 99. |
| Uses | How many uses it lasts before it breaks; 0 keeps the game's. An item given uses stacks to 1. From 0 to 100000. |
| Food it gives | How much hunger it fills when eaten, up to 20. 0 leaves the game's; above 0 makes it food. From 0 to 20. |
| Stays full for | How long the food keeps you from getting hungry again; a bigger number lasts longer. Used only when Food it gives is above 0. From 0 to 20. |
| Can eat when full | On: you can eat it even with a full hunger bar. Used only when Food it gives is above 0. |
| Name colour | The colour of its name when you hold it: common is white, rare is blue, epic is purple. Keep leaves the game's. Choose one of: Keep the game's, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic. |
| Its limits | Each limit of the game to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to; in one dimension or every one; or taken from a setting the player changes. Each row has: Value, How, Number, Only in, Player's setting. |
| Block | The block to change, the game's, another mod's or yours. |
| Its values | Each value of the block to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to. Each row has: Value, How, Number. |
| Mob | The mob to change, the game's, another mod's or yours. Mobs already in a world change as they load. |
| Its values | Each value of the mob to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to. Each row has: Value, How, Number. |
| Never made | Structures the game no longer makes, such as mineshafts; one of yours can take their place. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-gene

# Gene editor

A trait any thing can carry and pass to its young: a number such as Growth, or one of a few choices such as Coat colour.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Gene

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads in a tooltip and in the chat. |
| Saved as | The name the gene is kept under on each thing, and what rules call it. |
| Holds | A number in a range, such as Growth from 1 to 10, or one of a few choices, such as Black, Orange or White. Choose one of: A number, One of a few choices. |
| Lowest | The smallest the number can be. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Highest | The biggest the number can be. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Starts at | What a thing has when its species does not say. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Step | The number moves in steps of this much: 1 for whole numbers, 0 for any. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Choices | Each value the gene can take, which one wins when a thing has two, and how often it is found in the wild. Each row has: Value, Wins, In the wild, Block. |
| A child takes it | How a child gets this gene from its two parents. Choose one of: One copy from each parent, The parents' average, From one parent or the other, The higher of the two, The lower of the two. |
| Of two copies, shows | Which of its two numbers it shows. Choose one of: The higher, The lower, Their average, The first. |
| Chance to change | Out of every hundred children, how many have this gene changed: a number moves by a step, a choice turns into another. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Changes by | How much the number moves when it changes. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Changes | Which way the number moves when it changes. Choose one of: Up, Down, Up or down. |
| Carried once when | Another gene, such as Sex: where it shows the value below, this gene is carried once, the mother's copy, as orange is on a tomcat. |
| Shows | The value of that gene with which this one is carried once, such as Male. |
| Shapes | What this number changes in the thing that carries it: how fast a plant grows, how much a block drops, how tall a tree grows, or a mob's size, speed or health. Choose one of: Nothing, How fast it grows, How much it drops, How tall a tree grows, Its size, Its speed, Its health, How wide its trunk grows, How big its crown grows. |
| Each point above the start | How much more, out of a hundred, each point above the gene's start gives, and less for each point below. At 10, a plant with Growth 5 and a start of 2 grows 30 in a hundred faster. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Decides in a tree | What this choice decides in a tree grown from a sapling that carries it: the fruit it bears, its logs, its leaves, or the shape of its crown (name the choices round, pointed, wide or bush). Choose one of: Nothing, The fruit it bears, Its logs, Its leaves, The shape of its crown. |
| Shown | When the tooltip and the chat say it. Choose one of: Always, Once read by an analyser, Never. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md).

These point at it: [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md), [Species](editor-species.md).

# HUD number bar editor

One number of the player shown over the game as a bar or words, like saturation above the hunger bar.

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |

Choose one of: Saturation, Hunger, Health, Air, Armor, Armor toughness, Absorption hearts, Held item's durability, Level, A value of the player, An area value where the player stands, What the player looks at. |
| Value | The value of the player it draws, against the value's most. |
| Area value | The area value it draws, where the player stands, against the value's most. |
| Placed | Where it is drawn: over the game's own icons on the hunger, health, armor or air bar; a row of its own just above the drumsticks or the hearts (higher while air bubbles or armor show there, and stacked with the others there); beside a bar, outside the hotbar; or at the top. | Icons over the game's row | A row of icons for one of the game's rows (hunger, armour, health, air) is drawn beside it. Turn on to draw the icons over the game's own, as a saturation overlay. |
| Drawn as | A bar that fills, the number itself, ten icons as the game's own bars (two points an icon, half an icon for one), or a bar with its number. Choose one of: A bar, A number, Ten icons, A bar with its number, A veil over the screen, A veil over the sky. |
| Veil strength | How strong the tint is when the number is at its most. From 1 to 100 percent. |

Choose one of: Always, While below a share, While above a share, For a while after it changes, While holding an item, While sneaking, While under water. |
| Share | The share of its most it is compared with: shown while below it, or while above it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| For | How long it stays after the number changes. From 1 to 60 seconds. |
| Holding | The item, or a tag of items, that shows it while held in either hand. |
| Color | The color it is drawn in. |
| Wrap into layers | A value bigger than one row starts again in the next color, as many times as it needs. |
| One row holds | How much of the value fills one row. Ten icons hold 20, two for each icon. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Layer colors | The colors of the second row, the third and on, as color codes with spaces between. After the last one they start again. |
| Layers drawn | Over the first row, or each one above the row before. Choose one of: Over the first row, Each above the last. |
| Hide empty icons | Icons not reached are not drawn, instead of a faint dark square. |
| Recolor the game's own row | The mod draws the game's hearts or armor itself. After one full row, every further row's worth turns the row to the next color, so it never grows taller. Off keeps the game's own rows. |
| Row colors | The colors of the second row's worth, the third and on, as color codes with spaces between. After the last one they start again. |
| Icon | An item, or a picture of your own, drawn small beside it. None when empty. |
| Icon size | How big the icon is drawn, in the GUI's pixels. The usual size is 8. From 4 to 32 pixels. |
| Hidden in creative | Hidden in creative and spectator, where the game hides its own health and hunger. |
| Nudge across | Moves it right (or left, below nought) from its place, in the GUI's pixels. From -400 to 400 pixels. |
| Nudge down | Moves it down (or up, below nought) from its place, in the GUI's pixels. From -400 to 400 pixels. |

| Name | What players read when they hold it, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Texture | The flat picture of the item in hand and in the inventory. A 16 by 16 PNG. A Model, if you give one, is a 3D shape that replaces it. |
| Tooltip lines | Extra lines under its Name when a player points at it, such as "Tastes like thunder.". The Name itself is set above. Each row has: Words, Color. |
| Plays as frames | Whether the item's picture plays as a strip of frames, and how fast. It is set on the picture itself. |
| Shape | A 3D shape for this item to be held as, instead of its flat Texture. Leave it empty and the item is its Texture. |
| Stack size | How many fit in one inventory slot. Tools take 1, most things 64. This is not how long a tool lasts. From 1 to 99. |
| Fire-proof | Dropped, it does not burn in fire or lava, like netherite. |
| Is a wrench | Puts this item in the wrench tag, so it turns and picks up blocks of any mod that listens to that tag. |
| Other looks | Other pictures a rule can swap in for the Texture while it is true, such as charged or empty. The Texture is the one it wears the rest of the time. Each row has: Name, Picture. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

These point at it: [Block](editor-block.md), [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md), [Value](editor-value.md), [Material](editor-material.md), [Drawing in the world](editor-worldDraw.md), [Creative tab](editor-creativeTab.md), [Species](editor-species.md).

# Item change editor

What happens to an item after it is made: its count, its wear, a name, a lore line, a random enchantment. A loot row can say Then change it and name one.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Item change

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. |
| Game name | The change's name in the game, as a data pack or another mod names it. |
| Only when | A condition that must pass for the steps to apply. Make one with New, Condition. |
| Steps | What is done to the item, one step after another. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-lootTable

# Loot table editor

A weighted list of what can come out, rolled by a quest, a crate, a mob's or a block's drop, or a rule. It is written as the game's own, so a chest the game fills can name it too.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Loot table

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The table's name in the game, as a chest, a command or another mod names it. |
| Kind of table | What the table is for. It decides which conditions you can pick: a tool is only held when a block is broken. Choose one of: Chest, Block drops, Creature drops, Fishing, Gift, Digging up. |
| At least | How many times the list is drawn from each time the table is rolled: one number, or a range to pick from. From 0 to 64. |
| At most | How many times the list is drawn from each time the table is rolled: one number, or a range to pick from. From 0 to 64. |
| Give every entry | Every entry comes out on each roll and the weights are set aside: a bundle rather than a draw. |
| Entries | What can come out of one roll, each as likely as its weight against the others. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Drop](editor-drop.md), [Structure](editor-structure.md).

![Loot table editor](/media/docs/editor-lootTable.webp)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-machineRecipe

# Machine recipe editor

What one machine of yours turns into something else, and what it costs.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Machine recipe

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this recipe. Leave it empty and the card names itself from what goes in and what comes out. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this recipe. |
| Machine | The block that runs it. Recipes name their machine, so adding one changes no block. |
| What goes in | The thing the machine takes from the slots it takes from. |
| How many | How many of it one operation uses. From 1 to 64. |
| What comes out | Leave this empty for a generator: it burns what goes in to nothing. |
| How many | How many come out of one operation. From 0 to 64. |
| Second thing in | A second thing that goes in with the first, as two metals make an alloy. Leave it empty for a machine that takes one thing. |
| How many of the second | How many of the second thing one operation uses. From 1 to 64. |
| Energy | Whether the machine spends energy on this or makes it. Choose one of: Uses energy, Makes energy. |
| How much energy | Over the whole operation, not each tick. It is spread evenly across the seconds below. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Energy each tick | Use this much energy every tick instead of the whole amount above. 0 keeps the whole amount. The recipe waits when the machine runs short. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Seconds | How long one operation takes. The game reads it while it runs, so it can come from somewhere else. From 1 to 3600 seconds. |
| Fluid in | A fluid the machine uses up each time, chosen from the list. The machine holds it in its own tank: attach Fluid to it. |
| Fluid used | How much of the fluid each time; 1000 mB is one bucket. From 1 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Fluid each tick | Use this much of the fluid every tick instead of all of it at the end. 0 keeps the whole amount. The recipe waits when the tank runs short. From 0 to 100000 millibuckets. |
| From tank | Which of the machine's tanks: 1 is its own, 2 and on the tanks added to it. From 1 to 5. |
| Uses a thing of your own | Matter is a thing of your own that is not an item or a fluid, like heat or mana. The machine uses this much of it each time, from what it holds: attach Matter to the machine. |
| Type | One type of the kind, by name. Left empty, the kind itself, or any of its types going in. |
| Matter used | How much of the matter each time. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Fluid out | A fluid the machine makes each time, chosen from the list, into its own tank; it waits while there is no room. |
| Fluid made | How much of the fluid each time; 1000 mB is one bucket. From 1 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Into tank | Which of the machine's tanks: 1 is its own, 2 and on the tanks added to it. From 1 to 5. |
| Makes a thing of your own | A matter of your own the machine makes each time, into what it holds; it waits while there is no room. |
| Type | One type of the kind, by name. Left empty, the kind itself, or any of its types going in. |
| Matter made | How much of the matter each time. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Makes a second thing | A second stock the machine makes each time, into a tank that takes it: water into oxygen and hydrogen. |
| Type | One type of the kind, by name. Left empty, the kind itself, or any of its types going in. |
| Matter made | How much of the matter each time. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Sometimes also | A second thing it makes now and then beside the result, as a crusher gives a little gravel with the dust. It goes where the result goes, when there is room. |
| How many of it | How many of the second thing each time it comes. From 1 to 64. |
| Genes the result gets | What the result carries of the genes of what went in: an analyser copies and reads them, a breeder crosses two. Choose one of: None, A copy of the first's, A copy of the first's, read, The first and the second crossed, A copy of the second's, The first's, with the second's written over, One gene of the first's, at random. |
| First must show | A gene value the first thing must show to be taken, such as a species; empty takes any. |
| Of the gene | The gene that value is of; none is its species. |
| Make one for every | Writes this recipe once for everything in the set you pick: dye colours, wood types, stone types, metals, gems, or a list of your own. Where the recipe says (each) (or <colour>, <wood>, <stone>), each one's name goes; one the game lacks is left out. |
| Worked out from the inputs | What the result works out from the things the machine takes in, each by a formula: a value it holds, how many it makes, an effect and its strength, or which thing it is. The formulas see the machine too: energy, fluid and tier. Each row has: Works out, Which, Formula, Seconds. |
| How often | Out of every hundred times, how many give the second thing. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| More in and out | Any number of things more that go in or come out, beside the ones above: items, fluids or stocks of your own, each with how much and, coming out, how often. Each row has: Goes, What, Item, Fluid, Stock, Type, How much, How often, Tank. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |
| Only while a number > 0 | For advanced rules: a number worked out where the recipe is made. The recipe works only while the number is above 0. Make it a formula to use any piece of the rules. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Custom kind](editor-matter.md), [Gene](editor-gene.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md).

## Picture

![Machine recipe editor](/media/docs/editor-machineRecipe.webp)

## Related pages

- [Machine recipe](thing-machineRecipe.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-material

# Material editor

What parts are cut from, any item the game's iron ingot among them: its color, and the numbers and abilities it gives a part.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Material

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads on a part cut from it. |
| Saved as | The name it is saved as in a part's data, which a piece of your own code reads. |
| Cut from | The item a player puts in the stonecutter to cut parts of this material, or a tag of them. |
| Color | The color a part cut from it wears, and the tool's part with it. |
| Uses | What a head of it lasts, as the game's pickaxe of it does: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mining speed | How fast a head of it mines: iron 6, gold 12. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Damage | What a head of it adds to a hit: iron 2, diamond 3. From 0 to 1000. |
| Strong as | Which blocks give it their drops: an iron one gets diamonds from their ore, a stone one does not. Choose one of: Wood, Gold (as wood), Stone, Iron, Diamond, Netherite. |
| As a handle | What a handle of it multiplies the tool's uses and mining speed by: 100 leaves them as they are. From 10 to 1000 percent. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Sets alight | Seconds a hit of a tool with a part of it sets what it hits on fire. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Mends itself | A tool with a part of it gains back a use every five seconds. |
| Own stats | Stats of your own beside uses, speed and damage, such as Luck or Heat: a part gives its share of them to the tool, and a rule reads the tool's. Each row has: Stat, Amount. |
| Traits | Modifiers every tool with a part of this material carries, as if installed: their stat changes and their own rules. Two parts of it give the trait twice the level. Each row has: Modifier, Level a part. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Effect](editor-effect.md), [Item](editor-item.md).

![Material editor](/media/docs/editor-material.webp)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-creature

# Mob editor

A living thing with a model, animations and behavior.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Mob
- New thing > Mobs and models > Pet
- New thing > Mobs and models > Mount
- New thing > Mobs and models > Flying mount
- New thing > Mobs and models > Sea mount
- New thing > Mobs and models > Boss

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players read above it and on its spawn egg, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. /summon uses it. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Body | The model it wears: one made for a mob, with its feet on the ground and its front facing away from you. |
| Health | How much damage it takes to kill it. A player has 20, which is ten hearts. |
| Temperament | Passive runs when hurt. Neutral fights back when hurt. Hostile goes after the nearest player. Choose one of: Passive, Neutral, Hostile. |
| Gets about by | How it gets about: walking, climbing walls, flying, fluttering with no aim, swooping (circling and diving), swimming, swimming and leaping out, or set in a wall face. Choose one of: Walking, Climbing, Flying, Fluttering, Swooping, Swimming, Swimming and leaping, Set in a wall, Walking and flying. |
| Circles at | How high it circles over where it is, or over what it fights, before it dives. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Circle size | How wide the circle it flies round is, in blocks from its middle. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Leaps every | How often it jumps out of the water ahead of it, when swimming near the top. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Takes off above | It walks, and lifts off when what it hunts is this many blocks above it, or when it falls. A rule can also make it take off. From 0.5 to 64 blocks. |
| Lands within | It flies down and lands when what it hunts stands on the ground this close. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Lands after | How long it stays up with nothing to hunt before it comes down. 0 means it stays up until a rule lands it. From 0 to 600 seconds. |
| Sunk into the wall | How deep its back sits in the block of the nearest wall face it holds to. From 0 to 4 blocks. |
| Settles on | The blocks it now and then lands on and rests a while: flowers for a butterfly. Empty: it never settles. |
| Rests for | How long it sits on a block before it flutters off again. A player coming near startles it sooner. From 0 to 600 seconds. |
| Size | How big it is drawn and how big it stands, its hitbox with it: 1 is the size of its body, 0.5 half, 2 twice. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Its own picture | A picture in place of the one its body wears, laid out the same way: a variant wears the same body in other colours. |
| Other looks | Other pictures it can wear, laid out as its own is. A rule puts one on (Make it wear the look ...), and it keeps it when the world is saved. Each row has: Called, Picture. |
| Its own numbers | Numbers each mob keeps, such as its anger. Rules set and read them like any value. Each row has: Name, Most. |
| Width | How wide it is to hit and to collide with, in blocks. |
| Height | How tall it is to hit and to collide with, in blocks. |
| Made from the game's | The game's own thing this one behaves like; its behaviour stays the game's. A creature from the game, such as a zombie or a cow, written with its game name. Empty: a creature of its own. |
| Counted as | Which of the game's own groups it belongs to, which decides how many of it the world keeps around and when they spawn. Choose one of: An animal, A monster, Ambient, like a bat, A water animal. |
| Speed | How fast it walks. A cow walks at 0.2 and a zombie at 0.23. |
| Attack damage | How much one of its hits hurts, before armour. |
| Armour | How much of each hit its armour takes away, as a player's armour bar counts it. |
| Armour toughness | How well its armour holds against strong hits. |
| Knockback resistance | How much of a hit's push it ignores: 0 is none of it, 1 is all of it. |
| Follow range | How far away, in blocks, it notices a target and keeps after it. |
| Flying speed | How fast it flies, for a mob that flies. |
| Attack knockback | How far its hits push what they land on. |
| Step height | How high a step it walks up without jumping, in blocks. |
| Sound it makes | A sound, the game's or your own, it makes now and then. Empty keeps the game's. |
| Sound when hurt | A sound, the game's or your own, it makes when it is hurt. Empty keeps the game's. |
| Sound when it dies | A sound, the game's or your own, it makes when it dies. Empty keeps the game's. |
| Boss bar | Shows its health as a bar across the top of the screen to every player near it, as the Wither does. |
| Takes no hurt from | The damage types it shrugs off, the game's own and your own: a blaze takes no fire, a snow golem no freezing. |
| Tips over when it dies | Whether it falls on its side when it dies, as the game's own animals do. Off, it stays standing while it fades. |
| What it is doing | Which animation it plays for what it is doing. Edited on the Animations tab. |
| Order of its behaviours | Which of its behaviours comes first. Set by dragging them on the Mind tab, or with Move up and Move down. |
| Thinks every tick | A piece of your own code that the game runs twenty times a second for every one of these mobs, after its own goals, for what the settings here cannot say: a flight that circles and dives, a head that watches its own target. |
| Poses every frame | A piece of your own code that turns, moves, grows or hides its parts every frame it is drawn, after its animations: a body per stage of growth, segments that follow the head. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Damage type](editor-damageType.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

These point at it: [World event](editor-worldEvent.md), [Drop](editor-drop.md), [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Structure](editor-structure.md), [Game thing changed](editor-gameChange.md), [Species](editor-species.md), [Worn slots](editor-wornSlots.md).

# Mob behaviour editor

A piece of your own code that joins one activity of a mob's brain, the game's or another mod's.

## What you can set

Choose one of: Always (core), Idle, Work, Play, Rest, Meet, Panic, Raid, Before a raid, Hide, Fight, Celebrate, Admire an item, Avoid, Ride, Play dead, Long jump, Ram, Tongue, Swim, Lay spawn, Sniff, Investigate, Roar, Emerge, Dig. |
| Priority | Where it runs among the activity's behaviours: a lower number first. |
| Behaviour class | Your class's full name; it is made once for each mob, with no arguments. |
| Conditions | When the activity may run, one a line: a memory and present, absent or registered, such as tempting_player absent. They stand in for the activity's own, so list the game's too. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-configValue

# Mod settings editor

A setting players can change after the mod is built, in its settings file: a number, on or off, one word out of a list, or a list of entries they edit.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Mod settings

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the setting is called in the config screen. |
| Key in the file | The name of the setting in the settings file: letters, digits and underscores. |
| Type | What the setting holds: a whole number, a decimal such as a chance, on or off, one word out of a list you make, or a list of entries each with a few fields. Choose one of: Whole number, Decimal, On or off, A choice of words, A list of entries, Text. |
| Text | The words it holds until a player changes it. |
| Longest allowed | The most letters the settings file accepts. 0 means any length. |
| Value | What it is until a player changes it. |
| Lowest allowed | The settings file refuses anything below this. |
| Highest allowed | The settings file refuses anything above this. |
| On | Whether it is on until a player changes it. |
| Words | The words a player may choose from: small letters, digits and _. |
| Chosen | The word it is until a player changes it. |
| Which file | Common is one file for everyone; client is each player's own; server lives with the world. Choose one of: Common, Client, Server. |
| Each entry has | The fields every entry of the list has, each with its name in the file and what it holds. Each row has: Field, Holds. |
| Entries | The entries the file starts with, one a line, each field as name=value with ; between them. The player adds, changes and takes away entries in the file. |
| Comment | A line written above the setting in the settings file. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Recipe](editor-recipe.md), [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md), [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md), [Ritual](editor-ritual.md), [Feature](editor-feature.md).

## Picture

![Mod settings editor](/media/docs/editor-configValue.webp)

## Related pages

- [Mod settings](thing-configValue.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-model

# Model editor

The shape of a block, item or mob, made from boxes.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Model
- New thing > Mobs and models > Skin

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What this shape is called in the product. It is not shown in the game. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this model, in small letters with no spaces. The Name above is only for you. |
| Shape | The boxes and groups this shape is made of. Open the Model tab to build it. |
| View settings | What you set up to look at this model: reference pictures, wireframe, background. It stays in the project and is never put in the game. |
| Its pictures are | How the game draws what is clear in the pictures. Solid ignores it. With holes leaves a clear pixel out, as the game's own glass does. See-through draws each pixel as clear as it was painted, so what is inside can be seen. Choose one of: Solid, With holes, See-through. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Block](editor-block.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Projectile](editor-projectile.md), [Thing](editor-thing.md), [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md).

## Picture

![Model editor](/media/docs/editor-model.webp)

## Related pages

- [Model](thing-model.md)
- [Skin](thing-skin.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-movement

# Movement editor

How a living thing moves, the player or a mob: its speed and its jump, and a class of yours run as it moves.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Movement

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it in the project. |
| Living thing | Choose a mob, or a group of them such as the undead. |
| Speed | How fast it walks, as a share of its own; 1 is its own. From 0 to 20 normal. |
| Jump | How strongly it jumps, as a share of its own; 1 is its own. From 0 to 20 normal. |
| Each tick class | Your class's full name, or empty. It implements the mod's Movements.EachTick and runs every tick for each of them, a mob's on the server and the player's on its own client, where it may change its motion. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Movement editor](/media/docs/editor-movement.webp)

## Related pages

- [Movement](thing-movement.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-modRecipe

# Other mod's recipe editor

A recipe for a machine from a mod yours builds on, filled in by clicks.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Other mod's recipe

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The file name inside the mod. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. |
| Machine | The other mod's kind of recipe, read from its jar: each machine reads its own kind. |
| Recipe file | The recipe as the other mod writes one. The holes above fill it; it can be written here too. |
| Make one for every | Writes this recipe once for everything in the set you pick: dye colours, wood types, stone types, metals, gems, or a list of your own. Where the recipe says (each) (or <colour>, <wood>, <stone>), each one's name goes; one the game lacks is left out. |
| Loads only when | Whether the recipe exists at all. It is decided once, when the game loads, so a recipe for a mod that is not there is simply left out. This is not about the moment of crafting: use Works only when for that. Each row has: The pack, Name. |
| Add its mods by itself | When the recipe uses another mod's item or tag, it is loaded only when that mod is in the pack. Turn this off to load it always. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Other mod's recipe editor](/media/docs/editor-modRecipe.webp)

- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-painting

# Painting editor

A picture hung on a wall.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Painting

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The painting's title, which the game shows over it in the painting's list. |
| Game name | The painting's name in the game, as a command or a data pack names it. |
| Picture | What is painted. The game draws sixteen pixels a block, so a picture two blocks by two is thirty two pixels square; more pixels a block are finer. |
| Across | How many blocks it covers on the wall, across and up. The game's own go from one by one to four by four. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Up | How many blocks it covers on the wall, across and up. The game's own go from one by one to four by four. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Painted by | Whose painting it is, shown under the title. Left empty, no one is named. |
| Hung at random | Whether the game's own painting item may hang it when a player places one. Off, only a painting of it given by name hangs it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-particle

# Particle editor

Sparks, smoke, dust and the like.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Particle

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players see the particle, not its name. |
| Game name | The particle's name in the game, as /particle and another mod name it. |
| Picture | What one particle looks like; the game's own are eight pixels square. White takes the colour below as it is. |
| More pictures | Pictures after the first, shown one after another over its life or one chosen at random for each. Each row has: Picture. |
| Its pictures | Shown one after another as it ages, as smoke darkens, or one for each at random, as sparks vary. Choose one of: One after another, One at random. |
| Lasts | How long one lives before it is gone. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |
| Size | How large, where 1 is the game's ordinary particle, a fifth of a block. From 0.1 to 10. |
| Colour | The colour its picture is tinted: white leaves it as drawn. |
| Gravity | How fast it falls: 0 floats, 1 falls as a dropped thing does, below 0 rises. From -2 to 2. |
| Spreads | How fast it drifts away from where it appears, each way at random, in blocks a second. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Rises | How fast it moves up when it appears, in blocks a second; below 0 moves down. From -20 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Fades | It grows fainter as it ages rather than vanishing at once. |
| Glows | It is drawn at full brightness in the dark, as a flame is. |
| Stops at blocks | It lands on and slides along blocks rather than passing through them. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [World event](editor-worldEvent.md), [Block](editor-block.md), [Biome](editor-biome.md).

## Picture

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-projectile

# Projectile editor

A thing that flies, drawn by a model: a spell, a dart, a boomerang, a homing missile. Shot by the shoot words and a creature's Throw move.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Projectile

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players see it called. |
| Game name | Its game name in the game, small letters and underscores; the shoot words fire it by this. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front faces where it flies. |
| Speed | How fast it leaves, in blocks a second; a snowball flies 30, an arrow from a full bow 60. It flies at this speed whatever fires it; 0 is set down where it is made, as a lit charge. From 0 to 200 blocksPerSecond. |
| Gravity | How fast it falls: 1 falls as a snowball does, 0 flies straight as a fireball, below 0 floats up as a balloon. From -10 to 10 normal. |
| Damage | How much it hurts a mob it hits, in hearts. From 0 to 1000 hearts. |
| Picture | A picture of its own in place of the one its model wears. |
| Flight animation | An animation of its model it plays over and over as it flies: wings beating, a blade turning. |
| Scale | How big its model is drawn; 1 is the model's own size. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Spin | Turns a second about the way it flies, as a shuriken or a drill spins; 0 flies straight. From 0 to 20 perSecond. |
| Hitbox | How wide a box it hits with, in blocks. From 0.05 to 4 blocks. |
| Drag | How much of its speed the air takes each second; a snowball loses 18. From 0 to 99 percent. |
| Lifetime | How long it flies before it ends where it is, or turns back when it returns. From 0.5 to 120 seconds. |
| Knockback | How hard it pushes a mob it hits; 1 is a sword's own push. From 0 to 10. |
| Sets alight | How long a mob it hits burns; 0 sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Pierces | How many mobs it flies through before it stops at one. From 0 to 64 times. |
| Bounces | How many times it bounces off a wall before it ends there. From 0 to 64 times. |
| When it ends | What it does where it stops: vanish, stick in the block it hit as a thrown knife does, explode, break the block, or set fire. Choose one of: Vanishes, Sticks where it lands, Explodes, Breaks the block, Sets fire. |
| Explosion | How big the explosion is; TNT is 4. From 0.5 to 10. |
| Returns | Flies back to whoever threw it after it hits or reaches its reach, as a boomerang or a yoyo, through anything on the way. |
| Reach | How far it flies out before it turns back. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Comes back | When it turns back: at its reach or its first hit, or only when its thrower crouches, so it stays out as a yoyo held at the end of its string. Choose one of: At its reach or a hit, When its thrower crouches. |
| Rope | A rope from its thrower: it holds it no further than its length (a yoyo, a balloon on a string), pulls the thrower to where it sticks (a grappling hook), or pulls the mob it hits back to the thrower (a harpoon). Crouching lets go. Choose one of: No rope, Holds it at its length, Pulls its thrower to where it sticks, Pulls the mob it hits to its thrower. |
| Rope length | How long its rope is; past it, it is held back, or a hook that has not caught comes back. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Pull | How fast its rope pulls, in blocks a second. From 1 to 100 blocksPerSecond. |
| Rope colour | The colour its rope is drawn in. |
| Breaks blocks | How many blocks it breaks and flies on through, as a pickarang or a drill; 0 stops at the first. With Returns it turns back after the last. From 0 to 64 times. |
| Breaks up to | The hardest block it breaks: dirt is 0.5, stone 1.5, obsidian 50. A harder one stops it. From 0 to 100. |
| Collects items | Picks up the dropped items it touches and gives them to its thrower when it comes back, or drops them where it ends. |
| Homing | How hard it turns toward its target each tick: what its thrower fights, or the nearest mob. 0 flies where it was aimed. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Homing reach | How far it looks for a target. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Turns toward | What it homes on: the nearest mob (or what its thrower fights), only what its thrower fights or last hurt, or where its thrower looks, steered as a guided missile. Choose one of: The nearest mob, What its thrower fights, Where its thrower looks. |
| Comes down on | Flies its own way to a place and comes down on it: where its thrower looks, or on what its thrower fights (the nearest mob otherwise). Nothing: it flies as thrown. Choose one of: Nothing, flies as thrown, Where its thrower looks, What its thrower fights. |
| Arc height | How high its arc climbs on the way, in blocks. 0 flies straight there without falling. From 0 to 128 blocks. |
| Splits into how many | How many it splits into, fanned out evenly, like a cluster shell or a firework's stars. 0 never splits. From 0 to 32 times. |
| Pieces | Which of your projectiles it splits into. Empty: smaller copies of itself that do not split again. |
| Splits when | Where it lands, at the top of its arc as it starts to fall, or after a time of flying. Choose one of: It lands, At the top of its arc, After a time. |
| Splits after | How long it flies before it splits. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |
| Split spread | How wide the split pieces fan out, in degrees. From 0 to 180 degrees. |
| Holds what it hits | Sticks on the mob it hits and stays on it, slowing it, like an ice cube or a sticky bomb; at Slows 0 it only rides along, like a tracker. |
| Holds for | How long it stays on the mob. Then it ends there, with its Last hit and its When it lands. From 0.05 to 600 seconds. |
| Slows by | How much slower the mob it holds moves. 100 holds it still. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Carries | An item, block or mob it carries and lets out where it ends. Empty carries nothing. |
| How many it carries | How many of what it carries. From 0 to 64 times. |
| Lets it out as | Dropped as items, placed as blocks, or let out as mobs where it ends. Choose one of: Items, Blocks, Mobs. |
| Fuse range | It goes off this close to what sets it off, without hitting it. 0 has no fuse. From 0 to 16 blocks. |
| Fuse goes off near | What sets the fuse off: any mob, monsters, players, or a block of a kind. Choose one of: Any mob, Monsters, Players, A block of a kind. |
| Fuse block | The block or block tag that sets the fuse off. |
| Takes from what fired it | A stat of the weapon or ammunition that fired it goes into one of its numbers: a bolt hurts as its material does. Each row has: From its, Into its, How, Share. |
| Ammunition item | The item a weapon uses up to fire it with the Shoot ammunition line: a bullet, a shell, a bolt, or a #tag of them. |
| Trail | The particles it leaves behind it as it flies. Choose one of: None, Flame, Smoke, Heart, Crit, Portal, Happy, Soul, Snow, Enchanting letters, Music notes, Angry clouds, White clouds, Bubbles, A witch's sparkle, A totem's burst, A sword's sweep, End rod sparks, Glow squid light, Wax flecks, Electric sparks, Sculk souls, Water drops. |
| Hit sound | The sound it makes when it hits a mob or a block. Choose one of: None, Fire crackle, Thunder, Explosion, Anvil, Bell, Level up, Hurt, Pop, A door opening, A chest opening, Experience picked up, A button click, A villager agreeing, A villager refusing, An enderman's teleport, A portal's hum, A splash, Eating, A burp, The wither's arrival, The dragon's growl, A totem saving a life, An amethyst chime, A harp note. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Spell](editor-spell.md).

## Picture

![Projectile editor](/media/docs/editor-projectile.webp)

## Related pages

- [Projectile](thing-projectile.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-questBook

# Quests editor

Chapters of quests a player finishes for rewards, read in a book of the mod's own, each quest placed on its chapter's page.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Quests

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here, and the book's title in the game. |
| Game name | The name the mod knows it by. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Shared by | Whose progress it is: each player's alone, or shared by the players of one team (the game's own teams). Choose one of: Each player alone, The player's team. |
| Quests | Its chapters and quests, laid out on the Quests tab. |
| Layout | Where everything on the screen is, laid out on the Layout tab. |
| Quest shape | The outline a new quest is drawn in. A chapter may choose its own, and a quest its own. Choose one of: Circle, Square, Rounded square, Diamond, Hexagon, Octagon, Pentagon, Heart, Gear, No outline. |
| Quest size | How big a new quest is drawn, 1 the ordinary size, from a half to four. A chapter may choose its own, and a quest its own. From 0.5 to 4. |
| Page colour | The colour behind the quests. Leave it as it is to keep the ordinary one. |
| Page picture | A picture from your project drawn behind the quests, over the page colour. |
| Show the grid | The dots behind the quests that help the eye. |
| Line colour | The colour of the lines that join one quest to the next. |
| Done quests | The colour of a quest the player has finished. |
| Open quests | The colour of a quest the player can do now. |
| Locked quests | The colour of a quest that is not open yet. |
| Text colour | The colour of the words on the page. |
| Text size | How big the words are, 1 the ordinary size, from a half to double. From 0.5 to 2. |
| Rewards claimed by | In a book a team shares: whether each player of the team claims a reward for themselves, or the team claims it once. A reward may choose its own. Choose one of: Each player, The team, once. |
| Locked | The book shows its lock message and no quest counts until an operator unlocks it for a player with /<book> unlock. |
| Lock message | The words the book shows while it is locked. |
| Opens on | Straight into its first chapter, or first on a screen of yours whose buttons open the book at a chapter or a quest. That screen's Back button returns to it. |
| Button on the inventory | A button with its icon on the game's own inventory screen, survival and creative, that opens it: a way in with no item needed, beside an item, a key or a command. |
| Its icon | The item drawn on the button on the inventory. |
| Where it sits | Where the button sits: at a corner of the window, in a row with the other buttons there, as a quest mod's does; or by the inventory, above it at either end or beside it, moving with it when the recipe book opens. Choose one of: Top left of the window, Top right of the window, Bottom left of the window, Bottom right of the window, Above, at the left, Above, at the right, Beside it, on the left, Beside it, on the right. |
| Its look | The icon alone, lit when pointed at, as a quest mod's is; or the icon on a dark rounded button. Choose one of: The icon alone, On a dark button. |
| Toast for a quest done | The game's own toast, in the book's colors, when the player finishes a quest. |
| Toast for a chapter done | A toast when the player finishes every quest of a chapter. |
| Toast for the book done | A toast when the player finishes the whole book. |
| Toast for a reward | A toast for each reward the player is given. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Screen](editor-screen.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

## Picture

![Quests editor](/media/docs/editor-questBook.webp)

## Related pages

- [Quests](thing-questBook.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-recipe

# Recipe editor

Make something in a crafting table, furnace, stonecutter or smithing table.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Recipe

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The file name inside the mod. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. |
| Shape | Shaped keeps the things where you put them in the grid. Shapeless only cares which things are used. Smelting puts one thing in a furnace. Choose one of: Shaped, Shapeless, Smelting, Blasting, Smoking, Campfire, Stonecutting, Smithing, Trim, Transmute, Dye, Imbue, Brewing, Raw recipe. |
| Makes | What comes out of the crafting table. |
| How many | How many come out each time. From 1 to 64. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Slot | What goes in this slot of the crafting grid. Leave it empty for nothing. |
| Cooking time | How long it cooks. 0 is the game's own time for this kind: 10 seconds in a furnace, 5 in a blast furnace or smoker, 30 on a campfire. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Experience | The experience a player gets taking it out of a furnace. From 0 to 100. |
| Potion in the bottle | The potion that goes in. Leave it empty to turn a plain bottle item into the result item. |
| Potion that comes out | The potion the bottle becomes. Choose both potions to make a potion mix, for example awkward potion plus glowstone. |
| Trim pattern | The pattern the trim draws (from 1.21.5). Empty: the one the template is named for. |
| Also gives | More things a crafting grid gives with the result, each by its own chance. They come back as leftovers do: into the grid, else into the inventory; a crafter puts them out. On a furnace, blast furnace or smoker recipe they are given when you take the result out. Each row has: Thing, How many, Chance. |
| After crafting | What is left in a slot when the recipe is made. By default a thing is used up. It can stay, lose some durability (it breaks when worn out), or turn into another item. Each row has: Slot, Then it, Durability lost, Becomes. |
| Result from the inputs | How what it makes takes its data from what went in, in order: its enchantments, name, wear or colour, all its data, or the inputs' durability added up. Each row has: Takes, From, Bonus. |
| Slots with a rule | A slot that takes anything that passes a test instead of one thing: any of a list, anything with a tag, a value of at least so much, some data, or a gene. Each row has: Slot, Takes, Which, At least, The data is, But not. |
| Worked out from the inputs | What the result works out from what went in, each by a formula over the inputs' values: a value it holds, how many it makes, an effect and its strength, which thing it is, or an input's contents kept. Or all the parts kept inside it, so a robot built from them starts with them in its bag. Each row has: Works out, Which, Formula, Seconds. |
| Make one for every | Writes this recipe once for everything in the set you pick: dye colours, wood types, stone types, metals, gems, or a list of your own. Where the recipe says (each) (or <colour>, <wood>, <stone>), each one's name goes; one the game lacks is left out. |
| Loads only when | Whether the recipe exists at all. It is decided once, when the game loads, so a recipe for a mod that is not there is simply left out. This is not about the moment of crafting: use Works only when for that. Each row has: The pack, Name. |
| Add its mods by itself | When the recipe uses another mod's item or tag, it is loaded only when that mod is in the pack. Turn this off to load it always. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |
| Only while a number > 0 | For advanced rules: a number worked out where the recipe is made. The recipe works only while the number is above 0. Make it a formula to use any piece of the rules. |
| Show in recipe viewers | When this recipe works out its result from what goes in, the recipe viewers show a page for it: the inputs, the result and a line saying how it is made. Turn it off to keep the page out. |
| Example inputs for the page | The things the page draws as the inputs, separated by commas. Leave it empty to draw the first thing each slot takes. |
| Raw recipe | The studio has no picture for this kind of recipe. Its text below goes into your mod exactly as written. |
| Takes the place of | Pick a game recipe this one replaces. The game's own one is then gone. |
| Result name | A name for the thing this recipe gives. Leave it empty to keep the item's own name. |
| Lore lines | Lines of grey text under the name, one line each. Each row has: Line. |
| Enchantments | Enchantments the thing comes with when it is crafted. Each row has: Enchantment, Level. |
| Never breaks | The thing made by this recipe never loses durability. |
| Custom model number | A number a resource pack can use to give this copy its own look. 0 means none. From 0 to 100000000. |
| Other item data | Anything else the thing should carry, written as a JSON object with quoted names. It is added last, so it wins over the fields above. |
| Shares a book slot with | Recipes with the same group word show as one slot in the recipe book. Pick one that exists or type a new word. |
| Recipe book tab | The tab of the recipe book this recipe shows under. Choose one of: Building, Redstone, Equipment, Other. |
| Recipe book tab | The tab of the furnace's recipe book this recipe shows under. Choose one of: Food, Blocks, Other. |
| Show a note when unlocked | A small note pops up when the player learns this recipe. The game does this by default. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Potion](editor-potion.md), [Block](editor-block.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md).

## Picture

![Recipe editor](/media/docs/editor-recipe.webp)
