# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-recipeChange

# Recipe change editor

Change a recipe the game or another mod already has. Swap an input or the result, add inputs or extras.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Recipe change

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What it is called here. |
| Game name | Its name inside the game, in small letters. |
| Recipes | The recipes this changes: the game's, or those of a mod you build on. Find them by what they make or use, then read them. |
| Rule | The tests that pick recipes, kept as text. Change them in the editor. |
| Folder of the pack's mods | The folder with the mod files of your pack. Every recipe in them counts too. Leave it empty to use the game and the mods this project is built on. |
| Recipes the rule picked | The game names the rule picked when you last pressed Use these recipes. The build writes these. |
| What changes | A thing put in place of another wherever the recipe names it. Each row has: Swap, for, in. |
| Also needs | Things the recipe needs as well: in a shapeless recipe's list, or in the first free cell of a shaped grid. Each row has: Slot. |
| Also gives | More things a crafting grid gives with the result, each by its own chance. They come back as leftovers do: into the grid, else into the inventory; a crafter puts them out. On a furnace, blast furnace or smoker recipe they are given when you take the result out. Each row has: Thing, How many, Chance. |
| Result from the inputs | How what it makes takes its data from what went in, in order: its enchantments, name, wear or colour, all its data, or the inputs' durability added up. Each row has: Takes, From, Bonus. |
| As read | Each recipe as the game or the other mod has it, read when you pressed Read the recipes. The change is made on this. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

# Ritual editor

Offerings on pedestals around an altar, a catalyst on the altar, the conditions it asks, and the result it leaves on the altar.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Ritual

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the ritual is called in the studio. |
| Game name | The ritual's name in the game's data. |
| Altar | The block that performs it: any block that performs rituals. Rituals name their altar, so adding one changes no block. |
| Catalyst | The item that must lie on the altar. It becomes the result. |
| Offerings | One item a pedestal, in any order. Every pedestal within reach that holds an item must hold one of these. Each row has: Offering. |
| Result | What lies on the altar when the ritual is done. |
| How many | How many of the result it leaves. From 1 to 64. |
| Seconds | How long it takes. The offerings are taken one by one over this time. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| When | The time of day it may be started in. Choose one of: any time, by day, by night. |
| Levels it costs | Levels of experience the player who starts it pays. A player without them cannot start it. From 0 to 100. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |
| Only while a number > 0 | For advanced rules: a number worked out where the recipe is made. The recipe works only while the number is above 0. Make it a formula to use any piece of the rules. |
| Particles | What streams from each offering into the altar while it is performed. Choose one of: flame, smoke, heart, crit, portal, happy, soul, snow, enchanting letters, music notes, angry clouds, white clouds, bubbles, a witch's sparkle, a totem's burst, a sword's sweep, end rod sparks, glow squid light, wax flecks, electric sparks, sculk souls, water drops. |
| Sound | The sound it starts with and takes each offering with. Choose one of: fire crackle, thunder, explosion, anvil, bell, level up, hurt, pop, a door opening, a chest opening, experience picked up, a button click, a villager agreeing, a villager refusing, an enderman's teleport, a portal's hum, a splash, eating, a burp, the wither's arrival, the dragon's growl, a totem saving a life, an amethyst chime, a harp note. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-satellite

# Satellite editor

A launched thing that watches a place and reports back. A rule launches one over a place; every so often its report rule runs there and reads what you like (an area value, the blocks or mobs near), then acts: sets a value, notes a number on an item, sends energy down.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Satellite

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name of the satellite, as you and your players know it. |
| Game name | The satellite's name inside the game files. Lower case letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Reports every | How many seconds between its reports. From 1 to 86400 seconds. |
| Stays up for | How many seconds it stays up before it comes down. Nought: until a rule brings it down. From 0 to 31536000 seconds. |
| Covers | How many blocks round the place it watches count as covered, for the words that ask which satellites cover a place. From 1 to 100000 blocks. |
| No more than | How many of it may be up at once in the world. Nought: no limit. From 0 to 100000. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# Screen editor

| Pauses the game | Whether the game stops while it is open, in a world of one player. A world of several never stops. |
| Button on the inventory | A button with its icon on the game's own inventory screen, survival and creative, that opens it: a way in with no item needed, beside an item, a key or a command. |
| Its icon | The item drawn on the button on the inventory. |
| Where it sits | Where the button sits: at a corner of the window, in a row with the other buttons there, as a quest mod's does; or by the inventory, above it at either end or beside it, moving with it when the recipe book opens. Choose one of: Top left of the window, Top right of the window, Bottom left of the window, Bottom right of the window, Above, at the left, Above, at the right, Beside it, on the left, Beside it, on the right. |
| Its look | The icon alone, lit when pointed at, as a quest mod's is; or the icon on a dark rounded button. Choose one of: The icon alone, On a dark button. |
| Layout | Where everything on the screen is, laid out on the Layout tab. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-spell

# Spell editor

A spell of its own: what it does as rules (when it is cast, when it reaches a mob or a block, every tick it is kept up), what it costs (mana or any value), its cooldown and charge-up, and how it reaches: on the caster, along a ray, as a missile or all around. Cast by a wand, a scroll, any rule or a creature.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Spell

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the spell is called in the game. |
| Game name | The spell's game name in the game; another mod casts it by this. |
| What it is | A whole spell, or a part a spell is put together from: a medium says how a made spell reaches, a modifier changes it. A whole spell is also the part that says what a made spell does. Choose one of: A whole spell (or an effect), A medium (how it reaches), A modifier (what changes it). |
| Made of parts | Put this spell together from parts: a medium, effects (whole spells, this mod's or another mod's) and modifiers. Their costs add up and every part's moments run. Empty: it is a spell of its own. Each row has: Part. |
| Reaches | How it reaches what it does: the caster alone, what the caster touches, along where the caster looks, as a projectile, every mob around, or as a construct left where its ray ends. Choose one of: On the caster, By touch, Along a ray, As a missile, All around, Left in the world. |
| Range | How far its ray goes, or how wide its area is, in blocks. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Missile | What it fires: one of the game's, or a projectile of the mod's own. Its hit is the spell's hit. Choose one of: Small fireball, Fireball, Arrow, Snowball, Wither skull. |
| Construct | What it leaves where its ray ends: a ward hits everything inside it again and again, a trap waits for the first to come in and hits once, a sentinel hits the nearest one in reach. Choose one of: A ward (hits all inside, again and again), A trap (waits, hits once), A sentinel (hits the nearest). |
| Stays for | How long the construct stays in the world, in seconds. From 0.05 to 3600 seconds. |
| Acts every | How often a ward or a sentinel hits, in seconds. From 0.05 to 600 seconds. |
| Construct size | How far from its middle the construct reaches, in blocks. From 0.5 to 32 blocks. |
| Construct hits | Whom the construct hits: monsters alone, or every living thing but the one who cast it. Choose one of: Monsters, Everyone but the caster. |
| Split into | How many more copies of it go out as it is cast, fanned out to the sides: a split bolt, a fan of rays. From 0 to 16. |
| Power more | How much stronger it makes the spell, in a hundred: 50 is half as strong again. The power is handed to every moment of the spell. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Range more | How much further it makes the spell reach, and a construct wider, in a hundred. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Time more | How much longer it makes a kept-up spell and a construct last, in a hundred. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Copies more | How many more copies of the spell go out, fanned to the sides. From 0 to 16. |
| Cost more | How much more the whole made spell costs, in a hundred; below nought makes it cheaper. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Part item | The item that stands for it when a player puts a spell together in a block with slots (a rune, a herb, a focus), with the Make a spell word. |
| Costs | The value it is paid from: the player's mana, or a value the item that casts it keeps (a wand's charge). None makes it free. |
| Cost | How much of that value one cast takes; a kept-up spell takes this much a second. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Cooldown | How long before it can be cast again, in seconds. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Charge-up | How long the use is held before it goes, in seconds. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Grows while held | It goes when the use is let go, stronger the longer it was held, up to its charge-up time. |
| Power at full charge | How many times its own power it has when held for its whole charge-up. From 1 to 100. |
| Kept up | It goes on while the use is held, its moment every tick and its cost a second at a time: a beam, a stream of fire. |
| Lasts at most | How long it can be kept up at a time, in seconds; nought keeps it up while it can be paid. From 0 to 600 seconds. |
| Must be learned | Only a player who has learned it casts it (a spell book teaches it, or the Teach a spell word). |
| Kit | The kit it belongs to: a wand takes the spells of its kit. Empty is this mod's own; another mod's kit by its name adds the spell to that mod's wands. |
| Costs (another mod's) | A value typed by its name: another mod's (when the spell is paid from the mod it adds to), or the game's own: xp (experience points), levels, health or food. |
| Also takes | An item each cast takes from the caster's inventory (a reagent, a herb); none takes nothing. |
| How many | How many of that item each cast takes. From 1 to 64. |
| Also spends a stock | A stock of your own (matter held in items: a gas, an essence, mana in a jar) that each cast uses up from the items the caster carries. Pick a kind for any type of it, or one type. |
| How much of the stock | How much of the stock each cast spends. An item is used whole, so a little may be lost; with too little carried, the spell does not go. From 1 to 1000000. |
| Element | A word that sorts it: fire, ice, lightning, healing. |
| Tier | How strong it is, 1 to 10; a wand casts up to its own tier. From 1 to 10. |
| Trail | The particles along its ray, around its area, and around the caster while it charges. Choose one of: None, Flame, Smoke, Heart, Crit, Portal, Happy, Soul, Snow, Enchanting letters, Music notes, Angry clouds, White clouds, Bubbles, A witch's sparkle, A totem's burst, A sword's sweep, End rod sparks, Glow squid light, Wax flecks, Electric sparks, Sculk souls, Water drops. |
| Sound | What is heard as it is cast. Choose one of: None, Fire crackle, Thunder, Explosion, Anvil, Bell, Level up, Hurt, Pop, A door opening, A chest opening, Experience picked up, A button click, A villager agreeing, A villager refusing, An enderman's teleport, A portal's hum, A splash, Eating, A burp, The wither's arrival, The dragon's growl, A totem saving a life, An amethyst chime, A harp note. |
| Says | A line under its name on the wand's tooltip. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Projectile](editor-projectile.md), [Value](editor-value.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-stationRecipe

# Station recipe editor

A recipe done on a station's own screen, with cells, tanks and energy.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Station recipe

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this recipe. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this recipe. |
| Station | The block whose screen it fills. Its Slot groups give the cells. |
| Shape | Shaped matches the pattern anywhere in a group; shapeless any cells. Choose one of: Shaped, Shapeless. |
| Cells | What each cell of the station's screen holds, by the cell's name. Each row has: Cell, Slot. |
| Makes | What comes out of the crafting table. |
| How many | How many come out each time. From 1 to 64. |
| How often | Out of every hundred times the recipe runs, how many give its result. A hundred: every time. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| Seconds | 0 crafts when the result is taken, as a crafting table does. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| How much energy | Energy it uses over the whole craft; 0 for none. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Fluid in | A fluid it uses up from a tank, chosen from the list. |
| Fluid used | How much of the fluid each time; 1000 mB is one bucket. From 1 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| From tank | Which of the machine's tanks: 1 is its own, 2 and on the tanks added to it. From 1 to 5. |
| Make one for every | Writes this recipe once for everything in the set you pick: dye colours, wood types, stone types, metals, gems, or a list of your own. Where the recipe says (each) (or <colour>, <wood>, <stone>), each one's name goes; one the game lacks is left out. |
| Worked out from the inputs | What the result works out from the things in the cells, each by a formula: a value it holds, how many it makes, an effect and its strength, or which thing it is. Each row has: Works out, Which, Formula, Seconds. |
| Fluid out | A fluid it makes into a tank, chosen from the list. |
| Fluid made | How much of the fluid each time; 1000 mB is one bucket. From 1 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Into tank | Which of the machine's tanks: 1 is its own, 2 and on the tanks added to it. From 1 to 5. |
| More in and out | Any number of things more that go in or come out, beside the ones above: items, fluids or stocks of your own, each with how much and, coming out, how often. Each row has: Goes, What, Item, Fluid, Stock, Type, How much, How often, Tank. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |
| Only while a number > 0 | For advanced rules: a number worked out where the recipe is made. The recipe works only while the number is above 0. Make it a formula to use any piece of the rules. |
| Loads only when | Whether the recipe exists at all. It is decided once, when the game loads, so a recipe for a mod that is not there is simply left out. This is not about the moment of crafting: use Works only when for that. Each row has: The pack, Name. |
| Add its mods by itself | When the recipe uses another mod's item or tag, it is loaded only when that mod is in the pack. Turn this off to load it always. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Custom kind](editor-matter.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md).

## Picture

![Station recipe editor](/media/docs/editor-stationRecipe.webp)

- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-structure

# Structure editor

A building or ruin placed in the world.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Structure

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. The game never shows it. |
| Game name | The structure's name in the game, as a command finds it: /locate structure. |
| Made from | Built here, block by block, or a structure file saved in the game with a structure block. Choose one of: Built here, A structure file. |
| Blocks | Built on the Build tab, layer by layer. |
| File | A structure saved in the game with a structure block, from its generated folder. |
| Placed by | Whether the world's generation places it on its own, or it is only a piece another structure joins where its jigsaw blocks are. Choose one of: The world, Joining only, A rule, while playing. |
| Where | The biomes it stands in. Pick them by name, or choose the whole Overworld. |
| Spread | Where the world puts it: at random places kept apart, a set number in rings around the world's centre as strongholds are, or just one at the centre, in the nearest of its biomes. Choose one of: At random, kept apart, In rings around the centre, One, at the world's centre. |
| Apart | About how far apart two of them stand, in chunks of sixteen blocks. From 2 to 256 chunks. |
| Never closer than | The least distance between two of them, in chunks. From 1 to 255 chunks. |
| First ring at | How far from the world's centre its first ring is: strongholds' is 32 chunks. From 1 to 1023 chunks. |
| How many | How many of it the world has in all, set in rings around its centre. From 1 to 128. |
| Joins to | The pieces that join it where it has a jigsaw block, each as likely as its weight. A jigsaw block on an edge of a build faces out from that edge, and a piece joins it by one of its own facing back. Each row has: Piece, Weight. |
| Joins deep | How many pieces deep it grows from the first: each piece's own jigsaw blocks join the pieces it lists in turn. From 1 to 20 joins. |
| Ends with | A piece that closes a join when the structure runs out of depth or room: a wall or a dead end, so no doorway opens into the rock. |
| Fewest rooms | The least rooms a dungeon built by a rule has, the first and the last counted. It may have fewer only when no more fit at its doors. From 1 to 200 rooms. |
| Most rooms | The most rooms a dungeon built by a rule has. Each build picks a count between fewest and most from its seed. From 1 to 200 rooms. |
| Last room | The room built last, at the door farthest from the first room: where a boss or a treasure waits. Empty: the dungeon has no last room of its own. |
| Waiting in the last room | A mob that appears in the middle of the last room when the dungeon is built, and stays there. Empty: none. |
| Chest in the last room | A chest in the middle of the last room, filled from this loot table when it is first opened. Empty: no chest. |
| Used at most | How many times this room may stand in one dungeon built by a rule. 0 means as often as the dice give it. Once it has stood that many times, no more are placed. From 0 to 200 times. |
| Used at least | How many times this room must stand in one dungeon built by a rule. 0 means not asked. If the dice left it short, it is added at doors still open, even past the most rooms. From 0 to 200 times. |
| Close open doors with | The block that fills a door no room was joined to, so no doorway opens into the rock or the empty. |
| Door height | How tall a door left open is closed: the block of the door and the blocks above it. From 1 to 8 blocks. |
| Other first rooms | Other pieces it may start from, each as likely as its weight beside its own, which weighs 1. Each row has: Piece, Weight. |
| Spreads up to | How far its pieces may reach from where it starts, in blocks; the game allows 128. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Stands | How it meets the ground. Choose one of: On the ground, the ground raised to meet it, In a pit dug for it, Buried, the ground over it, Underground, at a height of its own. |
| Sunk by | How many blocks below the ground its lowest layer is. From -64 to 64 blocks. |
| At height | The height its lowest layer stands at, deep in the stone: 0 is far below the sea, the deep dark lower still. From -60 to 300 blocks. |
| Spawners bring | The mob each spawner in its build brings out, as a dungeon's does. A build without a spawner brings none. |
| Chests hold | What its chests and barrels are filled with the first time they open. Left empty, they hold what was put in them. |
| Containers hold | What each kind of container in its build holds: items of your choosing in counts fixed or random, or a loot table of the mod's own or the game's; several rows of one container all go in it. A row's container can also stand at random spots: it is there as often as its share. Each row has: Container, Holds, Item, Fewest, Most, Loot table, There. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Loot table](editor-lootTable.md), [Block](editor-block.md).

## Picture

![Structure editor](/media/docs/editor-structure.webp)

# Tag editor

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-texture

# Texture editor

The pixels a block, item or mob wears.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Texture

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this picture. |
| Replaces | The game's id for the texture this stands in for, like minecraft:block/stone. |
| Texture | The picture that replaces it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## In plain words

A texture is a picture. **Replaces** is for when your picture takes the place of one the game already has. Leave it empty for a picture of your own. For example, `minecraft:block/stone` is the game's name for the picture on stone, so a texture that replaces it makes every stone block in the game wear your picture. To make or import one, see [Pictures and textures](pictures-and-textures.md). To put your own picture on a new block, see [A block with your own picture](block-with-your-own-picture.md).

![Texture editor](/media/docs/editor-texture.webp)

- [Texture](thing-texture.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-player

# The player editor

The game's own player: its body, and rules for its moments, such as when it eats, is hurt or joins.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > The player

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| Max health | How many hearts a player has; the game's own is 10. From 0.5 to 512 hearts. |
| Size | How big a player is; 1 is the game's own size. From 0.0625 to 16 normal. |
| Speed | How fast a player walks, as a share of the game's own; 1 is the game's own. From 0 to 10 normal. |
| Gravity | How hard a player falls, as a share of the game's own; 1 is the game's own, below 1 floats. From -10 to 10 normal. |
| May fly | A player may fly as in creative, in every game mode. |
| Changes kept after death | What rules changed of a player's body stays after it dies; off, it starts again from the numbers here. |
| Reach for blocks | How far a player reaches to break and place; the game's own is 4.5. From 0 to 64 blocks. |
| Reach for others | How far a player reaches to hit and use a mob; the game's own is 3. From 0 to 64 blocks. |
| Step height | How high a player steps up without jumping; the game's own is 0.6. From 0 to 10 blocks. |
| Extra slots | Slots of your own beyond the game's, like rings or a back slot. They are kept with you, opened from a button on your inventory screen, and what is in them counts as worn. Each row has: Slot name, How many, Takes only, Look over, Starts showing. |
| Dropped when you die | What is in the extra slots falls to the ground when the player dies. Off, it stays in the slots. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md), [Value](editor-value.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-thing

# Thing editor

Something in the world that is not a mob and does not fly: a spell's ward, a frame on a wall, a floating orb, a balloon on a string, a trap. Made by a rule word, drawn by a model.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Thing

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players read above it, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front faces out of a wall it hangs on. |
| Animation | A clip it plays over and over as it stands. |
| Picture | A picture it wears in place of its model's own. |
| Drawn size | How big its model is drawn: 1 is the model's own size. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Spin | How many turns a second it spins as it stands. From 0 to 20 perSecond. |
| Width | How wide it is, in blocks: what can be hit and what it bumps into. From 0.05 to 16 blocks. |
| Height | How tall it is, in blocks. From 0.05 to 16 blocks. |
| When walked into | Walked through, stood on and bumped into like a block, or pushed along. Choose one of: Walked through, Solid, Pushed along. |
| Stays for | How long it stays before it ends by itself. 0 stays until it is broken. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Kept with the world | When on, it is still there after the world is saved and opened again. |
| Breaks after | How much it takes from hits before it breaks. 0 never breaks from hits (a player in creative still breaks it). From 0 to 1000 hearts. |
| Where it hangs | Where it is made (in the air), flat on the face of a block, or beside the one who made it. Choose one of: Where it is made, On a block's face, Beside its owner, Pinned to a block, On top of a block. |
| Fall | How fast it falls when it hangs nowhere. 0 floats in place; below 0 rises like a balloon. From -10 to 10 normal. |
| Height over its owner | How far above the one who made it it keeps. From -4 to 8 blocks. |
| Tied to its owner | A rope ties it to the one who made it, as a balloon on a string or a mob on a chain. |
| Rope colour | The colour its rope is drawn in. |
| Rope length | How far it can be from its owner before the rope pulls it back. From 1 to 32 blocks. |
| Rope pulls | Which way the rope pulls: it toward its owner (a balloon), or its owner back to it (a chained mob, a mob on a leash). Choose one of: It to its owner, Its owner to it. |
| Area | How far round it reaches, in blocks: the mobs inside are touched so often. 0 has no area. From 0 to 32 blocks. |
| How often | How often its Every time and Touches moments run. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |
| Touches | Whom its area touches. Choose one of: Every mob but its owner, Only monsters, Only players, Every one. |
| Particles | Particles it gives off as it stands, spread over its area. Choose one of: None, Flame, Smoke, Heart, Crit, Portal, Happy, Soul, Snow, Enchanting letters, Music notes, Angry clouds, White clouds, Bubbles, A witch's sparkle, A totem's burst, A sword's sweep, End rod sparks, Glow squid light, Wax flecks, Electric sparks, Sculk souls, Water drops. |
| Holds an item | A player puts an item in by using it and takes it out with an empty hand; it shows the item and drops it when it breaks. |
| Grows to | How many times its drawn size it grows to over its growing time, like a crystal. 1 does not grow. From 0.1 to 16 times. |
| Growing time | How long it takes to grow to full size. Its When it is grown runs then. From 0.05 to 3600 seconds. |
| Its box grows too | As it grows, the box that can be hit, touched and stood against grows with its drawing, so a crystal grown to twice its size is twice as tall to the game as well as to the eye. Off, the box stays its first size. |
| Sticks to what it touches | It clings to a mob or a player that touches it and goes along with them, like an ice cube or a web. Choose one of: Nothing, Mobs, Players, Mobs and players. |
| Slows it by | How much it slows what it sticks to, in percent. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Lets go after | Seconds before it lets go. 0 never lets go (until what it sticks to dies). From 0 to 600 seconds. |
| Joins others of its kind | Two of the same kind that touch become one. The new one is as big as both added, up to what it grows to. |
| Hurt only by | anything, nothing, or a list split by commas of damage kinds (magic, fire, explosion, projectile, player) or damage type game names. |
| Health | How much damage it takes before it breaks, when only some things hurt it. Its Breaks after number wins when that is set. From 0.5 to 1000 hearts. |
| Fire-proof | Fire and lava do not hurt or burn it. |
| Glows | Drawn at full light, even in the dark. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

## Picture

![Thing editor](/media/docs/editor-thing.webp)

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-value

# Value editor

A number or a list kept by an item, the player, a team or the world: Energy, XP, Kills, the foods a player has eaten.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Value

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads in the tooltip. |
| Saved as | The name it is saved as in the item's data, which a piece of your own code reads. |
| Kept by | The item that keeps it; each of that item a player holds keeps its own. |
| Shared by | Whose number it is: each player's alone, one shared by the player's team (the game's own teams), or one for the whole world. Choose one of: Each player alone, The player's team, The whole world. |
| Starts at | What a new one of the item has. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most | The most it can hold; adding past it stops there. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Holds | A number, a list of items, or words. A list is such as the foods the player has eaten: its number is how many items it holds, and rules add to it, take from it and ask whether it has one. Words are what a player types into a screen's text field. A list is each player's own. Choose one of: A number, A list of items, Words. |
| Tooltip if in the list | A line on an item's tooltip while the list holds that item, such as Eaten. Empty says nothing. |
| Tooltip if not | A line on an item's tooltip while the list does not hold it, such as Not eaten yet. Empty says nothing. |
| Tooltip on | Which items carry the line: foods only, or every item. Choose one of: Foods, Every item. |
| Comes back | How much it gains by itself each second, toward its most (a mana that refills); less than nought drains it. Nought leaves it to the rules. From -1000000000 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Waits after use | How long after it last went down before it comes back, in seconds. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Shown | Where a player sees it: a bar under the item's picture, a line of its tooltip, both, or nowhere. Choose one of: Bar and tooltip, Bar, Tooltip, Nowhere. |
| Bar color | The color of its bar under the item's picture. |
| Kept after death | For a value of the player: kept when it dies, or started again from Starts at. |
| Machines charge it | A machine with energy charges it in its slots, and modules spend it. |
| Charges at | How much a machine puts in each second. From 1 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Held by | Things that hold this value whatever is on them, the game's and other mods' too: an aspect, an essence, a worth. A recipe's formula reads it. Each row has: Thing, Amount. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Item](editor-item.md), [The player](editor-player.md).

These point at it: [Spell](editor-spell.md), [HUD number bar](editor-hud.md), [Tooltip lines](editor-tooltip.md), [Skill tree](editor-skillTree.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-vehicle

# Vehicle editor

Something to ride that is not alive, beyond the boat: a cart, a motor boat, a broom or an airship, a minecart of its own, a ride along a path. Steered with the game's own keys, with seats, fuel, cargo and parts.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Vehicle

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players see it called. |
| Game name | The name the game knows it by, in small letters. |
| Goes | How it goes: on the ground, on water, in the air, on the game's rails, or along a path of blocks with its riders inside. Choose one of: On the ground, On water, In the air, On rails, Along a path. |
| Looks like | The game's own minecart, with a block in it, or a model of its own. Choose one of: The game's minecart, Its own model. |
| Block in the cart | A block drawn inside the cart, by its game name, as a chest or a furnace in the game's own carts. Empty shows none. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front is the way it goes. |
| Animation | A clip it plays over and over. |
| Picture | A picture it wears in place of its model's own. |
| Drawn size | How big its model is drawn: 1 is the model's own size. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Width | How wide it is, in blocks: what can be hit and what it bumps into. From 0.2 to 8 blocks. |
| Height | How tall it is, in blocks. From 0.1 to 8 blocks. |
| Top speed | How fast it goes at most, in blocks a second. A horse runs about 10, a boat about 8. From 0 to 60 blocksPerSecond. |
| Time to top speed | How many seconds it takes to get to its top speed, and to stop again with nothing pressed. From 0.05 to 30 seconds. |
| Turn | How fast A and D turn it, in degrees a second. From 0 to 720 degreesPerSecond. |
| Climb | How fast it rises with the jump key and sinks with the sprint key, in blocks a second. From 0 to 40 blocksPerSecond. |
| Flies by | How it flies: hovering (a broom, a drone: the jump key rises, the sprint key sinks), on wings (a plane: its speed lifts it, it banks to turn and glides without power), or by thrust (a rocket: its engine against its weight). Choose one of: Hovering, Wings, Thrust. |
| Holds its height | When on, it stays at its height with nothing pressed; when off, it glides slowly down. |
| Take-off speed | How fast it must go before its wings lift it, in blocks a second. Slower in the air, it stalls and drops its nose. From 0 to 60 blocksPerSecond. |
| Glide | With no power, how many blocks forward it goes for each block down. From 1 to 60. |
| Most roll | How far A and D bank it, in degrees. The more it banks, the faster it turns. From 0 to 90 degrees. |
| Thrust | How hard its engine pushes up while the jump key fires it. More thrust than weight lifts it; a rule may set it from its engine blocks. From 0 to 100000. |
| Weight | How heavy it is against its thrust. A rule may set it from the blocks it is built of. From 0.01 to 100000. |
| Lands by | How it comes down: its engine brakes it near the ground, a parachute slows its fall, or nothing slows it. Choose one of: A landing burn, A parachute, Nothing. |
| Leaves the world at | The height at which it leaves for another world, its riders with it. 0 never leaves. From -64 to 4000 blocks. |
| Arrives in | The world it arrives in, by its game name: the End, the Nether, a world of the mod's own. Empty arrives over the same place in this world. |
| Arrives at height | How high it arrives over the same place, in blocks; from there it comes down. From -64 to 4000 blocks. |
| Gravity | How hard the world pulls it down, against the game's own pull: 1 is the game's, 0 floats. From 0 to 10 normal. |
| Drag | How much of its speed it loses each second with nothing pushing it: none coasts on, all stops at once. From 0 to 1. |
| Dives | Under water it goes down with the sprint key and up with the jump key, and holds its depth with neither, as a submarine. |
| Speed on land | Its share of its speed out of the water: a little for a boat, all of it for an amphibious one. From 0 to 1. |
| Also on water | It floats and drives on water too, as an amphibious car. |
| Boost | How many times faster it goes while the sprint key is held, spending fuel as fast. 1 has no boost. From 1 to 5 normal. |
| Steps up | How high a step it drives up without a jump, in blocks. From 0 to 4 blocks. |
| Steering | How its driver steers: by how it goes (where the driver looks in the air, A and D on the ground and water), A and D turn it, or it goes where the driver looks. Choose one of: By how it goes, A and D turn it, Where the driver looks. |
| Path of | The block it follows, by its game name, or a tag after a #. It goes straight on, turns where the line turns, takes the side its rider looks to where the line splits, and stops at the end. |
| Drives itself | When on, it runs along the rails by itself while it has fuel, as the game's furnace cart; when off, only with a rider. |
| Seats | How many can ride it. The first one on drives. From 1 to 8. |
| Riders unseen | Its riders are not seen while they ride, as when carried inside a pipe. |
| Seat height | How high its riders sit above its bottom, in blocks. From -2 to 6 blocks. |
| Fuel | What it needs to go: nothing, items put in, a fluid by the bucket, or whatever its rules give it. Empty, it stops. Choose one of: Nothing, Items put in, A fluid, What its rules give. |
| Fuel item | The item it burns, by its game name, or a tag after a #. Used on it, or kept in its cargo, it fills it. |
| Fuel fluid | The fluid it runs on, by its game name. A bucket of it used on it fills it, and the bucket comes back empty. |
| Fuel it holds | The most fuel it holds. From 1 to 1000000. |
| Fuel from one | How much fuel one item or one bucket gives. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Fuel used | How much fuel a second of going takes. Standing still takes none; holding its height in the air does. From 0 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Stops when empty | When on, it cannot go with no fuel left; when off, fuel only counts. |
| Cargo | Rows of nine slots it carries, opened by crouching and using it. 0 carries nothing. From 0 to 6. |
| Tank | How much fluid it carries, in millibuckets (1000 is one bucket). A block beside the rail that moves fluid by itself fills it or empties it. 0 carries none. From 0 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Tank takes | The fluids its tank takes, each by its game name (water, lava). Empty: any fluid, one at a time. |
| Battery | How much energy it carries. A block beside the rail that moves energy by itself charges it or drains it. 0 carries none. From 0 to 100000000. |
| Machine it carries | A block of your mod with its own slots and recipes that works inside the cart while the cart moves (a furnace cart, an apiary cart). Its slots are reached by a block that moves by itself beside the cart, and they drop when the cart breaks. |
| Part slots | How many parts a player can put in by using a part on it. From 0 to 8. |
| Built-in parts | Parts it always has, by their game names with commas between: a chest, a drill, a light. |
| Breaks after | How much it takes from hits before it breaks and drops its item, its cargo and its parts. 0 never breaks from hits. From 0 to 1000 hearts. |
| Its item | The item it drops when it breaks, and gives back when it packs up. |
| When left | What happens when its last rider gets off: it stays, or it packs up into its item in the rider's hands, as a broom. Choose one of: It stays, It packs up. |
| Sound while going | A sound it makes once a second while it goes, by its game name: an engine, wings, a rattle. |
| Sound standing | A sound it makes once a second with a driver while it stands, by its game name: an engine running slowly. |
| Sound boosting | A sound it makes once a second while it boosts, by its game name. |
| Lit | When it is drawn at full light, even in the dark: never, while it runs, or always. Choose one of: Never, While it runs, Always. |
| Hurts what it hits | How much a mob it runs into at full speed is hurt, and it is thrown aside; slower, less. 0 hurts nothing. From 0 to 100 hearts. |
| How often | How often its While it runs moment runs. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md), [Block](editor-block.md), [Item](editor-item.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

- [Glossary](glossary.md)

What a villager offers and asks for.

| From level | The villager's level it is first offered at: a novice's trades are the first two it has. Choose one of: Novice, Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, Master. |
| Rare | Among the wandering trader's rare offers rather than its common ones. |
| Wants | What the player pays. |
| Gives | What the player gets. |
| How many it wants | How many, before demand raises the price. From 1 to 64. |
| How many it gives | How many, before demand raises the price. From 1 to 64. |

| Price swing | How far demand and a player's reputation move the price: 0.05 for most, 0.2 for tools and armour. From 0 to 1. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-fluidReactions

# When fluids meet editor

What happens where a fluid meets another fluid or a block: lava meeting water makes obsidian, your own fluid meeting lava makes a block or drops an item. Each row says which fluids, what it makes, where, how often, and the sound and particles. It starts with the game's own two rows, which you can change or take away.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > When fluids meet

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What this table is called in your project. |
| Game name | The name the table is written under in the game's files, in small letters with underscores. |
| When fluids meet | One row for each meeting. A row is checked wherever the first fluid has the other fluid or block touching it, as the fluid is placed and whenever a block beside it changes. Each row has: This fluid, When it is, Meets the fluid, Or meets the block, Makes, As a, Where, How often, Sound, Particles, On the side. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Fluid](editor-fluid.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-ownWord

# Word of your own editor

A few lines you name once and use in any rule as one line: it is given as many things as it needs, and it can give back an answer.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Word of your own

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the word is called where a rule uses it, such as Greet or Bonus for. |
| First thing it is given | A name for something the rule that uses this word hands it, such as who or how much. Leave its kind at Nothing to hand it nothing. |
| Which is | What kind of thing it is given here. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no, A player, A mob, A place, An item. |
| Second thing it is given | A name for something the rule that uses this word hands it, such as who or how much. Leave its kind at Nothing to hand it nothing. |
| Which is | What kind of thing it is given here. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no, A player, A mob, A place, An item. |
| More things it is given | As many more things as the word needs, each with a name and what it is. The rule that uses the word fills each one. Each row has: Called, Which is. |
| It gives back | What the rule that uses this word gets back from it: nothing, or a number, words, or yes or no, set by a Give back line. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/editor-worldEvent

# World event editor

Something that happens to a whole dimension for a while: a blood sky, a fog bank, an aurora, a rift. When it starts, how long it lasts, what the players see and what it does round them. Rules start it, end it and ask whether it is on.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > World event

## What you can set

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name of the event, as you and your players know it. |
| Game name | The event's name inside the game files. Lower case letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Starts by itself | When the game rolls the chance below: at nightfall, midnight, sunrise or noon each day, or every minute. Never leaves it to your rules. Choose one of: At nightfall, At midnight, At sunrise, At noon, Every minute, Only when a rule starts it. |
| Chance each time | How likely it is to start each time the game rolls for it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| In weather | The weather it needs to start: any, clear, rain or thunder. Choose one of: Any weather, Clear, Rain, Thunder. |
| In dimensions | The dimensions where it can start by itself. Empty means every dimension. Each row has: Dimension. |
| Lasts | How many seconds it lasts. A rule can start it for another length. From 1 to 86400 seconds. |
| Lasts up to | Another length to pick between at random. Nought keeps it the length above. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Sky tint | The colour laid over the sky half of every screen in the dimension while it lasts. |
| Sky tint strength | How strong the tint is at its fullest, strongest at the top. Nought leaves the sky alone. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Fog colour | The colour laid over the whole screen while it lasts. |
| Fog thickness | How thick the fog is at its fullest. Nought brings no fog. It fades in the last five seconds. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Particles round each player | Particles thrown round every player in the dimension each second while it lasts: ash, spores, rain of sparks. Each row has: Particle, Each second, Spread over. |
| Pushes area values | An area value it adds to each second at every player's place while it lasts: a corruption rising, a rift charging. Each row has: Area value, Each second. |
| Calls mobs | Mobs that appear near each player while it lasts, so a night brings its own creatures. Each row has: Mob, Chance each second, No more than, Appears. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It points at: [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md).

These point at it: [Behavior](editor-behaviour.md).

## Picture

![World event editor](/media/docs/editor-worldEvent.webp)

## Related pages

- [World event](thing-worldEvent.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/things

# Things you can make

Press New thing, pick a category, then the thing. Each page says what it is and what you can set.

## Blocks and items

- [Area value](thing-areaValue.md): A number the world keeps by place, not by player or item: an aura in each chunk, an oil reservoir under it, radiation, a corruption that spreads, a pollution.
- [Armor](thing-armour.md): Something worn that protects.
- [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md): A block with a screen where a player fits, tunes, mends, names and takes apart the tool in their hand.
- [Backpack](thing-backpack.md): An item with slots of its own, opened from the hand.
- [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md): A bag that keeps the small pieces a carving tool takes away, by look, and gives them back when pieces are added.
- [Banner pattern](thing-bannerPattern.md): A pattern woven on a banner in the loom, and shown on a shield.
- [Battery](thing-battery.md): An item that keeps energy: charged in a machine, it charges the tools and armour a player carries, and powers a machine it is put in.
- [Block](thing-block.md): Something placed in the world: ore, stone, a crate.
- [Boat](thing-boat.md): A boat or a raft a player rows on water, with a chest or not.
- [Bow](thing-bow.md): The game's own bow, drawn and let go, to change: how long it draws, how hard and how fast what it shoots flies.
- [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md): An item that copies the blocks between two corners and builds the copy again wherever it is used, a few blocks a second, from the player's items.
- [Building tool](thing-builder.md): Places a square of blocks at once where it is used, a ghost of them shown first.
- [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md): A wand that lays a line, a wall or a box of blocks from a corner a player marks to the block it is used on, outlining it first.
- [Capsule](thing-capsule.md): An item that takes a box of blocks round the block it is used on, chests with their items too, and places it back wherever it is used next, showing a ghost first.
- [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md): A block made of small pieces of any block's look, carved on its Carve tab or by players in the world.
- [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md): A chisel or any tool that carves small pieces out of blocks or adds them, in one piece or a shape: a line, a flat square, a cube, a ball and more.
- [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md): A wand that copies the box between two corners and pastes it wherever it is used, outlining the paste first.
- [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md): An item that opens into a loot table when used, made with its table.
- [Crop](thing-crop.md): A plant that grows stage by stage on farmland from its own seeds, as wheat, and gives what it grows when it is ripe.
- [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md): The game's own crossbow, loaded and then fired, to change.
- [Designator](thing-designator.md): An item the player uses on a block to remember a place, then on an aiming block to give it that place as its [target](glossary.md#target).
- [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md): The game's own fishing rod: cast into water and reeled in with a catch.
- [Food](thing-food.md): Something eaten.
- [Forms for every material](thing-formSet.md): Makes a dust, a plate, a gear or any other form for every metal and gem the game has when it starts, other mods too.
- [Fuel](thing-fuel.md): Something a furnace burns.
- [Gene](thing-gene.md): A trait any thing can carry and pass to its young: a number such as Growth, or one of a few choices such as Coat colour.
- [Hat](thing-hat.md): Something worn on the head, drawn on the wearer from its own picture.
- [Item](thing-item.md): Something held in the hand or kept in a chest.
- [Letter](thing-letter.md): An item that holds a few things and is mailed to a player.
- [Material](thing-material.md): What parts are cut from, any item the game's iron ingot among them: its color, and the numbers and abilities it gives a part.
- [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md): An item that catches a creature with its name, health and everything it is, and lets it out again where it is used.
- [Module](thing-module.md): Something installed into a tool or armour that takes modules, switching an ability on and spending its energy.
- [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md): A disc that plays a song in a jukebox, the game's or your own, its words shown as it starts.
- [Ore](thing-ore.md): A block that appears in the world in veins.
- [Ore with a pickaxe](thing-oreWithTier.md): An ore that needs an iron pickaxe, its ingot and a pickaxe.
- [Part](thing-part.md): A part a tool is assembled from, cut from any material in the stonecutter, wearing its material's color.
- [Plant](thing-plant.md): A flower or small plant that stands on grass, as a poppy.
- [Pocket](thing-pocket.md): Put into a backpack in the crafting grid, it adds nine slots.
- [Pointer](thing-pointer.md): An item whose needle turns toward something: a transmitter on a channel, a mob you tagged, or the nearest block of a kind.
- [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md): A piece of armour that runs on energy: each hit its wearer takes spends some, and empty it guards nothing until it is charged.
- [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md): A tool and weapon that runs on energy instead of wearing out: each block and each hit spends some, and empty it mines as a hand.
- [Satellite](thing-satellite.md): A launched thing that watches a place and reports back.
- [Set](thing-set.md): Makes an ore, its ingot, tools and armor, with recipes.
- [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md): Copies one block's settings and gives them to another of the same kind.
- [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md): An item that copies the shape of a carved block and prints it again on another block.
- [Shears](thing-shears.md): The game's own shears: they shear sheep and cut leaves, cobwebs and wool.
- [Shield](thing-shield.md): The game's own shield, raised to stop a hit, to change.
- [Space station](thing-spaceStation.md): A built place in a dimension of its own that anyone or any vehicle docks with, orbiting a world at a height that rules move.
- [Species](thing-species.md): A kind of bee, plant or animal: the gene values it starts with, what it looks like as a block, an item or a mob, and which two species bred give it.
- [Spell](thing-spell.md): A spell of its own: what it does as rules (when it is cast, when it reaches a mob or a block, every tick it is kept up), what it costs (mana or any value), its cooldown and charge-up, and how it reaches: on the caster, along a ray, as a missile or all around.
- [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md): An item that teaches the spells listed on it when it is used, so a wand that casts the spells a player knows can cast them.
- [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md): An item that casts its spell once and is used up.
- [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md): An item that casts spells: the ones listed on it, or every spell of a kit the player has learned.
- [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md): Something thrown that flies as itself and hits: a throwing star, a javelin.
- [Tool](thing-tool.md): A pickaxe, axe or shovel, or a hammer that breaks a square at once.
- [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md): One tool that mines as a pickaxe, an axe, a shovel and a hoe at once.
- [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md): A tool assembled from parts in the crafting grid, its numbers and abilities its materials'; a part laid beside it swaps in.
- [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md): An axe that fells a whole tree from one log, outlining the tree while it is aimed at.
- [Value](thing-value.md): A number or a list kept by an item, the player, a team or the world: Energy, XP, Kills, the foods a player has eaten.
- [Vehicle](thing-vehicle.md): Something to ride that is not alive, beyond the boat: a cart, a motor boat, a broom or an airship, a minecart of its own, a ride along a path.
- [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md): An item put into a vehicle by using it on it, that works there every so often: breaks the blocks ahead, harvests crops, lights the way, shoots, blows up, or what its own rules say.
- [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md): A pickaxe that mines a whole joined vein of ore from one block, outlining the vein while it is aimed at.
- [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md): An item a player marks places of their own with, lists them and travels to them, each shown on a bar along the top of the screen.
- [Weapon](thing-weapon.md): A sword, an axe, or something new that hits.
- [World event](thing-worldEvent.md): Something that happens to a whole dimension for a while: a blood sky, a fog bank, an aurora, a rift.

## Crafting and loot

- [Armor trim](thing-armourTrim.md): A trim put on armor at the smithing table, in any of the game's materials.
- [Condition](thing-condition.md): A test in plain words, like half of the time, only in a biome, only at night.
- [Drop](thing-drop.md): What falls out when a block breaks or a mob dies.
- [Effect](thing-effect.md): Something that happens to a mob for a while.
- [Enchantment](thing-enchantment.md): A power added to a tool or weapon.
- [Extras for an item](thing-itemExtras.md): What any item, the game's or yours, also does: composts, burns in a furnace, or what a dispenser does with it.
- [Game thing changed](thing-gameChange.md): One of the game's own blocks, items or mobs given new values, such as a block's hardness, an item's stack size or a mob's health, a structure the game makes no more, or a limit the game sets, such as the anvil's most cost.
- [Item change](thing-itemChange.md): What happens to an item after it is made: its count, its wear, a name, a lore line, a random enchantment.
- [Loot changed](thing-lootChange.md): What the game's own blocks, mobs and chests drop, changed in place: things taken out, or one thing given in place of another.
- [Loot table](thing-lootTable.md): A weighted list of what can come out, rolled by a quest, a crate, a mob's or a block's drop, or a rule.
- [Machine recipe](thing-machineRecipe.md): What one machine of yours turns into something else, and what it costs.
- [Other mod's recipe](thing-modRecipe.md): A recipe for a machine from a mod yours builds on, filled in by clicks.
- [Potion](thing-potion.md): A drink that gives an effect.
- [Recipe](thing-recipe.md): Make something in a crafting table, furnace, stonecutter or smithing table.
- [Recipe change](thing-recipeChange.md): Change a recipe the game or another mod already has.
- [Recipes taken away](thing-recipesRemoved.md): Take recipes the game has out of the game.
- [Ritual](thing-ritual.md): Offerings on pedestals around an altar, a catalyst on the altar, the conditions it asks, and the result it leaves on the altar.
- [Station recipe](thing-stationRecipe.md): A recipe done on a station's own screen, with cells, tanks and energy.
- [Villager trade](thing-villagerTrade.md): What a villager offers and asks for.

## Machines and networks

- [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md): A block that gives wireless items a range to its network.
- [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md): A block that keeps a target place: a launcher's, a gate's other end.
- [Altar](thing-altar.md): A block that performs rituals with offerings on pedestals around it, formed while a ring of gold blocks lies around it; say in its rules what forming does: summon, teleport, give, open a portal.
- [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md): A chest that keeps itself stocked from the storage network or by couriers.
- [Cable](thing-cable.md): Carries energy between machines.
- [Chemicals](thing-chemicals.md): The chemicals kind, ready made: gases and other chemicals that tanks hold and pipes carry beside energy, fluid and items.
- [Chest](thing-chest.md): A block that holds items and opens a screen you lay out.
- [Configurator](thing-configurator.md): A tool that sets the faces of a placed block: right-click a face to step its mode, sneak to go back.
- [Crafter](thing-crafter.md): Holds patterns, so the terminal can craft what they make.
- [Crafting station](thing-craftingStation.md): A block with a 3x3 grid and a result, like a crafting table.
- [Custom kind](thing-matter.md): A matter of your own beside energy and fluid: a chemical, mana, heat, whatever your mod calls it.
- [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md): A storage cable that carries 32 channels instead of 8.
- [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md): A storage disk that holds fluids by the bucket's thousandths.
- [Drawer](thing-drawer.md): A block that holds many of one item, shown on its front.
- [Drive](thing-drive.md): A block whose slots hold storage disks.
- [Electric furnace](thing-furnaceMachine.md): A machine that cooks sand into glass using energy.
- [Face part](thing-facePart.md): An item placed on a face of a block that holds parts: it takes in, sends out, places, breaks, counts, shows or covers.
- [Fluid](thing-fluid.md): A liquid that flows in the world and fills a bucket, as water does.
- [Fluid tank](thing-fluidTank.md): A tank that holds 8000 mB and opens its own screen.
- [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md): A machine built of many blocks: it works only while the blocks around it stand as its pattern, drawn layer by layer on its Pattern tab, says.
- [Generator](thing-generator.md): Burns something and makes energy, on a recipe you write.
- [Generator with fuel](thing-fuelGenerator.md): A generator that burns coal into energy, ready to run.
- [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md): A filter as an item: marked in the filter of a pipe's face, that face lets through what its rules say, items and tags, mods, wear and enchantment.
- [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md): Carries items between chests and machines.
- [Link](thing-storeLink.md): A block that joins the chests beside it to every other link in range, with no cable: a spark or a crystal.
- [Machine](thing-machine.md): A block with an inventory, a tank or power.
- [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md): A part of a machine built of many blocks: pipes and cables reach the machine through it, using it opens the machine's screen, and while the machine stands its state "formed" is on, so it may look different then (give that look a picture, or an empty one to hide it under the machine's own model).
- [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md): Sends letters and keeps each player's post.
- [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md): A pipe that carries a matter of your own from the blocks that give it to the blocks that take it, holding none itself.
- [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md): A block that holds a matter of your own and joins pipes of it on every side: a chemical tank, a mana pool, a store of heat.
- [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md): The block a storage network can need to work.
- [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md): Turns a blank pattern into a recipe for the crafter.
- [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md): A block that holds one item put on it by hand and shows it floating above it; an altar's rituals take their offerings from the pedestals around it.
- [Pipe](thing-pipe.md): Carries fluid between tanks and machines.
- [Powered machine](thing-poweredMachine.md): A machine with a recipe that uses energy and time.
- [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md): A block that gives out the redstone sent on its channel, by a transmitter or by a rule.
- [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md): A chest that is the same chest wherever it is placed: every shared chest on one channel holds the same items, in every world.
- [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md): A tank that is the same tank wherever it is placed: every shared tank on one channel holds the same fluid, in every world, kept even while none of them is loaded.
- [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md): Joins cells, drawers, chests and terminals into one network.
- [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md): A block that holds many kinds of item, joined by cables.
- [Storage crate](thing-crate.md): A box that keeps what it holds when broken: carry it away full.
- [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md): An item that holds many kinds of item by count.
- [Tank](thing-tank.md): Holds a fluid and gives it to whatever asks for it.
- [Terminal](thing-terminal.md): Lists what the network holds, to take and put by clicks.
- [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md): Gives what it offers for what it wants, from its own slots.
- [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md): A block that sends the redstone reaching it on a channel, to every receiver on that channel, however far away.
- [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md): An item a player uses on a placed block that takes upgrades: it goes in and makes the block faster, bigger, quicker to move things or cheaper to run.
- [When fluids meet](thing-fluidReactions.md): What happens where a fluid meets another fluid or a block: lava meeting water makes obsidian, your own fluid meeting lava makes a block or drops an item.
- [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md): A block that sends the energy its cables bring on a channel, or, set to receive, gives out on its cables the energy the channel brings.
- [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md): An item that opens a terminal's screen from far away, while in its range.

## Mobs and models

- [Animation](thing-animation.md): How a model moves over time.
- [Attribute](thing-attribute.md): A number every living thing has, as luck and armor are.
- [Boss](thing-boss.md): A hostile mob with a boss bar, special moves and a phase it enters when it is badly hurt.
- [Damage change](thing-damageChange.md): A hurt a living thing takes, changed or cancelled by who takes it, who deals it and what it is, on every game version, without code of yours inside the game's own.
- [Flying mount](thing-flyingMount.md): A mount that flies with its rider, beating its wings on each jump.
- [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md): A creature built of parts and materials, as a golem is: used on a block it becomes the creature, its health, speed, armor, jobs and look its parts'.
- [Mob](thing-creature.md): A living thing with a model, animations and behavior.
- [Mob behaviour](thing-mobBehaviour.md): A piece of your own code that joins one activity of a mob's brain, the game's or another mod's.
- [Model](thing-model.md): The shape of a block, item or mob, made from boxes.
- [Mount](thing-mount.md): A mob tamed by riding it until it calms, then saddled, ridden and given bags and armour.
- [Movement](thing-movement.md): How a living thing moves, the player or a mob: its speed and its jump, and a class of yours run as it moves.
- [Painting](thing-painting.md): A picture hung on a wall.
- [Particle](thing-particle.md): Sparks, smoke, dust and the like.
- [Pet](thing-pet.md): A mob a player tames with an item; it sits, follows and fights for them.
- [Player animation](thing-playerAnimation.md): How a player's body moves for a moment, a wave or a bow, played on a player by a rule.
- [Projectile](thing-projectile.md): A thing that flies, drawn by a model: a spell, a dart, a boomerang, a homing missile.
- [Sea mount](thing-seaMount.md): A swimming mob ridden under water, its rider breathing.
- [Skin](thing-skin.md): A player's skin: the body and its picture to paint, with poses to show it in.
- [Sound](thing-sound.md): A sound the game plays.
- [Texture](thing-texture.md): The pixels a block, item or mob wears.
- [The player](thing-player.md): The game's own player: its body, and rules for its moments, such as when it eats, is hurt or joins.
- [Thing](thing-thing.md): Something in the world that is not a mob and does not fly: a spell's ward, a frame on a wall, a floating orb, a balloon on a string, a trap.
- [Villager job](thing-villagerProfession.md): A job a villager takes at its workstation, with its coat and its trades.
- [Worn slots](thing-wornSlots.md): Slots you name on any mob, the game's own or yours: a hat on a cow, boots on its four legs, a saddle on a pig, armor on a wolf.

## Logic and code

- [Access transformer (NeoForge)](thing-accessTransformer.md): Opens members the game keeps private, on NeoForge.
- [Access widener (Fabric)](thing-accessWidener.md): Opens members the game keeps private, on Fabric, in the game's own names.
- [Another mod](thing-dependency.md): A mod this one uses or works with, such as a recipe viewer: built against, in the test game, and named in both manifests.
- [Behavior](thing-behaviour.md): What happens when something happens: when this sword hits, set the target on fire.
- [Code](thing-code.md): A Java class of your own, kept safe when the mod is rebuilt.
- [Command](thing-command.md): A command typed in chat with a slash, whose rules run when a player types it.
- [Commands to run](thing-function.md): A list of the game's commands run together by name, when a world loads, or every tick.
- [Damage type](thing-damageType.md): A way of getting hurt, with its own message.
- [Dimension file of your own](thing-dimensionFile.md): A dimension written by hand as the game's own data file, which a biome source of your own code can fill.
- [File of your own](thing-ownFile.md): Any file the mod ships as it is, under resources/: data, assets, anything the game reads.
- [Game rule](thing-gameRule.md): A rule of the world, set with the gamerule command.
- [Locks](thing-locks.md): What a player may not use, wear, break, place, hit, enter or ride until they reach a skill level, a value or an advancement.
- [Look of a block made in code](thing-blockLook.md): The blockstate, models, loot table and name a block registered in your own code needs.
- [Mixin](thing-mixin.md): A piece of your own code that changes one of the game's classes, listed in your mixin config for you.
- [Mixin config](thing-mixinConfig.md): Your own mixins: notes placed inside the game's code.
- [Mod settings](thing-configValue.md): A setting players can change after the mod is built, in its settings file: a number, on or off, one word out of a list, or a list of entries they edit.
- [Pack file](thing-packFile.md): One file of a data pack or a resource pack, in any folder the game reads, yours or the game's changed.
- [Tag](thing-tag.md): A named group of blocks or items other rules can point at.
- [Translation](thing-translation.md): The names of your things in another language.
- [Word of your own](thing-ownWord.md): A few lines you name once and use in any rule as one line: it is given as many things as it needs, and it can give back an answer.

## The world

- [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md): A block that ripens in a minute in the light and gives berries when a player picks it, then grows again.
- [Biome](thing-biome.md): A region of the world with its own look and life.
- [Caves](thing-carver.md): Caves, ravines or Nether tunnels the world cuts into its ground.
- [Dimension](thing-dimension.md): A whole other world reached through a portal.
- [Feature](thing-feature.md): Something the world grows as it is made: a patch of flowers, a tree, a boulder, a lake, a vein of a block.
- [Structure](thing-structure.md): A building or ruin placed in the world.
- [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md): An item that finds the nearest of the structures it names and shows the way: an eye for a dungeon, a map stone for ruins.
- [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md): A block that marks where it stands by a name, for rules to send players there: a warp stone, a home, a town's gate.
- [World type](thing-worldType.md): A choice on the game's Create New World screen.

## Screens and guides

- [Advancement](thing-advancement.md): One of the game's own advancements: a goal with a toast, reached by an item, a kill or a rule.
- [Chest menu](thing-chestMenu.md): A chest's screen of items, one to six rows of nine, opened by a rule for one player; each item runs its own lines when clicked, and nothing can be taken from it.
- [Component](thing-component.md): A small layout placed inside other screens as one control: a card, a row of a list, a header.
- [Creative tab](thing-creativeTab.md): A tab of the creative inventory with the things you put in it, or your things added to one of the game's tabs.
- [Drawing in the world](thing-worldDraw.md): Drawn in the world from what the player looks at: an outline, the vein a key will break, a beam from the hand.
- [Guide book](thing-guideBook.md): A book of pages about the mod: words, pictures, items and recipes.
- [HUD drawing in code](thing-hudDraw.md): Your own code that draws on the HUD every frame, in a box you place on the screen.
- [HUD layout](thing-overlay.md): A whole screen layout you drag together: bars, words and pictures kept to a corner or an edge.
- [HUD number bar](thing-hud.md): One number of the player shown over the game as a bar or words, like saturation above the hunger bar.
- [Key binding](thing-keyBinding.md): A key players press to do something of yours.
- [Quests](thing-questBook.md): Chapters of quests a player finishes for rewards, read in a book of the mod's own, each quest placed on its chapter's page.
- [Research](thing-research.md): Studies a player researches with items, levels and time, each unlocking recipes and more.
- [Scene](thing-scene.md): A short in-game demonstration of how something works.
- [Screen](thing-screen.md): A screen of the mod's own, laid out by dragging: opened by a rule, or shown always over the game.
- [Skill](thing-skill.md): A skill with levels, like Mining or Farming: XP comes from any moment, each level reached runs its rewards, and locks may wait for a level.
- [Skill tree](thing-skillTree.md): Skills a player buys with points, each after the ones it needs.
- [Tooltip lines](thing-tooltip.md): Lines added to the tooltip of any item or block, the mod's or the game's, or of every item, each filled in from the item's numbers and values and shown by its own condition.

## Project kinds

- [Mod](project-mod.md): Blocks, items, recipes and everything else, built for NeoForge and Fabric.
- [Data pack](project-datapack.md): Recipes, drops, tags and world data with no code, for a plain game.
- [Resource pack](project-resourcepack.md): Textures, models, sounds and translations for the game's own things.
- [Modpack](project-modpack.md): A collection of published mods, yours and other people's, ready to install.
- [Extension](project-extension.md): New kinds of things, or a new game version, for Modryos itself.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-accessPoint

# Access point

A block that gives wireless items a range to its network. Upgrades widen it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Access point


## What you can set

### Wireless access point

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Range | How far from this block a wireless item that needs an access point still works. 0: anywhere in the same world. From 0 to 100000 blocks. |

### Takes upgrades

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Upgrades it takes | How many upgrades it holds at once: in a block with an inventory, the last places of it, slots of its screen. They fall out when it is broken. From 0 to 16. |
| Takes tiers up to | The highest tier of upgrade it takes: an upgrade of a higher tier does not go in. From 1 to 5. |
| Tier | How many times over it works, holds and moves from the start, before any upgrade: 1 is as its numbers say. From 1 to 64 times. |
| A tier of | The block of its set whose recipes it runs, so a higher tier makes what the first one makes. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Wireless access point, Takes upgrades.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-advancement

# Advancement

One of the game's own advancements: a goal with a toast, reached by an item, a kill or a rule.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Advancement


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Advancement](editor-advancement.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The title the game shows in its toast and its advancements screen. |
| Game name | The name the mod knows it by. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Words | The line under the title. |
| Picture | The item drawn beside its title. |
| Reached by | Having an item, killing a mob, a rule that grants it, or any of the things the game watches for. Choose one of: Having an item, Killing a mob, A rule, Anything the game watches for. |
| Item | The item a player must have. |
| Mob | The mob a player must kill, chosen from the list. |
| Needs | Whether a player must do all of these things, or any one of them. Choose one of: All of them, Any one of them. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Condition](editor-condition.md).
