# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-chest

# Chest

A block that holds items and opens a screen you lay out.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Chest


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-chestMenu

# Chest menu

A chest's screen of items, one to six rows of nine, opened by a rule for one player; each item runs its own lines when clicked, and nothing can be taken from it. It works for players who did not install the mod: a welcome menu, a shop, a kit, a warp list.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Chest menu


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Chest menu](editor-chestMenu.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the menu is called in the project. A rule opens it by this name. |
| Game name | The name the game knows the menu by inside the mod: lower case letters, digits and underscores. |
| Title | The words over the items, where a chest says Chest. Empty, the menu's own name. |
| Rows | How many rows of nine slots it has, from one to six, as a chest or a double chest has. From 1 to 6. |
| Items | What the menu shows, each in its slot with its name and its line. Each one clicked is a moment of its own on the Behavior tab. Each row has: Slot, Shown as, Name, Line, Closes the menu. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-command

# Command

A command typed in chat with a slash, whose rules run when a player types it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Command


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Command](editor-command.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| Typed as | What a player types after the slash. Add a second word for a sub-command: goatapples reload becomes /goatapples reload. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Who may run it | Every player, or only operators. Choose one of: Everyone, Operators. |
| How trusted they must be | As the game counts it: 1 may pass spawn protection, 2 may use cheats and command blocks, 3 may kick and ban, 4 may stop the server. The server console is 4. From 1 to 4. |
| Short name is fine | Turn on to stop the warning that another mod may use the same first word. Players can always type /<your mod's game name> <command> instead. |
| May be run from the console | Typed in the server's own window, where nobody ran it: lines that need the player who ran it are left out then, and say so. |
| Typed after it | What a player types after the command, in order, each with a name the game shows and suggests it by. A rule of the command uses each by its name. Each row has: Called, Which is, Its choices. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-copyWand

# Copy wand

A wand that copies the box between two corners and pastes it wherever it is used, outlining the paste first.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Copy wand


## What you can set

### Acts on many blocks

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| What it does | Line: blocks in a straight run from the marked corner to the block used on. Wall: a wall standing on that run, as high as the two corners are apart. Box: the whole box between them. Copy: the box between the marked corner and the block used on is copied, then each use pastes it. Tree: mining a log fells every log of the tree. Vein: mining a block breaks every joined block of its kind. Choose one of: A line, A wall, A box, Copy and paste, Fell a tree, Mine a vein. |
| At most | The most blocks one action places, copies or breaks, 1 to 4096. From 1 to 4096. |
| Places | The block it places: the one in the player's other hand, or one chosen here. Choose one of: Off-hand block, A chosen block. |
| Block | The block it places, picked by its name in the game's list of blocks. |
| Only | The blocks it starts on: one block, or a group of blocks such as every ore. Empty: any block; a tree always starts on a log. |
| Uses up blocks | Each block placed is taken from the player's inventory, as placing it by hand would; off, it places for free. In creative it is always free. |
| Turns with you | A paste is turned as far as the player has turned since the copy: copied facing north, pasted facing east, it is turned a quarter, doors and stairs too. |
| Outline first | While it is held, what it would place, copy or break is outlined round the block under the cross, before anything is done. |
| Can undo | Used in the air while sneaking, it puts back what its last action changed and gives the blocks back, up to ten actions back. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Crafter

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Keeps in stock | A thing the crafter keeps the network stocked with: while there are fewer than the number below, it crafts more from its patterns. None: it crafts only when asked. |
| Keeps at least | How many of the thing above the network should hold. The crafter checks every two seconds and crafts up to a stack at a time. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Jobs at once | How many crafting requests the patterns in this crafter run at the same time. A job over the limit waits. From 1 to 1000. |
| Seconds a step takes | How long this crafter waits between the steps of its patterns when the store is asked to craft. 0: as fast as the game checks. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Patterns made in a machine | Each row is a pattern that sends things to a machine next to the crafter: it takes the inputs out of the network, puts them into the machine, and waits for the result to come back. Works with any block that takes items or fluids, from any mod. Each row has: Kind, First thing that goes in, How many, Second thing that goes in, How many, Fluid that goes in, Amount of fluid, Item that comes out, How many come out, Fluid that comes out, Amount of fluid. |
| Machine side | Which side of the crafter has the machine. Any side: every block next to the crafter that takes the things is tried. Choose one of: Any side, Up, Down, North, South, East, West. |
| Give up after | How long the crafter waits for a machine to give back what it made. After that the pattern gives up and the request is marked as short. From 1 to 86400 seconds. |
| Runs at once | How many runs of a machine pattern wait on machines at the same time. More wait their turn. From 1 to 64. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Crafter.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-crop

# Crop

A plant that grows stage by stage on farmland from its own seeds, as wheat, and gives what it grows when it is ripe.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Crop


## What you can set

### Grows as a plant

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Stages | How many times it grows before it is ripe: wheat grows 7 times, beetroot 3. 0 is a flower that never grows. Each stage wears its own picture; ripe, it wears the block's own. From 0 to 7. |
| Picture just planted | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 1 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 2 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 3 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 4 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 5 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Picture at stage 6 | What it wears at this stage; with none it wears the block's own picture. |
| Gives when ripe | What breaking it ripe gives, the game's or your own, as wheat gives wheat; its seeds come too. Broken before, it gives back one seed. |
| Up to | At most this many of it, at least one. From 1 to 16. |
| Stands on | What it can be planted on and stays on: farmland as wheat, grass and dirt as a flower, sand as a cactus, or the top of anything solid. Take that away and it breaks. Choose one of: Farmland, Grass and dirt, Sand, Anything solid. |
| Drawn as | A crop is four upright pictures in a square, as wheat; a cross is two pictures crossing, as a flower or a sapling. Choose one of: A crop, A cross. |
| Name of its seeds | What the seeds that plant it are called in the game, as Wheat Seeds; with none, its own name and Seeds. |
| Picture of its seeds | The seeds in the hand and the inventory; with none, its first picture. |
| Bone meal grows it | Bone meal on it makes it grow a stage or more at once, as on wheat. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-crossbow

# Crossbow

The game's own crossbow, loaded and then fired, to change.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Crossbow


## What you can set

### Shoots

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Works like | Which of the game's own it starts from: a bow drawn and let go, a crossbow loaded and then fired, or thrown as a snowball or a trident is, the thing itself flying. Choose one of: The game's Bow, The game's Crossbow, Thrown. |
| Damage | What what it shoots takes from what it hits, where a heart is 2: the game's arrow 2 before its speed counts, a trident 8. From 0 to 1000. |
| Full draw | How long it takes to draw fully; let go sooner and it shoots weaker, as the game's bow does in its 1 second. From 0.05 to 10 seconds. |
| Flies at | How fast what it shoots flies, against the game's own: 1 is the game's, 2 twice as fast and farther. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Burning | What it shoots flies alight and sets what it hits on fire, as the Flame enchantment does. |
| Where it lands | What a thrown thing does when it hits: lies there to be picked up again, or breaks. Choose one of: Lies there, Breaks. |
| Flies | How it is drawn in flight: lying flat and spinning as a throwing star, point first as a javelin, or turned to the camera as the game draws a snowball. Choose one of: Flat, spinning, Point first, Facing the camera. |
| Shoots | What it looses: the game's arrow, or a projectile of your mod's own, which flies by its own settings. Choose one of: Arrow. |
| Shoots | What it takes from the inventory and shoots in place of arrows, yours or the game's, or any item of a tag; picked up again where it lands. With none, arrows. |
| Loading time | How long it takes to load, held before it is ready to fire; the game's crossbow takes 1.25 seconds. From 0.05 to 10 seconds. |
| Shots at once | How many it looses at once from one piece of ammunition, fanned out, as a crossbow with Multishot looses three. From 1 to 16 times. |
| Fan | How wide the shots at once fan out, in degrees from the first to the last. From 0 to 180 degrees. |
| Pause | Seconds before it can be thrown again, as the game's ender pearl waits 1. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Drawing | The picture as the draw begins. |
| Half drawn | The picture half way through the draw. |
| Drawn | The picture fully drawn. |
| Loaded | The picture of a crossbow loaded and ready to fire. |

### Wears out

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Uses before it breaks | How many blocks it mines, hits it lands or hits it takes before it breaks: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mended with | What mends it in an anvil, such as an iron ingot, or one of this mod's own things. |
| Comes enchanted with | Enchantments it has from the first time a player holds it, the game's own or your own, each at its level. Each row has: Enchantment, Level. |
| Enchants how well | How good the enchantments it is offered are: iron 14, diamond 10, gold 22. From 0 to 50. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Shoots, Wears out.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Face part](thing-facePart.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-matter

# Custom kind

A matter of your own beside energy and fluid: a chemical, mana, heat, whatever your mod calls it. Blocks hold it in tanks, pipes and channels carry it, rules move it and moving parts show it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Custom kind


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Custom kind](editor-matter.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players call it, as it is shown. |
| Key | The name blocks keep it under, as the game keeps it with your mod's game name in front. |
| Counted in | The word for one of it, shown after its amount: mana, units, degrees. |
| Colour | The colour it is drawn in where it shows. |
| Types | The types of it, each with a name and a colour: oxygen and hydrogen of a gas, fire and water of a magic essence. A tank of it takes any one type at a time, unless it names one. Each row has: Name, Key, Colour, Made of. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-damageChange

# Damage change

A hurt a living thing takes, changed or cancelled by who takes it, who deals it and what it is, on every game version, without code of yours inside the game's own.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Damage change


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Damage change](editor-damageChange.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it in the project. |
| Taken by | What is hurt: choose a mob, or a group of them such as skeletons. Empty means any living thing. |
| Dealt by | What deals the hurt: choose a mob (a skeleton for its arrow), or a group of them. Empty means anything or nothing. |
| Damage type | What the hurt is, such as falling or fire, chosen from the list. Empty means any. |
| Change | What happens to the hurt. Changes run in the order of their elements; a hurt brought to 0 or less is not dealt. Choose one of: Multiply it, Add to it, Set it, Cancel it, Your class decides. |
| Amount | What it is multiplied by, added to it or set to, in health points (a heart is two). From -1000 to 1000. |
| Change class | Your class's full name. It implements the mod's Damages.Change: handed what is hurt, the damage source and the amount, it answers the amount dealt. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-denseCable

# Dense cable

A storage cable that carries 32 channels instead of 8.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Dense cable


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### Channels

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channels | How many things beyond it one cable can lead to. 8 is a plain cable, 32 a dense one, 0 no limit. From 0 to 100000. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Connections, Channels.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

## What you can set

### Sets a block's target

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-dimension

# Dimension

A whole other world reached through a portal.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Dimension


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Dimension](editor-dimension.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| Game name | The dimension's name in the game, as a command goes there: /execute in. |
| Its land | What its ground is like. Choose one of: Hills and valleys, as the overworld's, Shaped land, each biome its own, Islands floating in the sky, Caves under a ceiling of rock, Flat, in layers, Empty, nothing at all. |
| Biomes | The biomes it is made of, yours and the game's, each taking a share of its land. |
| Rock | The block its hills are made of, under each biome's own ground. |
| Sea | What fills its low places. Choose one of: Water, Lava, Nothing. |
| Land height | The height its land stands at; each biome stands above or below it by its own land height. From -32 to 256 blocks. |
| Hilliness | How hilly the whole dimension is; each biome's roughness is a share of it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Caves | The caves cut into its ground: none, winding tunnels, or tunnels and great caverns as the overworld's. Choose one of: None, Tunnels, Tunnels and caverns. |
| Layers | Its ground from the bottom up, each layer a block and how thick it is. Each row has: Block, Thick. |
| Time | Whether day turns to night there. Choose one of: Day and night, as the overworld, Always day, Always night. |
| Sky | What is over it. The colours of its sky and fog are its biomes'. Choose one of: A sky with the sun and the moon, No sky, a thick haze, A dark sky, as the end's. |
| Clouds | Whether clouds drift over it, under a sky with the sun and the moon. |
| Light in the dark | How bright its darkest places are: none is as the overworld at night. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Portal | A way in, as the nether's: a frame of a block, lit by an item. Its inside becomes a portal; standing in it takes a player there and back. |
| Frame | The block its frame is built of, two to twenty one wide and three to twenty one high inside. |
| Lit by | The item a player uses on the frame to open it. |
| Portal colour | The colour of the swirl inside the frame. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Block](editor-block.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-drawer

# Drawer

A block that holds many of one item, shown on its front.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Drawer


## What you can set

### Drawer

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Holds | How many stacks of its item it holds. A capacity upgrade adds to it. From 1 to 100000 stacks. |
| Shows on front | Draws the item and how many on its front. |
| Keeps its item | Emptied, it still holds the place of its item, so only that item goes in again. |
| Voids the rest | Full, it still takes its item and destroys what does not fit, so a hopper or a pipe never backs up. |
| Kinds it holds | How many kinds it holds at once: 1, 2 side by side, or 4 in two rows. Each place has its own item and count. Click a place to put in or take out there. Choose one of: 1, 2, 4. |
| Compacts | One drawer for a whole chain, such as nugget, ingot and block. Any of them goes in and comes out, counted together. |
| The chain | The items, smallest first. Each is worth the next step's number of the one before. |
| Each step is worth | How many of one make the next, such as 9 nuggets or ingots for the one above. Match the recipes that craft them. From 2 to 64. |
| Hides the item | Its front does not show the item. A key item with the Turn a drawer setting action turns this on and off in the game. |
| Shows how many | Its front says how many. A key item with the Turn a drawer setting action turns this on and off in the game. |

### Takes upgrades

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Upgrades it takes | How many upgrades it holds at once: in a block with an inventory, the last places of it, slots of its screen. They fall out when it is broken. From 0 to 16. |
| Takes tiers up to | The highest tier of upgrade it takes: an upgrade of a higher tier does not go in. From 1 to 5. |
| Tier | How many times over it works, holds and moves from the start, before any upgrade: 1 is as its numbers say. From 1 to 64 times. |
| A tier of | The block of its set whose recipes it runs, so a higher tier makes what the first one makes. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Drawer, Takes upgrades.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-drive

# Drive

A block whose slots hold storage disks. Everything on its disks is in the network.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Drive


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Drive

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | Higher fills first and is emptied first. Chests and cells are 0. From -1000 to 1000. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Drive.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-drop

# Drop

What falls out when a block breaks or a mob dies.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Drop


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Drop](editor-drop.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The file name inside the mod. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. |
| From | The block broken or the mob killed that gives it. |
| Or the game's | Blocks and mobs of the game or another mod that drop it too, each one or a tag of them; another mod's is typed. What they drop already stays. |
| Gives | One item, or a roll of a loot table: a crate, or a handful of anything. Choose one of: An item, A loot table. |
| Drops | What it gives. Pick one of your things or one of the game's. |
| At least | The fewest that can drop. From 0 to 64. |
| At most | The most that can drop. From 1 to 64. |
| Loot table | The loot table rolled when it drops. |
| Chance | How often it drops, out of a hundred. From 0.1 to 100 percent. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Loot table](editor-lootTable.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-effect

# Effect

Something that happens to a mob for a while.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Effect


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Effect](editor-effect.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The effect's name, as the inventory and a potion's lines show it. |
| Game name | The effect's name in the game, as /effect and another mod name it. |
| Icon | The picture the inventory and the corner of the screen show while it lasts. The game draws its own at eighteen pixels square. |
| Is | Good, bad or neither: the game draws a bad one's icon with a red edge, and milk takes every one away. Choose one of: Good for you, Bad for you, Neither. |
| Colour | The colour of its swirls round whoever has it, and of a potion of it. |
| Changes to the body | The body's numbers it changes while it lasts, more each level, as Speed makes a player a fifth faster a level. Each row has: Changes, By, As. |
| While it lasts | What it does by itself every so often, sooner each level, as Poison and Regeneration do. Choose one of: Nothing more, Hurts, Heals, Feeds, Sets on fire. |
| How much | Hearts of hurt or healing, points of food, or seconds of fire each time. From 0 to 1000. |
| Every | How often at level I; each level after does it twice as often. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-itemExtras

# Extras for an item

What any item, the game's or yours, also does: composts, burns in a furnace, or what a dispenser does with it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Extras for an item


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Extras for an item](editor-itemExtras.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What it is called here. |
| Game name | Its name inside the game, in small letters. |
| Item | The item these extras are for, the game's or yours. |
| Composter chance | The chance one put in a composter raises its level, as seeds 30, bread 85; 0 is not at all. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Burns for | How many items one of it smelts as a furnace's fuel, as coal 8; 0 is not a fuel. From 0 to 1000 items. |
| A dispenser | What a dispenser does with it: drops it as it drops anything, places it as a block, or grows the plant in front of it as bone meal does. Choose one of: Drops it, Places it as a block, Grows plants as bone meal. |
| Stacks to | How many fit in one stack, up to 99, such as ender pearls 64; 0 keeps the game's. Items that wear out stack to 1. From 0 to 99. |
| Uses | How many uses it lasts before it breaks; 0 keeps the game's. An item given uses stacks to 1. From 0 to 100000. |
| A page in the recipe viewers | Plain lines, one per line, shown as this item's info page in the recipe viewers a player has installed. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-facePart

# Face part

An item placed on a face of a block that holds parts: it takes in, sends out, places, breaks, counts, shows or covers.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Face part


## What you can set

### A face part

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Does | What the part does with the block it faces or the space in front of it. Choose one of: Takes in from the block it faces, Sends out to the block it faces, Keeps the network's things in the block it faces, Places blocks in front, Breaks the block in front, Picks up items in front, Drops items in front, Gives a redstone signal at a level, Tunnel: the end things go in, Tunnel: the end things come out, Shows a count on its face, Covers a face with a block's look, Holds things of its own, Opens what the network keeps, A gate: a test, and what happens while it holds, A sensor: a signal while its test holds, Colours its face, A reader: keeps what it reads as a value, A writer: gives a value out, Acts as a player, Closes its face (a plug). |
| Goes on | Blocks that hold parts, or the face of any block: then it sits in the space in front, and one space holds a part for each block around it. Choose one of: Blocks that hold parts, Any block's face. |
| Moves | Items, fluid or energy: what this part takes in, sends out, keeps, counts or tunnels. Choose one of: Items, Fluid, Energy, Redstone (a tunnel), Light (a tunnel), The network itself (a tunnel). |
| Marks | The items its face lets through when it is placed. None: everything. A player changes them in the face's screen. |
| Holds | How much it holds: slots for items (in rows of nine), buckets of fluid, or thousands of energy. From 1 to 54. |
| Keeps of each mark | It takes this many of each of its marks from the network and keeps them. 0: a full stack. From 0 to 1000000. |
| When | The test it watches. Choose one of: A block it watches is full, A block it watches is empty, A block it watches has items, Its block gets redstone, The network keeps at least its level, The light in front is at least its level, A mob is in front. |
| Watches | The block it faces, or every block around the block it is on. Choose one of: The block it faces, Every block around. |
| Then | What happens while the test holds. The block's rules also hear the gate turn on and off. Choose one of: Its block moves nothing, A redstone signal out of its face. |
| Cuts the cable when shut | Off: the face stays shut, as always. On: while the test holds, the cable joins across this face; while it does not, the cable splits into two. A lever or a sensor can flip it. |
| What it does | It takes the first thing the network holds that its filter lets through, and acts with it on the block or the creature in front, as a player would. Choose one of: Uses the item (bone meal, a hoe, a bucket), Places it (a block), Hits a creature with it (a sword wears), Breaks the block with it as a tool. |
| The other way round | On: it acts while the test does not hold. |
| Colour | What leaves through this face goes only to faces of the same colour. Choose one of: None, White, Orange, Magenta, Light blue, Yellow, Lime, Pink, Gray, Light gray, Cyan, Purple, Blue, Brown, Green, Red, Black. |
| Fills first | Which block its face fills first: as the face says, by priority, each in turn, or the nearest. Choose one of: As the face says, By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Speed | How many times over its face's rate it moves, as that many speed upgrades would. From 0 to 8. |
| Acts every | How often it places, breaks, picks up, drops, tunnels or counts. Twenty ticks is a second. From 1 to 1200 ticks. |
| Level | The signal is on while the network holds at least this many. A gate or a sensor testing light counts up to 15. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Also asks for crafting | While the count is under the level, the part also asks the store to craft this many, once at a time. 0: it only gives its signal. From 0 to 6400. |
| Counts | The item it counts in the network. None: everything the network keeps. |
| Looks like | The block this part looks like. A cover covers a face with it; any other part wears it and keeps working. None: a cover takes the look of a block you use it on while sneaking; any other part keeps its own look. You can also sneak and use a block item on a part you placed. |
| Fits on | The blocks it goes on. None listed: every block that holds parts. |
| Reads | What it reads off the block it faces, again and again: its redstone, how many items it holds (of the item it counts, or all), the light or the mobs in front, or the block's answer when asked one of its readings. Choose one of: Redstone, Items, Light, Mobs, The block's answer, Every item, one by one, Fluid (mB), Energy. |
| Reads the fluid | The fluid it counts, written as its game name. Leave it empty to count all fluids in the block it faces. |
| Writes | What it does with its value: gives it as a redstone signal out of its face (0 to 15), or asks the block it faces to do one of its named actions with the value each time it changes. Choose one of: Redstone, Asks the block. |
| Value | For a reader, the name the world remembers what it reads by. For a writer, a name, or a sum of names and numbers like heat * 2 > 50. |
| Values are shared | Whether the values it keeps and reads are the whole world's, or only those of the cable network it sits on (two networks can then use the same name for different things). Choose one of: In the whole world, On this cable network only. |
| Keeps the last | How many of the values it read it keeps, newest first, so a sum can look back: last(heat, 1) is the one before, avg(heat) the average of them all. 1 keeps none extra. From 1 to 64. |
| Amount follows a value | A value's name, or a sum like min(spare, 5). The part then moves that many at a time, from 1 to 9. Leave it empty to keep the speed above. If the value does not exist yet, the speed above is used. |
| Pace follows a value | A value's name, or a sum. The part then acts every that many ticks, from 1 to 1200. Leave it empty to keep the number above. If the value does not exist yet, the number above is used. |
| Priority follows a value | A value's name, or a sum. Its face then has that priority; the higher, the sooner it is served. Leave it empty to keep the face's own priority. |
| Channel follows a value | A value's name, or a sum. Its face then uses that channel, 0 to 15 (the sixteen colours in order), or -1 for none. Leave it empty to keep the face's own channel. |
| Filter follows a list | The name of a list of items, such as the one an 'every item' reader makes. The part then moves only those items. A value holds one number, so a single item name cannot be a value; use a list. Leave it empty to keep the marks. |
| Asks for | The name it asks the block it faces, when it reads or writes by asking: one of that block's "When it is asked to". |
| Opens a screen when used | Using the part with an empty hand opens its slots (and, for a terminal, what the network keeps). Turn it off to keep the part closed. |
| Keeps energy | The part stores energy of its own, like a small battery. It fills from the network and gives to the block it faces. Each part on a block keeps its own. |
| Energy it holds | The most energy the part can store. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Takes in per tick | How much energy the part pulls from the network each tick. 0 means it takes none. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Gives out per tick | How much energy the part gives the block it faces each tick. 0 means it gives none. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Keep its energy in a value | A value name. The part writes its stored energy there, so a rule can read it as that value. Leave empty to keep it private. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: A face part.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-feature

# Feature

Something the world grows as it is made: a patch of flowers, a tree, a boulder, a lake, a vein of a block.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Feature


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Feature](editor-feature.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. The game never shows it. |
| Game name | The feature's name in the game, as a command places it: /place feature. |
| Shape | What the world makes each time it places one. Choose one of: A patch of plants, A tree, A boulder, A lake, A vein under the ground, A round patch in the ground, A spring in a cave wall, A geode, A huge mushroom, A pile, A column, An iceberg, Basalt columns, A patch of ground, A fossil, A dripstone cluster, A desert well, A delta, Blobs in the ground, Kelp, Seagrass, Sea pickles, Bamboo, A mix of your features, A growth on cave walls, Nether plants, Nether vines, A huge fungus, A sculk patch, Magma under the sea, A dungeon, Vines, Glowstone, A basalt pillar, Blue ice, Coral, A chorus plant, An island in the End, One block, A replaced block, A filled layer, Frozen water and snow, An ice spike, An End spike, An End gateway, A great dripstone, A pointed dripstone, A tree with roots, Scattered ore, A ground patch under water, One of two features, A bonus chest, A patch of flowers (the game's flower type), A patch of bushes or plants (the game's random patch), One of several features, evenly, The End's obsidian platform, A starting platform in the void, Deposits from a list. |
| Plants | What the patch is made of. Each is as likely as its weight: two poppies for every dandelion. Each row has: Plant, Weight. |
| Plants a patch | How many times it tries to plant one in a patch. Some land where nothing grows. From 1 to 128. |
| Trunk | The block the trunk is made of: a log of the game's or a block of yours. |
| Leaves | The block the leaves are made of. |
| Tree shape | How its leaves sit on the trunk, as the game's own trees. Choose one of: Round, as an oak, Pointed, as a spruce, Tall with branches, as a big oak, A low bush. |
| Trunk height | How tall the trunk grows, before a few blocks more by chance. From 1 to 32 blocks. |
| Made of | The block it is made of. |
| Found in | The ground the vein replaces. Choose one of: Stone, Deepslate, Netherrack, End stone. |
| Vein size | About how many blocks a vein holds. From 1 to 64. |
| Lowest | The lowest and highest height a vein is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| Highest | The lowest and highest height a vein is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| How many per chunk | How many veins it tries to place in each chunk. From 1 to 64. |
| Filled with | What the lake holds, or what the spring pours. Choose one of: Water, Lava. |
| Rim | The block around the lake where it meets the ground. |
| Across | How far the patch reaches from its middle. From 1 to 8 blocks. |
| Outer shell | The block of its outside, as the game's smooth basalt. |
| Middle shell | The block between, as the game's calcite. |
| Inside | The block that lines its hollow, as the game's amethyst. |
| Crystals | What grows on the inside. Left empty, nothing does. |
| Cap shape | The red mushroom's dome or the brown one's flat cap. Choose one of: Dome, Flat. |
| Cap | The block its cap is made of. |
| Stem | The block its stem is made of. |
| Cap width | How far the cap reaches from the stem. From 1 to 6 blocks. |
| Made of | The block the pile is made of, as hay bales in a village. |
| Made of | The block stacked up into a column, as sugar cane grows. |
| Up to | How tall it is, at most. From 1 to 32 blocks. |
| Made of | The block the iceberg is made of. It floats at the sea's level in an ocean. |
| Spread | How far its columns spread, as the Nether's basalt deltas. From 0 to 3 blocks. |
| Up to | How tall its columns of basalt rise at most. From 1 to 10 blocks. |
| Ground | The block laid over the ground, as moss in a lush cave. |
| Grows on it | The plant on most of the ground. Left empty, the ground is bare. |
| Across | How far the ground reaches from its middle. From 1 to 12 blocks. |
| Tree | One of your tree features. The roots grow round it and under it. |
| Roots | The block the roots are made of, as rooted dirt under an azalea. |
| Either | One of your features. It is placed half the time. |
| Or | Another of your features, placed the other half. A feature here grows only through this one, not on its own. |
| Bones | Which of the game's own fossils it leaves underground. Choose one of: Spines, Skulls, Spines and skulls. |
| Across | How far its stalactites and stalagmites reach in a cave. From 2 to 8 blocks. |
| Rim | The block around each pool, as magma round the Nether's lava deltas. |
| Across | How far its pools spread at most. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| In | The block the blobs replace where they find it. |
| Made of | The block each blob is made of, as blackstone in netherrack. |
| Across | How far a blob reaches from its middle. From 1 to 12 blocks. |
| Tall | How much of it grows two blocks tall. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| How many | How many sea pickles it tries to place. From 1 to 64. |
| On podzol | How often the ground under it turns to podzol, as in a bamboo jungle. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Picks one of | Your other features, one of them at each place, each as likely as its weight, as a forest mixes its trees. A feature here grows only through the mix, not on its own. Each row has: Feature, Weight. |
| Growth | What grows over the stone of caves. Choose one of: Glow lichen, on walls and ceilings, Sculk veins, on every side. |
| Plants | What spreads over the ground, each as likely as its weight. It grows only on nylium, as in a crimson forest. Each row has: Plant, Weight. |
| Grows | Which way the vines grow, as the Nether's own. Choose one of: Up from the ground, twisting, Down from the ceiling, weeping. |
| Grows on | The ground it grows from, as crimson nylium. |
| Stem | The block its stem is made of, as a crimson stem. |
| Cap | The block its cap is made of, as nether wart. |
| Lights | The block dotted through its cap, as shroomlight. Left empty, the cap is whole. |
| Spread | How far the sculk spreads from its middle. From 1 to 32. |
| With a catalyst | How often a sculk catalyst stands in the middle of it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Coral shape | Which of the warm ocean's corals grows, of the game's coral colours. Choose one of: A tree of branches, A claw, A mushroom. |
| List | The list of entries the player edits that says each deposit: its block, size, how rare and how deep. |
| Block field | The list's field that holds each deposit's block. |
| Size field | The list's field that holds each deposit's size, in blocks. |
| How often | How many the world places in each chunk, a square of sixteen blocks. Choose one of: Everywhere, eight a chunk, Often, three a chunk, Sometimes, one a chunk, Rarely, one in eight chunks, Very rarely, one in thirty two chunks, In clumps, thick in some places and thin in others, Just so many. |
| In each chunk | How many it places in a chunk where it places any. From 1 to 256. |
| Once in | It places any in one chunk of this many; one is every chunk. From 1 to 1000 chunks. |
| Where | At what height it is placed. Choose one of: Where it belongs: on the ground, or under it, On the ground, Between two heights, Most in the middle of two heights, On the top of the world, water too, On the ground, under the sea too, On cave floors, On cave ceilings. |
| Lowest | The lowest height it is placed at. The world's bottom is minus sixty four. From -64 to 320. |
| Highest | The highest height it is placed at. The sea is at sixty three. From -64 to 320. |
| In biomes | Where it grows: the game's biomes, a group of them such as every overworld biome, or biomes of yours. |

## What it becomes in the game

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-flyingMount

# Flying mount

A mount that flies with its rider, beating its wings on each jump.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Flying mount


## What you can set

### Has a spawn egg

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Egg colour | The colour of the egg itself. |
| Spot colour | The colour of the spots on the egg. |

### Can be tamed

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tamed by | What makes it a player's: an item given to it, riding it until it calms, or only a rule's words. Choose one of: Giving it an item, Riding it until it calms, Only a rule. |
| Tamed with | The item a player gives it, one each try. |
| Chance a try | How likely each item given, or each time it is ridden, tames it. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| Sits when told | Its owner's use makes it sit and stay, and stand again. |
| Follows owner | It keeps near its owner when it is not sitting. |
| Follows from | How far its owner may go before it comes after them. From 2 to 32 blocks. |
| Catches up | Left far behind, it appears beside its owner, as a tame wolf does. |
| Strikes back at its owner | Off, a tamed one never targets or attacks its owner or the owner's team, however it was hurt, as a wolf does not. |
| Defends owner | It attacks what hurts its owner and what its owner attacks. |
| Healed with | Foods its owner gives it to heal it. |

### Can be ridden

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Flies ridden | How it flies with a rider: the jump key rises, the sprint key (Ctrl) descends, forward goes where the rider looks, A and D turn it; hovering and flapping hold their height when no key is held, gliding sinks slowly. Choose one of: Does not fly, Glides, Hovers, Flaps, Its own way. |
| Climbs at | How fast it rises while its rider holds jump. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| Sinks at | How fast it sinks in the air with nothing held. 0: it hovers. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| Dives at | How fast it goes down while its rider holds the descend key. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| In water | Floating keeps its rider's head up; swimming dives and rises where the rider looks, and the rider breathes. Choose one of: Floats, Swims under. |
| Needs a saddle | It can be ridden only once a saddle is put on it. |
| Saddle | The item used on it as its saddle. |
| Ridden by | Only its owner once it is tamed, or anyone. Choose one of: Its owner, Anyone. |
| Speed ridden | How fast it goes with a rider, times its own speed. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| Flying speed | How fast it flies with a rider, times its own flying speed. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| Jumps | How high it jumps on a full charge of the jump bar. From 0 to 8 blocks. |
| Seat height | How far above or below its back the rider sits; the back is found from the shape of its body. From -4 to 8 blocks. |
| A and D | Turning turns the creature and the rider's view with it, as a horse does; strafing moves it sideways and keeps it facing. Choose one of: Turn it, Strafe, Nothing. |
| Mouse look | Steering, the creature faces where the rider looks, as a vanilla horse does; looking only, the view turns on its own and the creature faces where A and D turned it. Choose one of: Steers it, Looks only. |
| W and S | Forward and back move it along its body; set to nothing, only the other keys move it. Choose one of: Move it, Nothing. |
| Jump key | Auto rises a flier or a swimmer and makes the others jump with the jump bar; or choose to rise, to jump, or nothing. Choose one of: Auto, Rise, Jump, Nothing. |
| Free up and down | A flier or a swimmer rises while the jump key is held, holds its height when nothing is held, and descends on the sprint key. Off, it goes up and down only where the rider looks. |
| Descend key | The key held to take a flier or a swimmer down (changed in the game's Controls); the sneak key always gets the rider off. Choose one of: Sprint key (Ctrl), Swap-hands key (F), None. |
| Rider on a tilt | Following, the rider leans with the seat's part of the body as it tilts (a dragon pitched in flight); upright, he stays level whatever the body does. First person stays level either way. Choose one of: Follows the seat, Stays upright. |
| Rider can hit it | A left click while riding never lands on the creature itself unless this is on. |
| Falls hurt | Off, neither the rider nor the creature takes fall damage while riding, and the rider none from the fall off its back. |
| Seat forward | How far forward of the middle of its back the rider sits; below zero is behind. From -4 to 4 blocks. |
| Turn speed | How fast A and D turn it, and the rider's view with it, in degrees a second. From 10 to 360 degrees a second. |
| Seats | How many ride it at once; the first steers. From 1 to 4. |

### Carries gear

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Bags | Rows of nine slots its owner opens by sneaking and using it; none for no bags. From 0 to 6. |
| Armour it wears | Items put on it as armour, each with what it gives and the look it wears with it. Each row has: Item, Armour, Toughness, Look. |

Every mob also has the settings on the [Mob](editor-creature.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Has a spawn egg, Can be tamed, Can be ridden, Carries gear.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Damage type](editor-damageType.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Mob](thing-creature.md), [Pet](thing-pet.md), [Mount](thing-mount.md), [Sea mount](thing-seaMount.md), [Boss](thing-boss.md).
