# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-formedMachine

# Formed machine

A machine built of many blocks: it works only while the blocks around it stand as its pattern, drawn layer by layer on its Pattern tab, says. A frame of iron to start.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Formed machine


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its buffer. Set it to nothing for a cable, which holds nothing of its own. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. A run of cable carries as much as its narrowest one, not the sum of them. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| No limit | On: energy cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### What it makes

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots it takes | The first slots of its inventory, the ones it takes from. They sit left of the arrow in its screen. From 1 to 54. |
| Slots it puts into | The slots after the ones it takes from. They sit right of the arrow. From 0 to 54. |
| When powered | What a redstone signal reaching the block does to it. Choose one of: No change, It stops, It only runs then. |
| When it is full | What it does when the slots it puts into are full. Choose one of: It waits, It throws it away. |
| Recipe type name | A name of your own for the kind of recipes this machine runs, shown as their page in the recipe viewer: Distilling, Infusing. |
| Runs the recipes of | Another machine whose recipes this one runs too, so many machines share one recipe type. Empty: its own. |
| Counts as working | While working: only while a recipe is under way, an idle machine rests. Always: it counts as working all the time. Choose one of: While working, Always. |

### Formed from a pattern

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Pattern | A ring: the eight blocks around it on its own level. Below: the nine under it. A cube: all twenty-six around it. Your own: the places you list, turned the way it faces. Any size: a box or a group of touching blocks it finds by looking, its size between a smallest and a largest. Choose one of: a ring around it, a floor under it, a cube around it, places of your own, drawn, any size, found by looking. |
| Build shape | A box: walls on all six sides round an inside. An open box: walls and a floor, no roof. Touching: every block of the build that touches another, any shape; it grows as blocks are added. Choose one of: a box, an open box, blocks that touch. |
| Smallest across | The fewest blocks across (both ways), the walls counted. From 3 to 64. |
| Largest across | The most blocks across (both ways), the walls counted. From 3 to 64. |
| Lowest | The fewest blocks high, the floor (and roof) counted. From 2 to 64 blocks. |
| Tallest | The most blocks high, the floor (and roof) counted. From 2 to 64 blocks. |
| Most blocks | The most blocks that may touch in one build; more and it does not form. From 1 to 4096. |
| Blocks of the build | Each kind of block the build is made of: where it may stand, at least and at most how many, and what one is worth. The inside may always be empty. Each row has: Block, Where, At least, At most, Worth. |
| Inside scales | What the room inside the formed build multiplies: its capacities, its rates, both, or nothing. A tank 3 inside holds three times its capacity. Choose one of: nothing, its capacities, its rates, capacities and rates. |
| Made of | The block every place of the pattern must hold. |
| Drawn pattern | The pattern drawn on the Pattern tab, layer by layer: each cell a test a block must pass (a block, a tag, any of several, a fluid, air, anything), and one cell the machine itself. |
| Stands | As it faces: the pattern turns with the machine's front. Any way round: it forms whichever of the four ways it was built. Choose one of: as it faces, any way. |
| Mirrored too | Its mirror copy forms as well, left and right swapped. |
| Several sizes | A band of the drawing that may repeat, so a taller or a longer build forms as well. It forms the largest size that stands. Choose one of: one size, taller, longer. |
| Band from | The first layer (or row, from the front) of the band that repeats, counted from 1. From 1 to 48. |
| Band to | The last layer (or row) of the band that repeats. From 1 to 48. |
| At least | The fewest times the band stands. From 1 to 48. |
| At most | The most times the band stands; at most 16 sizes in all. From 1 to 48. |
| How many of a block | Of the blocks standing in the pattern, at least and at most so many of one: at least 1 item port, at most 2 energy ports. Each row has: Block, At least, At most. |
| Worth of a block | Several kinds of block may stand in one place, each worth so much: a basic cell 1, an elite cell 8. Formed, the machine adds up the worth of the blocks standing in its pattern. Each row has: Block, Worth. |
| Worth scales | What the formed machine's worth multiplies: its capacities, its rates, both, or nothing (its rules still read it). Choose one of: nothing, its capacities, its rates, capacities and rates. |
| Looks | By itself: every second. With an item: when a player uses the item on it, as a hammer or a wrench. By a rule: when a rule says so. Once formed it looks every second, so a block taken away breaks it. Choose one of: by itself, with an item, by a rule. |
| Item | The item (or tag) a player uses on it to make it look and form. |
| Screen only when formed | Before it is formed, using it only says what is missing; its screen opens once it is formed. |
| Ghost of what is missing | While a player is near and it is not formed, a small glowing copy of each missing block stands where it goes. |
| Places | Each place from the block, as a player standing at its front sees it, and the block it must hold. Each row has: Right, Up, Behind, Block. |
| Works only when formed | A machine that makes nothing until its pattern is complete, as a machine built of many blocks does. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Energy, Connections, What it makes, Formed from a pattern.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-formSet

# Forms for every material

Makes a dust, a plate, a gear or any other form for every metal and gem the game has when it starts, other mods too. One grey picture per form is tinted in each material's colour.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Forms for every material


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Forms for every material](editor-formSet.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for this set, only for you. |
| Forms | Each row is one thing made for every material, like a dust or a plate. Each row has: Form, Item name in the game, Tag, Picture. |
| Materials found by | A material is found for every item that fits one of these. A star stands for any text. Each row has: Item name. |
| Recipes | Recipes made for every material found when the game starts. Write one once with (material) and form names like (ingot), (nugget) or (dust); a recipe is skipped for a material when an item it needs is missing. Each row has: Recipe type, Recipe (JSON), Only if this mod is loaded. |
| Only if not made yet | On: a form is not made when an item with the same name already exists, so you never get two copper dusts. Mods that load after yours are not seen. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-gameChange

# Game thing changed

One of the game's own blocks, items or mobs given new values, such as a block's hardness, an item's stack size or a mob's health, a structure the game makes no more, or a limit the game sets, such as the anvil's most cost.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Game thing changed


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Game thing changed](editor-gameChange.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What it is called here. |
| Game name | Its name inside the mod, in small letters. |
| Changes | What kind of the game's things this changes: a block, an item, a mob, structures, or limits the game sets. Choose one of: A block, An item, A mob, Structures, Limits. |
| Item | The item to change, the game's, another mod's or yours: how many stack, and how many uses it lasts. |
| Stacks to | How many fit in one stack, up to 99, such as ender pearls 64; 0 keeps the game's. Items that wear out stack to 1. From 0 to 99. |
| Uses | How many uses it lasts before it breaks; 0 keeps the game's. An item given uses stacks to 1. From 0 to 100000. |
| Food it gives | How much hunger it fills when eaten, up to 20. 0 leaves the game's; above 0 makes it food. From 0 to 20. |
| Its limits | Each limit of the game to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to; in one dimension or every one; or taken from a setting the player changes. Each row has: Value, How, Number, Only in, Player's setting. |
| Block | The block to change, the game's, another mod's or yours. |
| Its values | Each value of the block to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to. Each row has: Value, How, Number. |
| Mob | The mob to change, the game's, another mod's or yours. Mobs already in a world change as they load. |
| Its values | Each value of the mob to change, and how: made a number, multiplied, or added to. Each row has: Value, How, Number. |
| Never made | Structures the game no longer makes, such as mineshafts; one of yours can take their place. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-gene

# Gene

A trait any thing can carry and pass to its young: a number such as Growth, or one of a few choices such as Coat colour.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Gene


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Gene](editor-gene.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads in a tooltip and in the chat. |
| Saved as | The name the gene is kept under on each thing, and what rules call it. |
| Holds | A number in a range, such as Growth from 1 to 10, or one of a few choices, such as Black, Orange or White. Choose one of: A number, One of a few choices. |
| Lowest | The smallest the number can be. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Highest | The biggest the number can be. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Starts at | What a thing has when its species does not say. From -1000000 to 1000000. |
| Choices | Each value the gene can take, which one wins when a thing has two, and how often it is found in the wild. Each row has: Value, Wins, In the wild, Block. |
| A child takes it | How a child gets this gene from its two parents. Choose one of: One copy from each parent, The parents' average, From one parent or the other, The higher of the two, The lower of the two. |
| Chance to change | Out of every hundred children, how many have this gene changed: a number moves by a step, a choice turns into another. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Shapes | What this number changes in the thing that carries it: how fast a plant grows, how much a block drops, how tall a tree grows, or a mob's size, speed or health. Choose one of: Nothing, How fast it grows, How much it drops, How tall a tree grows, Its size, Its speed, Its health, How wide its trunk grows, How big its crown grows. |
| Each point above the start | How much more, out of a hundred, each point above the gene's start gives, and less for each point below. At 10, a plant with Growth 5 and a start of 2 grows 30 in a hundred faster. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Decides in a tree | What this choice decides in a tree grown from a sapling that carries it: the fruit it bears, its logs, its leaves, or the shape of its crown (name the choices round, pointed, wide or bush). Choose one of: Nothing, The fruit it bears, Its logs, Its leaves, The shape of its crown. |
| Shown | When the tooltip and the chat say it. Choose one of: Always, Once read by an analyser, Never. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-generator

# Generator

Burns something and makes energy, on a recipe you write.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Generator


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its buffer. Set it to nothing for a cable, which holds nothing of its own. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. A run of cable carries as much as its narrowest one, not the sum of them. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| No limit | On: energy cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### What it makes

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots it takes | The first slots of its inventory, the ones it takes from. They sit left of the arrow in its screen. From 1 to 54. |
| Slots it puts into | The slots after the ones it takes from. They sit right of the arrow. From 0 to 54. |
| When powered | What a redstone signal reaching the block does to it. Choose one of: No change, It stops, It only runs then. |
| When it is full | What it does when the slots it puts into are full. Choose one of: It waits, It throws it away. |
| Recipe type name | A name of your own for the kind of recipes this machine runs, shown as their page in the recipe viewer: Distilling, Infusing. |
| Runs the recipes of | Another machine whose recipes this one runs too, so many machines share one recipe type. Empty: its own. |
| Counts as working | While working: only while a recipe is under way, an idle machine rests. Always: it counts as working all the time. Choose one of: While working, Always. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Energy, Connections, What it makes.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-partsCreature

# Golem-style creature

A creature built of parts and materials, as a golem is: used on a block it becomes the creature, its health, speed, armor, jobs and look its parts'.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Golem-style creature


## What you can set

### Made of parts

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| First part | A part it is made of, drawn first, under the others. |
| Second part | A part it is made of, drawn over the first. |
| Third part | A part it is made of, drawn over the second. |
| Fourth part | A part it is made of, drawn over the rest; leave it empty for a tool of three. |
| Its own changes | Changes to the stats after its parts', such as a hammer that mines three across at half speed. Each row has: Stat, How, Amount, Only on blocks. |
| Becomes a creature | Used on a block, it is placed as this creature, built of its parts: their materials give its health, speed, armor and damage, their jobs its work, their pieces its look. Its owner crouching with an empty hand takes it apart into this item again; when it dies it drops its parts. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Made of parts.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-hat

# Hat

Something worn on the head, drawn on the wearer from its own picture.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Hat


## What you can set

### Worn

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Worn on | Which slot it goes in: one of the four armor slots, or a slot of the shared slot mod a player installs beside it, on NeoForge and on Fabric 1.21.1. Without that mod a ring or a belt works from the off hand. Choose one of: Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Ring, Necklace, Belt, Back, Hands, Another slot. |
| Slot name | The name the slot mod gives that slot, such as charm or head/face. |
| Material | Pieces with the same material share its numbers and its worn picture, like iron or diamond. Leave it empty and the piece is its own material. |
| Armor points | The armor points it gives, each half a shirt over the health bar: an iron chestplate gives 6, iron boots 2. From 0 to 30. |
| Body color | The color it is drawn in on its wearer. |
| On the body | The picture it is drawn in on its wearer, on the game's layout of worn armor, painted as any picture is; without one it is drawn in its color. |
| Toughness | How much of a heavy hit the armor still stops: diamond 2, netherite 3. From 0 to 20. |
| Stands firm | How much less its wearer is pushed back by a hit, from nought to one: netherite 0.1 a piece. From 0 to 1. |
| Worn shape | A model of yours drawn on whoever wears it, a player or a mob: a hat, wings, a jetpack, a full suit. Each group named for a body part (Head, Body, Right arm, Left arm, Right leg, Left leg) moves with that part; Make one starts it on the wearer's body. |
| Follows | The body part a group of the shape follows when its name is not a body part's. Choose one of: The part its slot is on, Head, Body, Right arm, Left arm, Right leg, Left leg. |
| Its animations | Animations of the worn shape, each playing while its wearer does something or while a value of the piece is on: wings that flap while flying, a flame while the engine is on. Several play at once. Each row has: Animation, While, Value. |
| Parts shown only | A group of the worn shape drawn only while something holds: a module's part while its value is on, a visor while crouching. Groups not named here are always drawn. Each row has: Group, While, Value. |
| Or a carved shape | A block you carved on its Carve tab, worn on the body part in place of the flat armor, in the real pictures of its looks. A worn shape above wins. |
| Width on the body | How many pixels across the carved block or copied design is drawn on the wearer. A head is 8; 10 sits over it like a helmet. From 1 to 48. |
| Takes a carved design | Sneak and use this on a carved block to copy its design onto the item, then wear it to show the design on the body part. Sneak and use in the air to clear it. The block stays. Set the size above. |
| Tint | A color the worn shape's picture is multiplied by; white keeps it as painted. |
| Glows | The worn shape is drawn at full light, bright in the dark. |
| See-through | How much you see through the worn shape, from 0 (solid) to 90. From 0 to 90. |
| Hides the flat armor | The game's flat armor picture is not drawn, only the worn shape. |
| Only for its look over | While it is worn, the armor in this slot keeps protecting but is not drawn, and this piece is drawn in its place: a cosmetic slot. Choose one of: Nothing, The helmet, The chestplate, The leggings, The boots. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Worn.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-hudDraw

# HUD drawing in code

Your own code that draws on the HUD every frame, in a box you place on the screen.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > HUD drawing in code


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [HUD drawing in code](editor-hudDraw.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it in the project. |
| Drawing class | Your class's full name. It implements the mod's HudDraws.Drawing: handed a canvas and its box, it draws with the canvas's fill, text and item, the same on every game version. |
| Placed | The edge or the middle of the screen its box keeps to. Choose one of: Top left, Top center, Top right, Left, Center, Right, Bottom left, Bottom center, Bottom right. |
| Across | How far its box is set in from that edge across, in the GUI's pixels; from the middle, how far to the right. From -4000 to 4000. |
| Down | How far its box is set in from that edge up or down, in the GUI's pixels; from the middle, how far down. From -4000 to 4000. |
| Layer | Over the game's HUD, above the hotbar, the chat and the rest; or under it, over the world. Choose one of: Over the HUD, Under the HUD. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-hud

# HUD number bar

One number of the player shown over the game as a bar or words, like saturation above the hunger bar.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > HUD number bar


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [HUD number bar](editor-hud.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| Shows | What it draws: one of the player's own numbers, a value of the player, or the block the player looks at with its readings, in a panel at the top center. Choose one of: Saturation, Hunger, Health, Air, Armor, Armor toughness, Absorption hearts, Held item's durability, Level, A value of the player, An area value where the player stands, What the player looks at. |
| Value | The value of the player it draws, against the value's most. |
| Area value | The area value it draws, where the player stands, against the value's most. |
| Placed | Where it is drawn: over the game's own icons on the hunger, health, armor or air bar; a row of its own just above the drumsticks or the hearts (higher while air bubbles or armor show there, and stacked with the others there); beside a bar, outside the hotbar; or at the top. Choose one of: On the hunger bar, On the health bar, On the armor bar, On the air bar, Above the hunger bar, Above the health bar, Beside the hunger bar, Beside the health bar, Top left, Top center, Top right. |
| Drawn as | A bar that fills, the number itself, ten icons as the game's own bars (two points an icon, half an icon for one), or a bar with its number. Choose one of: A bar, A number, Ten icons, A bar with its number, A veil over the screen, A veil over the sky. |
| Veil strength | How strong the tint is when the number is at its most. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| Number says | How the number reads: the number itself, the number out of its most (7/20), or a share (35%). Choose one of: The number, Out of its most, A share. |
| Shown | When it is drawn: always, while low or high, for a few seconds after it changes, while an item is held, while sneaking, or under water. Choose one of: Always, While below a share, While above a share, For a while after it changes, While holding an item, While sneaking, While under water. |
| Share | The share of its most it is compared with: shown while below it, or while above it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| For | How long it stays after the number changes. From 1 to 60 seconds. |
| Holding | The item, or a tag of items, that shows it while held in either hand. |
| Color | The color it is drawn in. |
| Wrap into layers | A value bigger than one row starts again in the next color, as many times as it needs. |
| One row holds | How much of the value fills one row. Ten icons hold 20, two for each icon. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Layer colors | The colors of the second row, the third and on, as color codes with spaces between. After the last one they start again. |
| Layers drawn | Over the first row, or each one above the row before. Choose one of: Over the first row, Each above the last. |
| Hide empty icons | Icons not reached are not drawn, instead of a faint dark square. |
| Recolor the game's own row | The mod draws the game's hearts or armor itself. After one full row, every further row's worth turns the row to the next color, so it never grows taller. Off keeps the game's own rows. |
| Row colors | The colors of the second row's worth, the third and on, as color codes with spaces between. After the last one they start again. |
| Icon | An item, or a picture of your own, drawn small beside it. None when empty. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Value](editor-value.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md).

# Item

Something held in the hand or kept in a chest.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Item


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Item](editor-item.md) editor lists every setting.

| --- | --- |

| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |

| Tooltip lines | Extra lines under its Name when a player points at it, such as "Tastes like thunder.". The Name itself is set above. Each row has: Words, Color. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-itemFilter

# Item filter

A filter as an item: marked in the filter of a pipe's face, that face lets through what its rules say, items and tags, mods, wear and enchantment.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Item filter


## What you can set

### A filter

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Items and tags | The items it names, or every item of a tag. Names nothing and no mods: every item. |
| Mods | Every item of these mods, by the mod's game name (minecraft for the game's own). |
| Wear | Which items pass by their wear: any, unworn (and things that never wear), worn, or a quarter of their uses or less left. Choose one of: Any, Unworn, Worn, Nearly broken. |
| Enchanted | Whether items must be enchanted, must not be, or either. Choose one of: Either, Only enchanted, Only plain. |
| Genes | Genes an item must show to pass, every line at once, such as species Goldbloom or Growth at least 5. An item with no genes does not pass. Each row has: Gene, Is, Value. |
| Has data | Data the item must carry beyond what it comes with, every one: custom name, enchantments, potion contents, damage. Empty asks nothing. |
| Made of | Stock types the item must hold some of, any one: Fire, Earth, or a kind for all its types. Empty asks nothing. |
| Marks match data too | For a filter whose player marks items in the game: a marked sword only lets through swords with the same enchantments and name. Off, any sword matches. |
| Way round | Lets only what it names through, or everything but it. Choose one of: Only these, All but these. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: A filter.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-itemPipe

# Item pipe

Carries items between chests and machines. It holds nothing of its own.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Item pipe


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Connections.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-letter

# Letter

An item that holds a few things and is mailed to a player.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Letter


## What you can set

### Holds items

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds. From 1 to 54. |
| Slots mark items | The slots keep a picture of an item instead of the item. A player clicks an item on a slot to mark it, and clicks with an empty hand to clear it, so nothing is ever taken from them. This is how a filter you can edit in the game works. |
| Picks up | Carried anywhere in the inventory, it takes what the player walks over before the player's own slots do. |
| Picks up only | The items it picks up, each an item or a #tag. Empty, it picks up anything that fits in it. |
| Only what it holds | It only picks up the kinds already in its slots. Put one in to teach it. |
| Most in a slot | How many of one item a slot holds. 64 is the game's own; set it higher for a slot that holds thousands. From 1 to 2147483647. |
| Keeps at least | When something is taken out, this many stay in the slot. 0 lets the slot empty. From 0 to 99999. |
| Uses what it holds | Used, it acts as the thing chosen in it: the last one you clicked in its slots. Crouching, it opens them. |
| Holds other bags | Other things that hold items can go inside it, so you can carry a bag of bags. Off, it refuses them, as a shulker box does. |
| Packs nine into one | While you carry it, nine of a thing in your slots turn into what the crafting grid makes of nine (nine iron ingots become an iron block). |
| Put down as | Used while crouching on the ground, it becomes this block, holding what it held. Break it, or crouch and use it with an empty hand, and it is the same item again, with its name and colour. |
| Most slots with pockets | The most slots it can have once pockets are put in it. Its screen has room for all of them; the ones not opened yet are dark. 0 means it takes no pockets. From 0 to 54. |
| Opens from the inventory | While it is worn, a button on the player's own inventory screen opens it. It drops with its contents when the player dies. |
| Screen | Its screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws the slots in rows. |

### Letter

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Costs to send | One of this is taken from you each time a letter is sent, like a stamp. Empty means sending is free. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Holds items, Letter.

| Bridge name | Give two links the same name and they join the stores beside them at any distance and in any dimension, as a pair. Empty: only links in range. |

| Opens | What using the link does: nothing (the index answers in chat), or opens the store screen with a search box over all the stores it joins. Choose one of: The chat, The store screen. |

# Loot table

A weighted list of what can come out, rolled by a quest, a crate, a mob's or a block's drop, or a rule. It is written as the game's own, so a chest the game fills can name it too.

| Game name | The table's name in the game, as a chest, a command or another mod names it. |
| Kind of table | What the table is for. It decides which conditions you can pick: a tool is only held when a block is broken. Choose one of: Chest, Block drops, Creature drops, Fishing, Gift, Digging up. |
| At least | How many times the list is drawn from each time the table is rolled: one number, or a range to pick from. From 0 to 64. |
| At most | How many times the list is drawn from each time the table is rolled: one number, or a range to pick from. From 0 to 64. |
| Entries | What can come out of one roll, each as likely as its weight against the others. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-machine

# Machine

A block with an inventory, a tank or power.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Machine


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its buffer. Set it to nothing for a cable, which holds nothing of its own. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. A run of cable carries as much as its narrowest one, not the sum of them. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| No limit | On: energy cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### What it makes

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots it takes | The first slots of its inventory, the ones it takes from. They sit left of the arrow in its screen. From 1 to 54. |
| Slots it puts into | The slots after the ones it takes from. They sit right of the arrow. From 0 to 54. |
| When powered | What a redstone signal reaching the block does to it. Choose one of: No change, It stops, It only runs then. |
| When it is full | What it does when the slots it puts into are full. Choose one of: It waits, It throws it away. |
| Recipe type name | A name of your own for the kind of recipes this machine runs, shown as their page in the recipe viewer: Distilling, Infusing. |
| Runs the recipes of | Another machine whose recipes this one runs too, so many machines share one recipe type. Empty: its own. |
| Counts as working | While working: only while a recipe is under way, an idle machine rests. Always: it counts as working all the time. Choose one of: While working, Always. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Energy, Connections, What it makes.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-machineCasing

# Machine casing

A part of a machine built of many blocks: pipes and cables reach the machine through it, using it opens the machine's screen, and while the machine stands its state "formed" is on, so it may look different then (give that look a picture, or an empty one to hide it under the machine's own model).

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Machine casing


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Block](editor-block.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players read in the game, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. You can change it any time. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Texture | The picture on every face of the block. |
| Time to break | How hard the block is; stone is 1.5, dirt 0.5. Higher is slower; obsidian is 50. The overview shows the seconds by hand. From 0 to 3600. |
| Form | The game's own shapes, each drawn from this block's picture and working as the game's own does: stairs you walk up, a slab that doubles, a fence and a wall that join their neighbours, a door and a trapdoor that open, a button and a pressure plate that give a redstone signal, a pane, a carpet, leaves that fall away when no log is near, a pillar that lies the way it is placed, and a rail the game's carts ride. Choose one of: A full block, Stairs, A slab, A wall, A fence, A fence gate, A door, A trapdoor, A pressure plate, A button, A pane, as glass and bars, A carpet, Leaves, A pillar, as a log, A rail, A slope, A slope, outer corner, A slope, inner corner, A ridge, as a roof top, A quarter round, as an arch, A round pillar, A window frame. |
| Wears the block used on it | Off, the shape shows this block's own picture. On, a player can use any full block on it, from this mod, the game or another mod, and the shape then shows that block's pictures instead, grass and leaves colours included. Using nothing while sneaking gives the block back, and breaking the shape gives it back too. The slope, corners, ridge, quarter round, round pillar and window frame turn to face you and hang upside down when placed on a ceiling or on the top half of a side, like stairs. |
| Turns carts | Whether a cart rolling onto it goes off to one side instead of straight on: never, while redstone powers it, or by the cart, when the cart matches the list below. Lay track on three sides of it, like a T. Choose one of: Never, While powered, By the cart. |
| Turns to | The side a turned cart goes off to, as the cart sees it coming in: its left or its right. Choose one of: Left, Right. |
| Which carts turn | The carts that turn, any one of these: a kind of cart (a chest minecart), an item it carries (coal), a tag of items (all ores), or the fluid in its tank (water), each by its game name. Empty: every cart turns. |
| Gives a signal | A redstone signal while a cart is on it: for any cart, only a full cart, only an empty cart, or stronger the fuller the cart is. Full counts its chest, its tank and its battery together. Choose one of: Never, For any cart, For a full cart, For an empty cart, By how full. |
| Picture of its ends | The picture on its two ends, as a log shows its rings; its sides wear the block's own picture. With none, the ends wear that too. |
| Picture of the top half | The door's upper half; its lower half and the item in the hand wear the block's own picture. With none, both halves wear that. |
| Works like | Wood: a door or trapdoor opens by hand, a button stays pressed longer and an arrow presses it, a pressure plate feels anything on it, a fence joins the game's wooden fences. Metal or stone: only redstone opens a door or trapdoor, and only a player or a mob presses a plate. Choose one of: Wood, Metal or stone. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Part of a formed machine.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-machineRecipe

# Machine recipe

What one machine of yours turns into something else, and what it costs.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Machine recipe


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Machine recipe](editor-machineRecipe.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this recipe. Leave it empty and the card names itself from what goes in and what comes out. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this recipe. |
| Machine | The block that runs it. Recipes name their machine, so adding one changes no block. |
| What goes in | The thing the machine takes from the slots it takes from. |
| How many | How many of it one operation uses. From 1 to 64. |
| What comes out | Leave this empty for a generator: it burns what goes in to nothing. |
| How many | How many come out of one operation. From 0 to 64. |
| Second thing in | A second thing that goes in with the first, as two metals make an alloy. Leave it empty for a machine that takes one thing. |
| How many of the second | How many of the second thing one operation uses. From 1 to 64. |
| Energy | Whether the machine spends energy on this or makes it. Choose one of: Uses energy, Makes energy. |
| How much energy | Over the whole operation, not each tick. It is spread evenly across the seconds below. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Seconds | How long one operation takes. The game reads it while it runs, so it can come from somewhere else. From 1 to 3600 seconds. |
| More in and out | Any number of things more that go in or come out, beside the ones above: items, fluids or stocks of your own, each with how much and, coming out, how often. Each row has: Goes, What, Item, Fluid, Stock, Type, How much, How often, Tank. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Custom kind](editor-matter.md), [Gene](editor-gene.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-material

# Material

What parts are cut from, any item the game's iron ingot among them: its color, and the numbers and abilities it gives a part.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Material


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Material](editor-material.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads on a part cut from it. |
| Saved as | The name it is saved as in a part's data, which a piece of your own code reads. |
| Cut from | The item a player puts in the stonecutter to cut parts of this material, or a tag of them. |
| Color | The color a part cut from it wears, and the tool's part with it. |
| Uses | What a head of it lasts, as the game's pickaxe of it does: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mining speed | How fast a head of it mines: iron 6, gold 12. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Own stats | Stats of your own beside uses, speed and damage, such as Luck or Heat: a part gives its share of them to the tool, and a rule reads the tool's. Each row has: Stat, Amount. |
| Traits | Modifiers every tool with a part of this material carries, as if installed: their stat changes and their own rules. Two parts of it give the trait twice the level. Each row has: Modifier, Level a part. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Effect](editor-effect.md), [Item](editor-item.md).
