# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-poweredArmour

# Powered armour

A piece of armour that runs on energy: each hit its wearer takes spends some, and empty it guards nothing until it is charged.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Powered armour


## What you can set

### Worn

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Worn on | Which slot it goes in: one of the four armor slots, or a slot of the shared slot mod a player installs beside it, on NeoForge and on Fabric 1.21.1. Without that mod a ring or a belt works from the off hand. Choose one of: Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Ring, Necklace, Belt, Back, Hands, Another slot. |
| Slot name | The name the slot mod gives that slot, such as charm or head/face. |
| Material | Pieces with the same material share its numbers and its worn picture, like iron or diamond. Leave it empty and the piece is its own material. |
| Armor points | The armor points it gives, each half a shirt over the health bar: an iron chestplate gives 6, iron boots 2. From 0 to 30. |
| Body color | The color it is drawn in on its wearer. |
| On the body | The picture it is drawn in on its wearer, on the game's layout of worn armor, painted as any picture is; without one it is drawn in its color. |
| Toughness | How much of a heavy hit the armor still stops: diamond 2, netherite 3. From 0 to 20. |
| Stands firm | How much less its wearer is pushed back by a hit, from nought to one: netherite 0.1 a piece. From 0 to 1. |
| Worn shape | A model of yours drawn on whoever wears it, a player or a mob: a hat, wings, a jetpack, a full suit. Each group named for a body part (Head, Body, Right arm, Left arm, Right leg, Left leg) moves with that part; Make one starts it on the wearer's body. |
| Follows | The body part a group of the shape follows when its name is not a body part's. Choose one of: The part its slot is on, Head, Body, Right arm, Left arm, Right leg, Left leg. |
| Its animations | Animations of the worn shape, each playing while its wearer does something or while a value of the piece is on: wings that flap while flying, a flame while the engine is on. Several play at once. Each row has: Animation, While, Value. |
| Parts shown only | A group of the worn shape drawn only while something holds: a module's part while its value is on, a visor while crouching. Groups not named here are always drawn. Each row has: Group, While, Value. |
| Or a carved shape | A block you carved on its Carve tab, worn on the body part in place of the flat armor, in the real pictures of its looks. A worn shape above wins. |
| Width on the body | How many pixels across the carved block or copied design is drawn on the wearer. A head is 8; 10 sits over it like a helmet. From 1 to 48. |
| Takes a carved design | Sneak and use this on a carved block to copy its design onto the item, then wear it to show the design on the body part. Sneak and use in the air to clear it. The block stays. Set the size above. |
| Tint | A color the worn shape's picture is multiplied by; white keeps it as painted. |
| Glows | The worn shape is drawn at full light, bright in the dark. |
| See-through | How much you see through the worn shape, from 0 (solid) to 90. From 0 to 90. |
| Hides the flat armor | The game's flat armor picture is not drawn, only the worn shape. |
| Only for its look over | While it is worn, the armor in this slot keeps protecting but is not drawn, and this piece is drawn in its place: a cosmetic slot. Choose one of: Nothing, The helmet, The chestplate, The leggings, The boots. |

### Holds energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Holds up to | The most energy one of it keeps, in the same units as a machine's energy. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Kind of energy | What its energy is called: Energy, Mana, or a unit of the mod's own. Items of one kind charge each other; another kind is kept apart unless an item says it mixes. |
| Spends per use | Energy spent for each block it mines, each hit it gives, and each hit its wearer takes while it is worn. 0 spends nothing. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Spends each second | Energy spent every second while it is held in the hand or worn: a lamp, a jetpack, a suit that keeps its wearer cool. 0 spends nothing. From 0 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Charges other items | A battery: once a second it gives its energy to the items that hold energy in the place chosen, at its rate. It never charges another battery. Choose one of: No, Worn, On the head, On the chest, On the legs, On the feet, Charm slots, Ring slot, Necklace slot, Belt slot, Back slot, Gloves slot, Held, In the hand, Off hand, Hotbar, Anywhere carried, Another slot. |
| Slot name | The name the slot mod gives that slot, such as charm or head/face. |
| Draws when it runs short | When it is used and has too little, it takes what it lacks from the items of its kind in the place chosen, such as the tablets in the bag. No: it spends only its own. Choose one of: No, Worn, On the head, On the chest, On the legs, On the feet, Charm slots, Ring slot, Necklace slot, Belt slot, Back slot, Gloves slot, Held, In the hand, Off hand, Hotbar, Anywhere carried. |
| Charges at | How much energy goes in or out of it each second: from a machine, from a battery, or out of it into what it charges or powers. From 1 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Worth of 1 FE | How many of this kind one unit of other mods' energy (FE) is worth. At 1 it is the same; at 0.1, ten FE from a charger fill one of it, and a machine drawing 1 of it takes 10 FE. From 0.0001 to 1000000. |
| Mixes kinds | When it charges other items or draws, it also reaches items of another kind, at the worth of each (a converter). |
| Runs machines | Put in a machine's slots, it gives its energy to the machine at its rate, instead of being charged by it. |
| When it is empty | Stops: without the energy of one use, a tool mines as a hand does, a weapon hits as a fist, armour guards nothing and gives nothing, until it is charged. Works on: energy is only spent. Choose one of: It stops working, It works on. |
| Starts charged | How full a new one is, from 0 (empty) to 100 (full). From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Shown | Where a player sees its energy: a bar under the item's picture, a line of its tooltip, both, or nowhere. Choose one of: Bar and tooltip, Bar, Tooltip, Nowhere. |
| Bar colour | The colour of the energy bar under its picture. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Worn, Holds energy.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Face part](thing-facePart.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-poweredTool

# Powered tool

A tool and weapon that runs on energy instead of wearing out: each block and each hit spends some, and empty it mines as a hand.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Powered tool


## What you can set

### Mines

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Blocks it is for | The blocks it is the tool for: choose a group of blocks (all that a pickaxe or an axe mines) or single blocks. |
| Strong as | Which blocks give it their drops: an iron one gets diamonds from their ore, a stone one does not. Choose one of: Wood, Gold (as wood), Stone, Iron, Diamond, Netherite. |
| Mining speed | How fast it mines what it is the tool for, which is how long mining takes: stone takes 0.4 s at 6 (iron), 0.6 s at 4 (stone), 1.15 s at 2 (wood). A square breaks when its middle does. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Breaks at once | One block, or a square across the face it mines, as a hammer does, outlined in the game before it breaks. Each block of the square costs one use and gives its own drops. Choose one of: One block, Three by three, Five by five, Seven by seven, Nine by nine, Eleven by eleven. |
| Goes this deep | How many blocks deep the square goes, straight into the face it mines. One is just the square. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Used on a block | What it does where it is used, as the game's own tool does: strips a log as an axe, tills earth as a hoe, makes a path as a shovel. Choose one of: Nothing, Strips, as an axe, Tills, as a hoe, Makes a path, as a shovel. |

### Weapon

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Damage | What one full hit takes, where a heart is 2: an iron sword does 6, a diamond one 7. From 1 to 1000. |
| Hits a second | How often a full strength hit can land: a sword 1.6, an axe 0.9. From 0.1 to 20. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Effect level | How strong the effect of a hit is: Poison 2 hurts twice as fast as Poison 1. From 1 to 10. |
| Sets alight for | Seconds a hit sets what it hits on fire; nought sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |

### Holds energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Holds up to | The most energy one of it keeps, in the same units as a machine's energy. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Kind of energy | What its energy is called: Energy, Mana, or a unit of the mod's own. Items of one kind charge each other; another kind is kept apart unless an item says it mixes. |
| Spends per use | Energy spent for each block it mines, each hit it gives, and each hit its wearer takes while it is worn. 0 spends nothing. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Spends each second | Energy spent every second while it is held in the hand or worn: a lamp, a jetpack, a suit that keeps its wearer cool. 0 spends nothing. From 0 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Charges other items | A battery: once a second it gives its energy to the items that hold energy in the place chosen, at its rate. It never charges another battery. Choose one of: No, Worn, On the head, On the chest, On the legs, On the feet, Charm slots, Ring slot, Necklace slot, Belt slot, Back slot, Gloves slot, Held, In the hand, Off hand, Hotbar, Anywhere carried, Another slot. |
| Slot name | The name the slot mod gives that slot, such as charm or head/face. |
| Draws when it runs short | When it is used and has too little, it takes what it lacks from the items of its kind in the place chosen, such as the tablets in the bag. No: it spends only its own. Choose one of: No, Worn, On the head, On the chest, On the legs, On the feet, Charm slots, Ring slot, Necklace slot, Belt slot, Back slot, Gloves slot, Held, In the hand, Off hand, Hotbar, Anywhere carried. |
| Charges at | How much energy goes in or out of it each second: from a machine, from a battery, or out of it into what it charges or powers. From 1 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Worth of 1 FE | How many of this kind one unit of other mods' energy (FE) is worth. At 1 it is the same; at 0.1, ten FE from a charger fill one of it, and a machine drawing 1 of it takes 10 FE. From 0.0001 to 1000000. |
| Mixes kinds | When it charges other items or draws, it also reaches items of another kind, at the worth of each (a converter). |
| Runs machines | Put in a machine's slots, it gives its energy to the machine at its rate, instead of being charged by it. |
| When it is empty | Stops: without the energy of one use, a tool mines as a hand does, a weapon hits as a fist, armour guards nothing and gives nothing, until it is charged. Works on: energy is only spent. Choose one of: It stops working, It works on. |
| Starts charged | How full a new one is, from 0 (empty) to 100 (full). From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Shown | Where a player sees its energy: a bar under the item's picture, a line of its tooltip, both, or nowhere. Choose one of: Bar and tooltip, Bar, Tooltip, Nowhere. |
| Bar colour | The colour of the energy bar under its picture. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Mines, Weapon, Holds energy.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-projectile

# Projectile

A thing that flies, drawn by a model: a spell, a dart, a boomerang, a homing missile. Shot by the shoot words and a creature's Throw move.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Projectile


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Projectile](editor-projectile.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players see it called. |
| Game name | Its game name in the game, small letters and underscores; the shoot words fire it by this. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front faces where it flies. |
| Speed | How fast it leaves, in blocks a second; a snowball flies 30, an arrow from a full bow 60. It flies at this speed whatever fires it; 0 is set down where it is made, as a lit charge. From 0 to 200 blocksPerSecond. |
| Gravity | How fast it falls: 1 falls as a snowball does, 0 flies straight as a fireball, below 0 floats up as a balloon. From -10 to 10 normal. |
| Damage | How much it hurts a mob it hits, in hearts. From 0 to 1000 hearts. |
| Flight animation | An animation of its model it plays over and over as it flies: wings beating, a blade turning. |
| Scale | How big its model is drawn; 1 is the model's own size. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Spin | Turns a second about the way it flies, as a shuriken or a drill spins; 0 flies straight. From 0 to 20 perSecond. |
| Drag | How much of its speed the air takes each second; a snowball loses 18. From 0 to 99 percent. |
| Lifetime | How long it flies before it ends where it is, or turns back when it returns. From 0.5 to 120 seconds. |
| Knockback | How hard it pushes a mob it hits; 1 is a sword's own push. From 0 to 10. |
| Sets alight | How long a mob it hits burns; 0 sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Pierces | How many mobs it flies through before it stops at one. From 0 to 64 times. |
| Bounces | How many times it bounces off a wall before it ends there. From 0 to 64 times. |
| When it ends | What it does where it stops: vanish, stick in the block it hit as a thrown knife does, explode, break the block, or set fire. Choose one of: Vanishes, Sticks where it lands, Explodes, Breaks the block, Sets fire. |
| Explosion | How big the explosion is; TNT is 4. From 0.5 to 10. |
| Returns | Flies back to whoever threw it after it hits or reaches its reach, as a boomerang or a yoyo, through anything on the way. |
| Reach | How far it flies out before it turns back. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Homing | How hard it turns toward its target each tick: what its thrower fights, or the nearest mob. 0 flies where it was aimed. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Homing reach | How far it looks for a target. From 1 to 64 blocks. |
| Trail | The particles it leaves behind it as it flies. Choose one of: None, Flame, Smoke, Heart, Crit, Portal, Happy, Soul, Snow, Enchanting letters, Music notes, Angry clouds, White clouds, Bubbles, A witch's sparkle, A totem's burst, A sword's sweep, End rod sparks, Glow squid light, Wax flecks, Electric sparks, Sculk souls, Water drops. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md).

## Picture

![Projectile](/media/docs/editor-projectile.webp)

## Related pages

- [Projectile](editor-projectile.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-wirelessReceiver

# Receiver

A block that gives out the redstone sent on its channel, by a transmitter or by a rule.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Receiver


## What you can set

### Linked by a channel

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channel | The name that links it: blocks on the same channel are linked. A player renames a block in an anvil before placing it to put that one on another channel. |
| On its channel it | Sends: what it holds, and the redstone reaching it, go out on the channel, and its faces take in. Receives: it gets what is sent, gives out the channel's signal, and its faces give out. Shares: it holds what every sharing block on the channel holds, one chest or one tank in many places, in every world, kept by the world even while none of them is loaded. Choose one of: sends, receives, shares, jams. |
| Carries a redstone signal | A sending block sends the redstone that reaches it; a receiving block gives out the strongest signal on its channel. |
| Reaches | How far the link reaches, in blocks. 0 reaches anywhere, in every world. From 0 to 100000 blocks. |
| Only its owner's | The channel belongs to the player who placed it: another player's block on a channel of the same name is not linked to it. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Linked by a channel.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# Recipe

Make something in a crafting table, furnace, stonecutter or smithing table.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Recipe


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Recipe](editor-recipe.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | A name for you. Players never see it. |
| Game name | The file name inside the mod. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. |
| Shape | Shaped keeps the things where you put them in the grid. Shapeless only cares which things are used. Smelting puts one thing in a furnace. Choose one of: Shaped, Shapeless, Smelting, Blasting, Smoking, Campfire, Stonecutting, Smithing, Trim, Transmute, Dye, Imbue, Brewing, Raw recipe. |
| Makes | What comes out of the crafting table. |
| How many | How many come out each time. From 1 to 64. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-recipeChange

# Recipe change

Change a recipe the game or another mod already has. Swap an input or the result, add inputs or extras.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Recipe change


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Recipe change](editor-recipeChange.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What it is called here. |
| Game name | Its name inside the game, in small letters. |
| Recipes | The recipes this changes: the game's, or those of a mod you build on. Find them by what they make or use, then read them. |
| What changes | A thing put in place of another wherever the recipe names it. Each row has: Swap, for, in. |
| Also needs | Things the recipe needs as well: in a shapeless recipe's list, or in the first free cell of a shaped grid. Each row has: Slot. |
| Also gives | More things a crafting grid gives with the result, each by its own chance. They come back as leftovers do: into the grid, else into the inventory; a crafter puts them out. On a furnace, blast furnace or smoker recipe they are given when you take the result out. Each row has: Thing, How many, Chance. |
| Result from the inputs | How what it makes takes its data from what went in, in order: its enchantments, name, wear or colour, all its data, or the inputs' durability added up. Each row has: Takes, From, Bonus. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

| Sound | The sound it starts with and takes each offering with. Choose one of: fire crackle, thunder, explosion, anvil, bell, level up, hurt, pop, a door opening, a chest opening, experience picked up, a button click, a villager agreeing, a villager refusing, an enderman's teleport, a portal's hum, a splash, eating, a burp, the wither's arrival, the dragon's growl, a totem saving a life, an amethyst chime, a harp note. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-satellite

# Satellite

A launched thing that watches a place and reports back. A rule launches one over a place; every so often its report rule runs there and reads what you like (an area value, the blocks or mobs near), then acts: sets a value, notes a number on an item, sends energy down.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Satellite


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Satellite](editor-satellite.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name of the satellite, as you and your players know it. |
| Game name | The satellite's name inside the game files. Lower case letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Reports every | How many seconds between its reports. From 1 to 86400 seconds. |
| Stays up for | How many seconds it stays up before it comes down. Nought: until a rule brings it down. From 0 to 31536000 seconds. |
| Covers | How many blocks round the place it watches count as covered, for the words that ask which satellites cover a place. From 1 to 100000 blocks. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-seaMount

# Sea mount

A swimming mob ridden under water, its rider breathing.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Sea mount


## What you can set

### Has a spawn egg

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Egg colour | The colour of the egg itself. |
| Spot colour | The colour of the spots on the egg. |

### Can be tamed

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tamed by | What makes it a player's: an item given to it, riding it until it calms, or only a rule's words. Choose one of: Giving it an item, Riding it until it calms, Only a rule. |
| Tamed with | The item a player gives it, one each try. |
| Chance a try | How likely each item given, or each time it is ridden, tames it. From 1 to 100 percent. |
| Sits when told | Its owner's use makes it sit and stay, and stand again. |
| Follows owner | It keeps near its owner when it is not sitting. |
| Follows from | How far its owner may go before it comes after them. From 2 to 32 blocks. |
| Catches up | Left far behind, it appears beside its owner, as a tame wolf does. |
| Strikes back at its owner | Off, a tamed one never targets or attacks its owner or the owner's team, however it was hurt, as a wolf does not. |
| Defends owner | It attacks what hurts its owner and what its owner attacks. |
| Healed with | Foods its owner gives it to heal it. |

### Can be ridden

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Flies ridden | How it flies with a rider: the jump key rises, the sprint key (Ctrl) descends, forward goes where the rider looks, A and D turn it; hovering and flapping hold their height when no key is held, gliding sinks slowly. Choose one of: Does not fly, Glides, Hovers, Flaps, Its own way. |
| Climbs at | How fast it rises while its rider holds jump. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| Sinks at | How fast it sinks in the air with nothing held. 0: it hovers. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| Dives at | How fast it goes down while its rider holds the descend key. From 0 to 40 blocks a second. |
| In water | Floating keeps its rider's head up; swimming dives and rises where the rider looks, and the rider breathes. Choose one of: Floats, Swims under. |
| Needs a saddle | It can be ridden only once a saddle is put on it. |
| Saddle | The item used on it as its saddle. |
| Ridden by | Only its owner once it is tamed, or anyone. Choose one of: Its owner, Anyone. |
| Speed ridden | How fast it goes with a rider, times its own speed. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| Flying speed | How fast it flies with a rider, times its own flying speed. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| Jumps | How high it jumps on a full charge of the jump bar. From 0 to 8 blocks. |
| Seat height | How far above or below its back the rider sits; the back is found from the shape of its body. From -4 to 8 blocks. |
| A and D | Turning turns the creature and the rider's view with it, as a horse does; strafing moves it sideways and keeps it facing. Choose one of: Turn it, Strafe, Nothing. |
| Mouse look | Steering, the creature faces where the rider looks, as a vanilla horse does; looking only, the view turns on its own and the creature faces where A and D turned it. Choose one of: Steers it, Looks only. |
| W and S | Forward and back move it along its body; set to nothing, only the other keys move it. Choose one of: Move it, Nothing. |
| Jump key | Auto rises a flier or a swimmer and makes the others jump with the jump bar; or choose to rise, to jump, or nothing. Choose one of: Auto, Rise, Jump, Nothing. |
| Free up and down | A flier or a swimmer rises while the jump key is held, holds its height when nothing is held, and descends on the sprint key. Off, it goes up and down only where the rider looks. |
| Descend key | The key held to take a flier or a swimmer down (changed in the game's Controls); the sneak key always gets the rider off. Choose one of: Sprint key (Ctrl), Swap-hands key (F), None. |
| Rider on a tilt | Following, the rider leans with the seat's part of the body as it tilts (a dragon pitched in flight); upright, he stays level whatever the body does. First person stays level either way. Choose one of: Follows the seat, Stays upright. |
| Rider can hit it | A left click while riding never lands on the creature itself unless this is on. |
| Falls hurt | Off, neither the rider nor the creature takes fall damage while riding, and the rider none from the fall off its back. |
| Seat forward | How far forward of the middle of its back the rider sits; below zero is behind. From -4 to 4 blocks. |
| Turn speed | How fast A and D turn it, and the rider's view with it, in degrees a second. From 10 to 360 degrees a second. |
| Seats | How many ride it at once; the first steers. From 1 to 4. |

Every mob also has the settings on the [Mob](editor-creature.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Has a spawn egg, Can be tamed, Can be ridden.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Damage type](editor-damageType.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Mob](thing-creature.md), [Pet](thing-pet.md), [Mount](thing-mount.md), [Flying mount](thing-flyingMount.md), [Boss](thing-boss.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-sharedChest

# Shared chest

A chest that is the same chest wherever it is placed: every shared chest on one channel holds the same items, in every world.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Shared chest


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### Linked by a channel

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channel | The name that links it: blocks on the same channel are linked. A player renames a block in an anvil before placing it to put that one on another channel. |
| On its channel it | Sends: what it holds, and the redstone reaching it, go out on the channel, and its faces take in. Receives: it gets what is sent, gives out the channel's signal, and its faces give out. Shares: it holds what every sharing block on the channel holds, one chest or one tank in many places, in every world, kept by the world even while none of them is loaded. Choose one of: sends, receives, shares, jams. |
| Carries a redstone signal | A sending block sends the redstone that reaches it; a receiving block gives out the strongest signal on its channel. |
| Reaches | How far the link reaches, in blocks. 0 reaches anywhere, in every world. From 0 to 100000 blocks. |
| Only its owner's | The channel belongs to the player who placed it: another player's block on a channel of the same name is not linked to it. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Connections, Linked by a channel.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

## Picture

![Block](/media/docs/editor-block.webp)

## Related pages

- [Block](editor-block.md)
- [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-sharedTank

# Shared tank

A tank that is the same tank wherever it is placed: every shared tank on one channel holds the same fluid, in every world, kept even while none of them is loaded. Pipes fill and drain it like any tank.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Shared tank


## What you can set

### Fluid

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its tank. A bucket is 1,000. Set it to nothing for a pipe. From 0 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. From 0 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| No limit | On: fluid cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Only this fluid | Choose a fluid. Leave it empty and it takes whatever arrives first, then keeps to that one. |
| More tanks | Tanks beside its own, each holding a fluid of its own, as a machine taking water and giving lava. Each row has: Most it holds, Only this fluid, Reached from. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-skill

# Skill

A skill with levels, like Mining or Farming: XP comes from any moment, each level reached runs its rewards, and locks may wait for a level.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Skill


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Skill](editor-skill.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The skill's name, shown on the screen while playing. |
| Game name | Its name in the game and in rules. |
| Levels | The highest level the skill reaches. From 1 to 100000. |
| Starts at level | The level every player has before any XP. From 0 to 100000. |
| XP for each level | The XP it takes to go from a level to the next; a formula may read the level, as 50 * the level. From 1 to 100000000. |
| Shown while playing | Its name, level and a bar of XP at the top left of the screen. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## Picture

![Skill](/media/docs/editor-skill.webp)

## Related pages

- [Skill](editor-skill.md)
- [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-skin

# Skin

A player's skin: the body and its picture to paint, with poses to show it in.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Skin


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Model](editor-model.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What this shape is called in the product. It is not shown in the game. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this model, in small letters with no spaces. The Name above is only for you. |
| Shape | The boxes and groups this shape is made of. Open the Model tab to build it. |
| Its pictures are | How the game draws what is clear in the pictures. Solid ignores it. With holes leaves a clear pixel out, as the game's own glass does. See-through draws each pixel as clear as it was painted, so what is inside can be seen. Choose one of: Solid, With holes, See-through. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-spaceStation

# Space station

A built place in a dimension of its own that anyone or any vehicle docks with, orbiting a world at a height that rules move. Build the region where you like and say where the dock is.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Space station


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Space station](editor-spaceStation.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name of the station, as you and your players know it. |
| Game name | The station's name inside the game files. Lower case letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Built in | The dimension the station stands in: your space dimension. |
| Dock, across | Where arrivals stand: the block across (x). From -30000000 to 30000000. |
| Dock, up | Where arrivals stand: the height (y). From -2048 to 2048. |
| Dock, along | Where arrivals stand: the block along (z). From -30000000 to 30000000. |
| Orbits | The world below it. Sending someone down lands them on the ground of this dimension. |
| Starts at height | How high above that world the station is when the world is new. From 0 to 1000000000 blocks. |
| Falls a second | How much height it loses by itself each second, an orbit that decays. Nought: it stays where it is until a rule moves it. From 0 to 1000000000 perSecond. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-species

# Species

A kind of bee, plant or animal: the gene values it starts with, what it looks like as a block, an item or a mob, and which two species bred give it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Species


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Species](editor-species.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads before the thing's name, such as Forest Bee. |
| Saved as | The name the species is kept under, and what rules call it. |
| Wins | When a thing carries two species, a dominant one shows over a recessive one. Choose one of: Dominant, Recessive. |
| Gene values | What each gene is in this species. A gene not listed starts as the gene says. Each row has: Gene, Value. |
| Block | The block this species grows as: what a crossing places, and a block that carries it. |
| Item | The item that carries this species, such as its seeds or its bee. |
| Comes from | Each line: two species bred give this one, by a chance, where its conditions hold. Each row has: First, Second, Chance, Only in, Near, Within, When, Takes the new species' genes. |
| Needs | What this species needs where it is, every line at once: a block near or under it, a biome, a time of day. A plant that lacks one does not grow, and rules can ask it. Each row has: Block, Within, Only in, When, Light at least, Light at most, Value, Value at least, Value at most. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It points at: [Gene](editor-gene.md), [Block](editor-block.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-spell

# Spell

A spell of its own: what it does as rules (when it is cast, when it reaches a mob or a block, every tick it is kept up), what it costs (mana or any value), its cooldown and charge-up, and how it reaches: on the caster, along a ray, as a missile or all around. Cast by a wand, a scroll, any rule or a creature.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Spell


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Spell](editor-spell.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the spell is called in the game. |
| Game name | The spell's game name in the game; another mod casts it by this. |
| What it is | A whole spell, or a part a spell is put together from: a medium says how a made spell reaches, a modifier changes it. A whole spell is also the part that says what a made spell does. Choose one of: A whole spell (or an effect), A medium (how it reaches), A modifier (what changes it). |
| Made of parts | Put this spell together from parts: a medium, effects (whole spells, this mod's or another mod's) and modifiers. Their costs add up and every part's moments run. Empty: it is a spell of its own. Each row has: Part. |
| Reaches | How it reaches what it does: the caster alone, what the caster touches, along where the caster looks, as a projectile, every mob around, or as a construct left where its ray ends. Choose one of: On the caster, By touch, Along a ray, As a missile, All around, Left in the world. |
| Range | How far its ray goes, or how wide its area is, in blocks. From 1 to 128 blocks. |
| Missile | What it fires: one of the game's, or a projectile of the mod's own. Its hit is the spell's hit. Choose one of: Small fireball, Fireball, Arrow, Snowball, Wither skull. |
| Construct | What it leaves where its ray ends: a ward hits everything inside it again and again, a trap waits for the first to come in and hits once, a sentinel hits the nearest one in reach. Choose one of: A ward (hits all inside, again and again), A trap (waits, hits once), A sentinel (hits the nearest). |
| Stays for | How long the construct stays in the world, in seconds. From 0.05 to 3600 seconds. |
| Acts every | How often a ward or a sentinel hits, in seconds. From 0.05 to 600 seconds. |
| Construct size | How far from its middle the construct reaches, in blocks. From 0.5 to 32 blocks. |
| Construct hits | Whom the construct hits: monsters alone, or every living thing but the one who cast it. Choose one of: Monsters, Everyone but the caster. |
| Power more | How much stronger it makes the spell, in a hundred: 50 is half as strong again. The power is handed to every moment of the spell. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Range more | How much further it makes the spell reach, and a construct wider, in a hundred. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Time more | How much longer it makes a kept-up spell and a construct last, in a hundred. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Copies more | How many more copies of the spell go out, fanned to the sides. From 0 to 16. |
| Cost more | How much more the whole made spell costs, in a hundred; below nought makes it cheaper. From -100 to 1000 percent. |
| Part item | The item that stands for it when a player puts a spell together in a block with slots (a rune, a herb, a focus), with the Make a spell word. |
| Costs | The value it is paid from: the player's mana, or a value the item that casts it keeps (a wand's charge). None makes it free. |
| Cost | How much of that value one cast takes; a kept-up spell takes this much a second. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Cooldown | How long before it can be cast again, in seconds. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Charge-up | How long the use is held before it goes, in seconds. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Kept up | It goes on while the use is held, its moment every tick and its cost a second at a time: a beam, a stream of fire. |
| Must be learned | Only a player who has learned it casts it (a spell book teaches it, or the Teach a spell word). |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Projectile](editor-projectile.md), [Value](editor-value.md).

## Picture

![Spell](/media/docs/editor-spell.webp)

## Related pages

- [Spell](editor-spell.md)
- [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-spellBook

# Spell book

An item that teaches the spells listed on it when it is used, so a wand that casts the spells a player knows can cast them.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Spell book


## What you can set

### Holds spells

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| When used | What using it does: casts its spell, teaches its spells, or casts once and is used up. Choose one of: Casts, Teaches, Casts once, used up. |
| Spells | The spells listed here, or every spell of its kit the player has learned (other mods' too). Choose one of: Listed here, Learned of its kit. |
| Spells it holds | The spells it casts or teaches, in the order sneak-use goes through them. Each row has: Spell. |
| Kit | The kit whose learned spells it casts; empty is this mod's own. |
| Cost share | What share of a spell's cost it takes, in percent: 50 casts at half the mana. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Cooldown share | What share of a spell's cooldown it waits, in percent. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Power share | How strong it makes its spells, in percent: their moments read it as power (1 at a hundred), so a hurt of 4 times power hurts 6 from a wand of 150. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Range share | How far it makes its spells reach, in percent of their range. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Up to tier | The strongest tier of spell it casts. From 1 to 10. |
| Switch with | How the player chooses its spell: sneak and use, or only by rules (a key of the mod's). Choose one of: Sneak and use, Rules only. |
| Spell slots | How many spells it keeps, one a slot (a staff of several). Its listed spells fill them first; the Make a spell word puts a spell made of parts in one. Nought keeps no slots. From 0 to 9. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Holds spells.

## What it works with

| When used | What using it does: casts its spell, teaches its spells, or casts once and is used up. Choose one of: Casts, Teaches, Casts once, used up. |
| Spells | The spells listed here, or every spell of its kit the player has learned (other mods' too). Choose one of: Listed here, Learned of its kit. |
| Spells it holds | The spells it casts or teaches, in the order sneak-use goes through them. Each row has: Spell. |
| Kit | The kit whose learned spells it casts; empty is this mod's own. |
| Cost share | What share of a spell's cost it takes, in percent: 50 casts at half the mana. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Cooldown share | What share of a spell's cooldown it waits, in percent. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Power share | How strong it makes its spells, in percent: their moments read it as power (1 at a hundred), so a hurt of 4 times power hurts 6 from a wand of 150. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Range share | How far it makes its spells reach, in percent of their range. From 0 to 1000 percent. |
| Up to tier | The strongest tier of spell it casts. From 1 to 10. |
| Switch with | How the player chooses its spell: sneak and use, or only by rules (a key of the mod's). Choose one of: Sneak and use, Rules only. |
| Spell slots | How many spells it keeps, one a slot (a staff of several). Its listed spells fill them first; the Make a spell word puts a spell made of parts in one. Nought keeps no slots. From 0 to 9. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Holds spells.

## What it works with

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Face part](thing-facePart.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-stationRecipe

# Station recipe

A recipe done on a station's own screen, with cells, tanks and energy.

## How to add it

- New thing > Crafting and loot > Station recipe


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Station recipe](editor-stationRecipe.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this recipe. |
| Game name | The name the game files use for this recipe. |
| Station | The block whose screen it fills. Its Slot groups give the cells. |
| Shape | Shaped matches the pattern anywhere in a group; shapeless any cells. Choose one of: Shaped, Shapeless. |
| Cells | What each cell of the station's screen holds, by the cell's name. Each row has: Cell, Slot. |
| Makes | What comes out of the crafting table. |
| How many | How many come out each time. From 1 to 64. |
| Seconds | 0 crafts when the result is taken, as a crafting table does. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| How much energy | Energy it uses over the whole craft; 0 for none. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| More in and out | Any number of things more that go in or come out, beside the ones above: items, fluids or stocks of your own, each with how much and, coming out, how often. Each row has: Goes, What, Item, Fluid, Stock, Type, How much, How often, Tank. |
| Works only when | The recipe only works when this holds: at night, in a biome, in some weather, after an advancement, when a setting is on, or what is around the place it is made. Every row must hold. Each row has: When, Block, Value, Dimension, Weather, Name, Setting, At least, At most, Hours, At least, At most, Blocks away, Turned round. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Block](editor-block.md), [Custom kind](editor-matter.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mod settings](editor-configValue.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-storageCable

# Storage cable

Joins cells, drawers, chests and terminals into one network.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Storage cable


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### Channels

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channels | How many things beyond it one cable can lead to. 8 is a plain cable, 32 a dense one, 0 no limit. From 0 to 100000. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Connections, Channels.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-storageDisk

# Storage disk

An item that holds many kinds of item by count. Put it in a drive; carry it away full.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Storage disk


## What you can set

### Storage disk

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Holds | What kind of stock it keeps: items, fluids, energy, or a stock you name (mana, gas, anything). Choose one of: Items, Fluids, Energy, A stock you name. |
| Stock name | The name of the stock it keeps, as the rules call it: mana, gas, souls. |
| Size | How much it holds of every kind together: items by count, fluids by the bucket's thousandths, energy and named stock by amount. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Kinds | How many different kinds it holds at most. From 1 to 1000. |
| Only takes | The things it takes; anything else goes elsewhere. A fluid by its bucket. None: it takes anything of its kind. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Storage disk.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-structure

# Structure

A building or ruin placed in the world.

## How to add it

- New thing > The world > Structure


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Structure](editor-structure.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. The game never shows it. |
| Game name | The structure's name in the game, as a command finds it: /locate structure. |
| Made from | Built here, block by block, or a structure file saved in the game with a structure block. Choose one of: Built here, A structure file. |
| Blocks | Built on the Build tab, layer by layer. |
| File | A structure saved in the game with a structure block, from its generated folder. |
| Placed by | Whether the world's generation places it on its own, or it is only a piece another structure joins where its jigsaw blocks are. Choose one of: The world, Joining only, A rule, while playing. |
| Where | The biomes it stands in. Pick them by name, or choose the whole Overworld. |
| Spread | Where the world puts it: at random places kept apart, a set number in rings around the world's centre as strongholds are, or just one at the centre, in the nearest of its biomes. Choose one of: At random, kept apart, In rings around the centre, One, at the world's centre. |
| Apart | About how far apart two of them stand, in chunks of sixteen blocks. From 2 to 256 chunks. |
| First ring at | How far from the world's centre its first ring is: strongholds' is 32 chunks. From 1 to 1023 chunks. |
| How many | How many of it the world has in all, set in rings around its centre. From 1 to 128. |
| Joins to | The pieces that join it where it has a jigsaw block, each as likely as its weight. A jigsaw block on an edge of a build faces out from that edge, and a piece joins it by one of its own facing back. Each row has: Piece, Weight. |
| Joins deep | How many pieces deep it grows from the first: each piece's own jigsaw blocks join the pieces it lists in turn. From 1 to 20 joins. |
| Ends with | A piece that closes a join when the structure runs out of depth or room: a wall or a dead end, so no doorway opens into the rock. |
| Fewest rooms | The least rooms a dungeon built by a rule has, the first and the last counted. It may have fewer only when no more fit at its doors. From 1 to 200 rooms. |
| Most rooms | The most rooms a dungeon built by a rule has. Each build picks a count between fewest and most from its seed. From 1 to 200 rooms. |
| Last room | The room built last, at the door farthest from the first room: where a boss or a treasure waits. Empty: the dungeon has no last room of its own. |
| Waiting in the last room | A mob that appears in the middle of the last room when the dungeon is built, and stays there. Empty: none. |
| Chest in the last room | A chest in the middle of the last room, filled from this loot table when it is first opened. Empty: no chest. |
| Close open doors with | The block that fills a door no room was joined to, so no doorway opens into the rock or the empty. |
| Stands | How it meets the ground. Choose one of: On the ground, the ground raised to meet it, In a pit dug for it, Buried, the ground over it, Underground, at a height of its own. |
| At height | The height its lowest layer stands at, deep in the stone: 0 is far below the sea, the deep dark lower still. From -60 to 300 blocks. |
| Spawners bring | The mob each spawner in its build brings out, as a dungeon's does. A build without a spawner brings none. |
| Chests hold | What its chests and barrels are filled with the first time they open. Left empty, they hold what was put in them. |
| Containers hold | What each kind of container in its build holds: items of your choosing in counts fixed or random, or a loot table of the mod's own or the game's; several rows of one container all go in it. A row's container can also stand at random spots: it is there as often as its share. Each row has: Container, Holds, Item, Fewest, Most, Loot table, There. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Biome](editor-biome.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md), [Loot table](editor-lootTable.md), [Block](editor-block.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-tag

# Tag

A named group of blocks or items other rules can point at.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Tag


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Tag](editor-tag.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this group. |
| Group id | The game's id for the group, like minecraft:mineable/pickaxe. A vanilla one gets your members added; a new one is yours. |
| Of | What the group holds: blocks, items, biomes, structures, mobs, fluids, kinds of hurt or enchantments. Choose one of: Blocks, Items, Biomes, Structures, Mobs, Fluids, Kinds of hurt, Enchantments. |
| Members | The ids in the group, separated by spaces. Another group goes in with a # in front. |
| Taken out | Members taken out of the tag, whoever put them in: the game, another mod. Ids or #tags, separated by spaces. |
| Clear the tag first | Drops everything the game and other mods put in this tag. Only the members you list here stay. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.
