# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-tank

# Tank

Holds a fluid and gives it to whatever asks for it.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Tank


## What you can set

### Fluid

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its tank. A bucket is 1,000. Set it to nothing for a pipe. From 0 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. From 0 to 1000000 millibuckets. |
| No limit | On: fluid cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Only this fluid | Choose a fluid. Leave it empty and it takes whatever arrives first, then keeps to that one. |
| More tanks | Tanks beside its own, each holding a fluid of its own, as a machine taking water and giving lava. Each row has: Most it holds, Only this fluid, Reached from. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Fluid, Connections.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-texture

# Texture

The pixels a block, item or mob wears.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Texture


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Texture](editor-texture.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call this picture. |
| Replaces | The game's id for the texture this stands in for, like minecraft:block/stone. |
| Texture | The picture that replaces it. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

## In plain words

A texture is a picture. **Replaces** is for when your picture takes the place of one the game already has. Leave it empty for a picture of your own. For example, `minecraft:block/stone` is the game's name for the picture on stone, so a texture that replaces it makes every stone block in the game wear your picture. To make or import one, see [Pictures and textures](pictures-and-textures.md). To put your own picture on a new block, see [A block with your own picture](block-with-your-own-picture.md).

# The player

The game's own player: its body, and rules for its moments, such as when it eats, is hurt or joins.

## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [The player](editor-player.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Max health | How many hearts a player has; the game's own is 10. From 0.5 to 512 hearts. |
| Size | How big a player is; 1 is the game's own size. From 0.0625 to 16 normal. |
| Speed | How fast a player walks, as a share of the game's own; 1 is the game's own. From 0 to 10 normal. |
| Gravity | How hard a player falls, as a share of the game's own; 1 is the game's own, below 1 floats. From -10 to 10 normal. |
| May fly | A player may fly as in creative, in every game mode. |
| Changes kept after death | What rules changed of a player's body stays after it dies; off, it starts again from the numbers here. |
| Extra slots | Slots of your own beyond the game's, like rings or a back slot. They are kept with you, opened from a button on your inventory screen, and what is in them counts as worn. Each row has: Slot name, How many, Takes only, Look over, Starts showing. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-thing

# Thing

Something in the world that is not a mob and does not fly: a spell's ward, a frame on a wall, a floating orb, a balloon on a string, a trap. Made by a rule word, drawn by a model.

## How to add it

- New thing > Mobs and models > Thing


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Thing](editor-thing.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players read above it, in any words: spaces and capitals are fine, like "Ruby Blade of Sam". The Game name is the short name the game uses instead. |
| Game name | The short name the game and its commands use: small letters, digits and underscores, like katana. In commands and recipes the mod's short name and a colon go in front: for a mod called rubygear, katana is written rubygear, a colon, then katana. Players never read it; that is the Name. Change it later and it is renamed everywhere. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front faces out of a wall it hangs on. |
| Animation | A clip it plays over and over as it stands. |
| Drawn size | How big its model is drawn: 1 is the model's own size. From 0.0625 to 16. |
| Width | How wide it is, in blocks: what can be hit and what it bumps into. From 0.05 to 16 blocks. |
| Height | How tall it is, in blocks. From 0.05 to 16 blocks. |
| When walked into | Walked through, stood on and bumped into like a block, or pushed along. Choose one of: Walked through, Solid, Pushed along. |
| Stays for | How long it stays before it ends by itself. 0 stays until it is broken. From 0 to 3600 seconds. |
| Breaks after | How much it takes from hits before it breaks. 0 never breaks from hits (a player in creative still breaks it). From 0 to 1000 hearts. |
| Where it hangs | Where it is made (in the air), flat on the face of a block, or beside the one who made it. Choose one of: Where it is made, On a block's face, Beside its owner, Pinned to a block, On top of a block. |
| Area | How far round it reaches, in blocks: the mobs inside are touched so often. 0 has no area. From 0 to 32 blocks. |
| Holds an item | A player puts an item in by using it and takes it out with an empty hand; it shows the item and drops it when it breaks. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-thrown

# Thrown weapon

Something thrown that flies as itself and hits: a throwing star, a javelin.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Thrown weapon


## What you can set

### Shoots

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Works like | Which of the game's own it starts from: a bow drawn and let go, a crossbow loaded and then fired, or thrown as a snowball or a trident is, the thing itself flying. Choose one of: The game's Bow, The game's Crossbow, Thrown. |
| Damage | What what it shoots takes from what it hits, where a heart is 2: the game's arrow 2 before its speed counts, a trident 8. From 0 to 1000. |
| Full draw | How long it takes to draw fully; let go sooner and it shoots weaker, as the game's bow does in its 1 second. From 0.05 to 10 seconds. |
| Flies at | How fast what it shoots flies, against the game's own: 1 is the game's, 2 twice as fast and farther. From 0.1 to 5 times. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Burning | What it shoots flies alight and sets what it hits on fire, as the Flame enchantment does. |
| Where it lands | What a thrown thing does when it hits: lies there to be picked up again, or breaks. Choose one of: Lies there, Breaks. |
| Flies | How it is drawn in flight: lying flat and spinning as a throwing star, point first as a javelin, or turned to the camera as the game draws a snowball. Choose one of: Flat, spinning, Point first, Facing the camera. |
| Shoots | What it looses: the game's arrow, or a projectile of your mod's own, which flies by its own settings. Choose one of: Arrow. |
| Shoots | What it takes from the inventory and shoots in place of arrows, yours or the game's, or any item of a tag; picked up again where it lands. With none, arrows. |
| Loading time | How long it takes to load, held before it is ready to fire; the game's crossbow takes 1.25 seconds. From 0.05 to 10 seconds. |
| Shots at once | How many it looses at once from one piece of ammunition, fanned out, as a crossbow with Multishot looses three. From 1 to 16 times. |
| Fan | How wide the shots at once fan out, in degrees from the first to the last. From 0 to 180 degrees. |
| Pause | Seconds before it can be thrown again, as the game's ender pearl waits 1. From 0 to 60 seconds. |
| Drawing | The picture as the draw begins. |
| Half drawn | The picture half way through the draw. |
| Drawn | The picture fully drawn. |
| Loaded | The picture of a crossbow loaded and ready to fire. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Shoots.

## What it works with

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-tool

# Tool

A pickaxe, axe or shovel, or a hammer that breaks a square at once.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Tool


## What you can set

### Mines

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Blocks it is for | The blocks it is the tool for: choose a group of blocks (all that a pickaxe or an axe mines) or single blocks. |
| Strong as | Which blocks give it their drops: an iron one gets diamonds from their ore, a stone one does not. Choose one of: Wood, Gold (as wood), Stone, Iron, Diamond, Netherite. |
| Mining speed | How fast it mines what it is the tool for, which is how long mining takes: stone takes 0.4 s at 6 (iron), 0.6 s at 4 (stone), 1.15 s at 2 (wood). A square breaks when its middle does. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Breaks at once | One block, or a square across the face it mines, as a hammer does, outlined in the game before it breaks. Each block of the square costs one use and gives its own drops. Choose one of: One block, Three by three, Five by five, Seven by seven, Nine by nine, Eleven by eleven. |
| Goes this deep | How many blocks deep the square goes, straight into the face it mines. One is just the square. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Used on a block | What it does where it is used, as the game's own tool does: strips a log as an axe, tills earth as a hoe, makes a path as a shovel. Choose one of: Nothing, Strips, as an axe, Tills, as a hoe, Makes a path, as a shovel. |

### Weapon

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Damage | What one full hit takes, where a heart is 2: an iron sword does 6, a diamond one 7. From 1 to 1000. |
| Hits a second | How often a full strength hit can land: a sword 1.6, an axe 0.9. From 0.1 to 20. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Effect level | How strong the effect of a hit is: Poison 2 hurts twice as fast as Poison 1. From 1 to 10. |
| Sets alight for | Seconds a hit sets what it hits on fire; nought sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |

### Wears out

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Uses before it breaks | How many blocks it mines, hits it lands or hits it takes before it breaks: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mended with | What mends it in an anvil, such as an iron ingot, or one of this mod's own things. |
| Comes enchanted with | Enchantments it has from the first time a player holds it, the game's own or your own, each at its level. Each row has: Enchantment, Level. |
| Enchants how well | How good the enchantments it is offered are: iron 14, diamond 10, gold 22. From 0 to 50. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Mines, Weapon, Wears out.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-tooltip

# Tooltip lines

Lines added to the tooltip of any item or block, the mod's or the game's, or of every item, each filled in from the item's numbers and values and shown by its own condition.

## How to add it

- New thing > Screens and guides > Tooltip lines


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Tooltip lines](editor-tooltip.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What you call it here. |
| On | One item or block (or a tag of them), or every item in the game. Choose one of: One item, block or tag, Every item. |
| Item | The item, block or tag whose tooltip gets the lines: the mod's own or the game's. |
| Lines | Each line's words, color and when it shows. A line can say the item's numbers and a value it or the player keeps: see Words. Each row has: Words, Color, Shown, Value, Amount. |
| Placed | Right under the item's name, or at the end of its tooltip. Choose one of: At the end, Under the name. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It points at: [Value](editor-value.md).

## Picture

![Tooltip lines](/media/docs/editor-tooltip.webp)

## Related pages

- [Tooltip lines](editor-tooltip.md)
- [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-tradeStation

# Trade station

Gives what it offers for what it wants, from its own slots.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Trade station


## What you can set

### Inventory

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Slots | How many stacks it holds, up to 256. Past six rows, its screen scrolls them or shows them all, as Screen shows says. From 1 to 256. |
| Screen shows | How its screen lays out more rows than six, until you lay it out on the Screen tab: six rows and a bar that scrolls the rest, or every slot at once in a screen grown to fit them. Choose one of: Six rows and a scroll bar, The whole grid at once. |
| Slots across | How many slots a row of its screen holds, 1 to 24. Past nine, the screen grows wider. From 1 to 24. |
| Items per slot | The most of one thing a slot takes. The game reads it live, so a mod setting can stand in. From 1 to 64. |
| Most a second | The most that moves in or out of it each second along a network. Hoppers keep their own speed. From 1 to 1024. |
| No limit | On: items cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |
| Items travel at | How fast an item crosses this block on a pipe that passes items on. At nought an item arrives the moment the network moves it. Above nought it takes time to cross, pipe by pipe, and each pipe holds and keeps what is inside it. From 0 to 20 blocksPerSecond. |
| Shares the cards in it | Every value card put in it gives its value by its name, to the whole world or to the cable network it sits on, so a reader or a sum anywhere there can use the name. A card named in an anvil uses that name; otherwise the item's own. Choose one of: No, With the whole world, On its cable network. |
| Opens a screen | Used by hand, it opens its slots in a screen laid out on the Screen tab. |
| Takes back with | Empty hand: any empty hand takes the item back. Sneaking: only an empty hand while sneaking does. Choose one of: An empty hand, Sneaking, empty hand. |
| Put in and take out by hand | A block with no screen takes the stack in the player's hand when used, and gives it back to an empty hand (sneaking or not), as a lectern or a decorated pot does. Turn it off when only machines and commands fill it. |
| Screen | The machine's screen, laid out on the Screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws it from the slots and gauges. |

### Trade station

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Gives | The thing it gives. Leave it and Wants empty, and the station's first slot shows what it gives and its second what it wants, so a player sets the offer in the game. |
| How many it gives | How many of it one trade gives. From 1 to 64. |
| Wants | The thing it takes as payment. |
| How many it wants | How many of it one trade costs. From 1 to 64. |
| Goods for sale | Add goods and it becomes a shop: using it opens a trading screen that lists them with their prices. Each row has: Gives, How many it gives, Price paid in, Price, In stock. |
| Goods on sale at once | How many of the goods are for sale at a time, taken in turn from the list. 0 shows them all. From 0 to 64. |
| Goods change every | Seconds before the next goods of the list go on sale and the stock fills again. 0 never changes them. From 0 to 1000000 seconds. |
| Next goods | Which goods go on sale when they change: the next ones down the list, or a shuffled pick each time. Choose one of: Next in the list, Shuffled. |
| Buys from players | Things it buys: a player who uses it holding one sells them and is paid. Each row has: Buys, How many at a time, Pays in, Pays. |
| Buys what is dropped on it | Things it buys that a player drops or throws on top of it are sold, as a shipping bin does. |
| Buys what lands in its slots | Things it buys that land in its slots, from a hopper or a player, are sold. Give it slots (Inventory) for this. |
| Pays out | Where the money for things dropped on it or put in its slots goes. A hopper under it can take money out of its slots. Choose one of: The player who sold, Into its slots, On top of it. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Inventory, Trade station.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Wireless energy node](thing-wirelessNode.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-wirelessTransmitter

# Transmitter

A block that sends the redstone reaching it on a channel, to every receiver on that channel, however far away.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Transmitter


## What you can set

### Linked by a channel

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channel | The name that links it: blocks on the same channel are linked. A player renames a block in an anvil before placing it to put that one on another channel. |
| On its channel it | Sends: what it holds, and the redstone reaching it, go out on the channel, and its faces take in. Receives: it gets what is sent, gives out the channel's signal, and its faces give out. Shares: it holds what every sharing block on the channel holds, one chest or one tank in many places, in every world, kept by the world even while none of them is loaded. Choose one of: sends, receives, shares, jams. |
| Carries a redstone signal | A sending block sends the redstone that reaches it; a receiving block gives out the strongest signal on its channel. |
| Reaches | How far the link reaches, in blocks. 0 reaches anywhere, in every world. From 0 to 100000 blocks. |
| Only its owner's | The channel belongs to the player who placed it: another player's block on a channel of the same name is not linked to it. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Linked by a channel.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-treeAxe

# Tree axe

An axe that fells a whole tree from one log, outlining the tree while it is aimed at.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Tree axe


## What you can set

### Mines

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Blocks it is for | The blocks it is the tool for: choose a group of blocks (all that a pickaxe or an axe mines) or single blocks. |
| Strong as | Which blocks give it their drops: an iron one gets diamonds from their ore, a stone one does not. Choose one of: Wood, Gold (as wood), Stone, Iron, Diamond, Netherite. |
| Mining speed | How fast it mines what it is the tool for, which is how long mining takes: stone takes 0.4 s at 6 (iron), 0.6 s at 4 (stone), 1.15 s at 2 (wood). A square breaks when its middle does. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Breaks at once | One block, or a square across the face it mines, as a hammer does, outlined in the game before it breaks. Each block of the square costs one use and gives its own drops. Choose one of: One block, Three by three, Five by five, Seven by seven, Nine by nine, Eleven by eleven. |
| Goes this deep | How many blocks deep the square goes, straight into the face it mines. One is just the square. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Used on a block | What it does where it is used, as the game's own tool does: strips a log as an axe, tills earth as a hoe, makes a path as a shovel. Choose one of: Nothing, Strips, as an axe, Tills, as a hoe, Makes a path, as a shovel. |

### Weapon

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Damage | What one full hit takes, where a heart is 2: an iron sword does 6, a diamond one 7. From 1 to 1000. |
| Hits a second | How often a full strength hit can land: a sword 1.6, an axe 0.9. From 0.1 to 20. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Effect level | How strong the effect of a hit is: Poison 2 hurts twice as fast as Poison 1. From 1 to 10. |
| Sets alight for | Seconds a hit sets what it hits on fire; nought sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |

### Wears out

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Uses before it breaks | How many blocks it mines, hits it lands or hits it takes before it breaks: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mended with | What mends it in an anvil, such as an iron ingot, or one of this mod's own things. |
| Comes enchanted with | Enchantments it has from the first time a player holds it, the game's own or your own, each at its level. Each row has: Enchantment, Level. |
| Enchants how well | How good the enchantments it is offered are: iron 14, diamond 10, gold 22. From 0 to 50. |

### Acts on many blocks

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| What it does | Line: blocks in a straight run from the marked corner to the block used on. Wall: a wall standing on that run, as high as the two corners are apart. Box: the whole box between them. Copy: the box between the marked corner and the block used on is copied, then each use pastes it. Tree: mining a log fells every log of the tree. Vein: mining a block breaks every joined block of its kind. Choose one of: A line, A wall, A box, Copy and paste, Fell a tree, Mine a vein. |
| At most | The most blocks one action places, copies or breaks, 1 to 4096. From 1 to 4096. |
| Places | The block it places: the one in the player's other hand, or one chosen here. Choose one of: Off-hand block, A chosen block. |
| Block | The block it places, picked by its name in the game's list of blocks. |
| Only | The blocks it starts on: one block, or a group of blocks such as every ore. Empty: any block; a tree always starts on a log. |
| Uses up blocks | Each block placed is taken from the player's inventory, as placing it by hand would; off, it places for free. In creative it is always free. |
| Turns with you | A paste is turned as far as the player has turned since the copy: copied facing north, pasted facing east, it is turned a quarter, doors and stairs too. |
| Outline first | While it is held, what it would place, copy or break is outlined round the block under the cross, before anything is done. |
| Can undo | Used in the air while sneaking, it puts back what its last action changed and gives the blocks back, up to ten actions back. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Mines, Weapon, Wears out, Acts on many blocks.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Upgrade](thing-upgrade.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Face part](thing-facePart.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-upgrade

# Upgrade

An item a player uses on a placed block that takes upgrades: it goes in and makes the block faster, bigger, quicker to move things or cheaper to run.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Upgrade


## What you can set

### An upgrade

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| It adds to | Speed: the block works faster. Capacity: it holds more of everything. Rate: things move in and out of it faster. Efficiency: it uses less energy for the same work. Range: it reaches farther (a channel's range, an altar's reach, what its rules read). Energy: it uses more energy for the same work, or less with a share below nothing. Choose one of: Speed, Capacity, Rate, Efficiency, Range, Energy use, Nothing: only what it gives. |
| By | How much each one adds: 50 makes one upgrade half as much again, two of them twice. From 1 to 1000 percent. |
| Tier | Its tier, 1 to 5: it adds its share once for each tier, and goes only into a block that takes its tier. From 1 to 5. |
| Goes into | The blocks that take it, picked from the list. None picked: every block that takes upgrades. |
| It also changes | More numbers the same upgrade changes, each by its own share for each of its tiers: a speed upgrade that uses 30 more energy, a range upgrade that slows by 20. Each row has: It adds to, By. |
| It gives | A plain amount it gives the block, not a share: a signal while something rides a belt, items let down into what is under it, the blocks things are thrown up or moved ahead at its end. Each upgrade put on gives it for each of its tiers. Each row has: What it gives, Amount. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: An upgrade.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Item](thing-item.md), [Crate](thing-lootCrate.md), [Backpack](thing-backpack.md), [Settings copier](thing-settingsCopier.md), [Letter](thing-letter.md), [Pocket](thing-pocket.md), [Storage disk](thing-storageDisk.md), [Disk for fluids](thing-fluidDisk.md), [Wireless terminal](thing-wirelessTerminal.md), [Structure finder](thing-structureFinder.md), [Pointer](thing-pointer.md), [Designator](thing-designator.md), [Item filter](thing-itemFilter.md), [Configurator](thing-configurator.md), [Face part](thing-facePart.md), [Waypoint compass](thing-waypointCompass.md), [Spell wand](thing-spellWand.md), [Spell book](thing-spellBook.md), [Spell scroll](thing-spellScroll.md), [Tool](thing-tool.md), [Weapon](thing-weapon.md), [Armor](thing-armour.md), [Food](thing-food.md), [Fuel](thing-fuel.md), [Bow](thing-bow.md), [Crossbow](thing-crossbow.md), [Shield](thing-shield.md), [Part](thing-part.md), [Tool of parts](thing-partsTool.md), [Golem-style creature](thing-partsCreature.md), [Battery](thing-battery.md), [Powered tool](thing-poweredTool.md), [Powered armour](thing-poweredArmour.md), [Building wand](thing-buildingWand.md), [Copy wand](thing-copyWand.md), [Capsule](thing-capsule.md), [Building plan](thing-buildingPlan.md), [Mob catcher](thing-mobCatcher.md), [Carving tool](thing-carvingTool.md), [Bag of pieces](thing-bitBag.md), [Shape pattern](thing-shapePattern.md), [Tree axe](thing-treeAxe.md), [Vein pickaxe](thing-veinPickaxe.md), [Module](thing-module.md), [Building tool](thing-builder.md), [Thrown weapon](thing-thrown.md), [Music disc](thing-musicDisc.md), [Shears](thing-shears.md), [Fishing rod](thing-fishingRod.md), [Tool for everything](thing-multiTool.md), [Hat](thing-hat.md), [Vehicle part](thing-vehiclePart.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-value

# Value

A number or a list kept by an item, the player, a team or the world: Energy, XP, Kills, the foods a player has eaten.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Value


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Value](editor-value.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What a player reads in the tooltip. |
| Saved as | The name it is saved as in the item's data, which a piece of your own code reads. |
| Kept by | The item that keeps it; each of that item a player holds keeps its own. |
| Shared by | Whose number it is: each player's alone, one shared by the player's team (the game's own teams), or one for the whole world. Choose one of: Each player alone, The player's team, The whole world. |
| Starts at | What a new one of the item has. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most | The most it can hold; adding past it stops there. From 1 to 1000000000. |
| Holds | A number, a list of items, or words. A list is such as the foods the player has eaten: its number is how many items it holds, and rules add to it, take from it and ask whether it has one. Words are what a player types into a screen's text field. A list is each player's own. Choose one of: A number, A list of items, Words. |
| Tooltip if in the list | A line on an item's tooltip while the list holds that item, such as Eaten. Empty says nothing. |
| Tooltip if not | A line on an item's tooltip while the list does not hold it, such as Not eaten yet. Empty says nothing. |
| Tooltip on | Which items carry the line: foods only, or every item. Choose one of: Foods, Every item. |
| Comes back | How much it gains by itself each second, toward its most (a mana that refills); less than nought drains it. Nought leaves it to the rules. From -1000000000 to 1000000000 perSecond. |
| Shown | Where a player sees it: a bar under the item's picture, a line of its tooltip, both, or nowhere. Choose one of: Bar and tooltip, Bar, Tooltip, Nowhere. |
| Bar color | The color of its bar under the item's picture. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Item](editor-item.md), [The player](editor-player.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-vehicle

# Vehicle

Something to ride that is not alive, beyond the boat: a cart, a motor boat, a broom or an airship, a minecart of its own, a ride along a path. Steered with the game's own keys, with seats, fuel, cargo and parts.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Vehicle


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Vehicle](editor-vehicle.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What players see it called. |
| Game name | The name the game knows it by, in small letters. |
| Goes | How it goes: on the ground, on water, in the air, on the game's rails, or along a path of blocks with its riders inside. Choose one of: On the ground, On water, In the air, On rails, Along a path. |
| Looks like | The game's own minecart, with a block in it, or a model of its own. Choose one of: The game's minecart, Its own model. |
| Block in the cart | A block drawn inside the cart, by its game name, as a chest or a furnace in the game's own carts. Empty shows none. |
| Model | The model it is drawn by, made in the model editor. Its front is the way it goes. |
| Top speed | How fast it goes at most, in blocks a second. A horse runs about 10, a boat about 8. From 0 to 60 blocksPerSecond. |
| Climb | How fast it rises with the jump key and sinks with the sprint key, in blocks a second. From 0 to 40 blocksPerSecond. |
| Flies by | How it flies: hovering (a broom, a drone: the jump key rises, the sprint key sinks), on wings (a plane: its speed lifts it, it banks to turn and glides without power), or by thrust (a rocket: its engine against its weight). Choose one of: Hovering, Wings, Thrust. |
| Take-off speed | How fast it must go before its wings lift it, in blocks a second. Slower in the air, it stalls and drops its nose. From 0 to 60 blocksPerSecond. |
| Thrust | How hard its engine pushes up while the jump key fires it. More thrust than weight lifts it; a rule may set it from its engine blocks. From 0 to 100000. |
| Weight | How heavy it is against its thrust. A rule may set it from the blocks it is built of. From 0.01 to 100000. |
| Path of | The block it follows, by its game name, or a tag after a #. It goes straight on, turns where the line turns, takes the side its rider looks to where the line splits, and stops at the end. |
| Seats | How many can ride it. The first one on drives. From 1 to 8. |
| Fuel | What it needs to go: nothing, items put in, a fluid by the bucket, or whatever its rules give it. Empty, it stops. Choose one of: Nothing, Items put in, A fluid, What its rules give. |
| Fuel item | The item it burns, by its game name, or a tag after a #. Used on it, or kept in its cargo, it fills it. |
| Fuel fluid | The fluid it runs on, by its game name. A bucket of it used on it fills it, and the bucket comes back empty. |
| Fuel it holds | The most fuel it holds. From 1 to 1000000. |
| Fuel from one | How much fuel one item or one bucket gives. From 0 to 1000000. |
| Fuel used | How much fuel a second of going takes. Standing still takes none; holding its height in the air does. From 0 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Cargo | Rows of nine slots it carries, opened by crouching and using it. 0 carries nothing. From 0 to 6. |
| Part slots | How many parts a player can put in by using a part on it. From 0 to 8. |
| Its item | The item it drops when it breaks, and gives back when it packs up. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Animation](editor-animation.md), [Block](editor-block.md), [Item](editor-item.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-vehiclePart

# Vehicle part

An item put into a vehicle by using it on it, that works there every so often: breaks the blocks ahead, harvests crops, lights the way, shoots, blows up, or what its own rules say.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Vehicle part


## What you can set

### Vehicle part

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Does | Its work in a vehicle. Anything else is said in its rules, under Every time it works in a vehicle. Choose one of: Only its rules, Breaks the blocks ahead, Harvests and plants crops, Sets torches where it is dark, Throws cargo ahead, Blows up on a crash or an activator rail, Picks up items round it, Shoots, Sets blocks from its cargo ahead. |
| Reach | How far it works, in blocks: how far ahead a drill breaks, how far round a farmer looks, how strong a blast is. From 1 to 8 blocks. |
| How often | How often it works while the vehicle runs. From 0.05 to 60 seconds. |
| Fuel a time | The vehicle's fuel each time it works. With too little, it waits. From 0 to 100000. |
| Adds cargo | Rows of nine slots it adds to the vehicle's cargo, as a chest. From 0 to 3. |
| Shoots | The projectile it shoots, by its game name: an arrow, a fireball, or a projectile of the mod's own. |
| Aims | Straight ahead of the vehicle, or at the nearest monster within eight blocks for each block of reach. Choose one of: Straight ahead, At the nearest monster. |

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-veinPickaxe

# Vein pickaxe

A pickaxe that mines a whole joined vein of ore from one block, outlining the vein while it is aimed at.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > Vein pickaxe


## What you can set

### Mines

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Blocks it is for | The blocks it is the tool for: choose a group of blocks (all that a pickaxe or an axe mines) or single blocks. |
| Strong as | Which blocks give it their drops: an iron one gets diamonds from their ore, a stone one does not. Choose one of: Wood, Gold (as wood), Stone, Iron, Diamond, Netherite. |
| Mining speed | How fast it mines what it is the tool for, which is how long mining takes: stone takes 0.4 s at 6 (iron), 0.6 s at 4 (stone), 1.15 s at 2 (wood). A square breaks when its middle does. From 0.5 to 100. |
| Breaks at once | One block, or a square across the face it mines, as a hammer does, outlined in the game before it breaks. Each block of the square costs one use and gives its own drops. Choose one of: One block, Three by three, Five by five, Seven by seven, Nine by nine, Eleven by eleven. |
| Goes this deep | How many blocks deep the square goes, straight into the face it mines. One is just the square. From 1 to 16 blocks. |
| Used on a block | What it does where it is used, as the game's own tool does: strips a log as an axe, tills earth as a hoe, makes a path as a shovel. Choose one of: Nothing, Strips, as an axe, Tills, as a hoe, Makes a path, as a shovel. |

### Weapon

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Damage | What one full hit takes, where a heart is 2: an iron sword does 6, a diamond one 7. From 1 to 1000. |
| Hits a second | How often a full strength hit can land: a sword 1.6, an axe 0.9. From 0.1 to 20. |
| A hit gives | An effect every hit gives what it hits. Choose one of: Nothing extra, Speed, Slowness, Strength, Weakness, Regeneration, Poison, Glowing, Invisibility, Levitation, Fire resistance, Night vision, Jump boost. |
| For | How long the effect of a hit lasts. From 1 to 600 seconds. |
| Effect level | How strong the effect of a hit is: Poison 2 hurts twice as fast as Poison 1. From 1 to 10. |
| Sets alight for | Seconds a hit sets what it hits on fire; nought sets nothing alight. From 0 to 60 seconds. |

### Wears out

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Uses before it breaks | How many blocks it mines, hits it lands or hits it takes before it breaks: iron 250, diamond 1561. From 1 to 100000. |
| Mended with | What mends it in an anvil, such as an iron ingot, or one of this mod's own things. |
| Comes enchanted with | Enchantments it has from the first time a player holds it, the game's own or your own, each at its level. Each row has: Enchantment, Level. |
| Enchants how well | How good the enchantments it is offered are: iron 14, diamond 10, gold 22. From 0 to 50. |

### Acts on many blocks

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| What it does | Line: blocks in a straight run from the marked corner to the block used on. Wall: a wall standing on that run, as high as the two corners are apart. Box: the whole box between them. Copy: the box between the marked corner and the block used on is copied, then each use pastes it. Tree: mining a log fells every log of the tree. Vein: mining a block breaks every joined block of its kind. Choose one of: A line, A wall, A box, Copy and paste, Fell a tree, Mine a vein. |
| At most | The most blocks one action places, copies or breaks, 1 to 4096. From 1 to 4096. |
| Places | The block it places: the one in the player's other hand, or one chosen here. Choose one of: Off-hand block, A chosen block. |
| Block | The block it places, picked by its name in the game's list of blocks. |
| Only | The blocks it starts on: one block, or a group of blocks such as every ore. Empty: any block; a tree always starts on a log. |
| Uses up blocks | Each block placed is taken from the player's inventory, as placing it by hand would; off, it places for free. In creative it is always free. |
| Turns with you | A paste is turned as far as the player has turned since the copy: copied facing north, pasted facing east, it is turned a quarter, doors and stairs too. |
| Outline first | While it is held, what it would place, copy or break is outlined round the block under the cross, before anything is done. |
| Can undo | Used in the air while sneaking, it puts back what its last action changed and gives the blocks back, up to ten actions back. |

Every item also has the settings on the [Item](editor-item.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Mines, Weapon, Wears out, Acts on many blocks.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-fluidReactions

# When fluids meet

What happens where a fluid meets another fluid or a block: lava meeting water makes obsidian, your own fluid meeting lava makes a block or drops an item. Each row says which fluids, what it makes, where, how often, and the sound and particles. It starts with the game's own two rows, which you can change or take away.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > When fluids meet


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [When fluids meet](editor-fluidReactions.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What this table is called in your project. |
| Game name | The name the table is written under in the game's files, in small letters with underscores. |
| When fluids meet | One row for each meeting. A row is checked wherever the first fluid has the other fluid or block touching it, as the fluid is placed and whenever a block beside it changes. Each row has: This fluid, When it is, Meets the fluid, Or meets the block, Makes, As a, Where, How often, Sound, Particles, On the side. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is written into the mod when you [Cook](glossary.md#cook) or press [Play](glossary.md#play).

## What it works with

It points at: [Fluid](editor-fluid.md).

## Picture

![When fluids meet](/media/docs/editor-fluidReactions.webp)

- [When fluids meet](editor-fluidReactions.md)
- [Templates and samples](templates-and-samples.md)
- [Glossary](glossary.md)

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-wirelessNode

# Wireless energy node

A block that sends the energy its cables bring on a channel, or, set to receive, gives out on its cables the energy the channel brings.

## How to add it

- New thing > Machines and networks > Wireless energy node


## What you can set

### Energy

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Most it holds | Its buffer. Set it to nothing for a cable, which holds nothing of its own. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| Most a second | The most that crosses this block each second. A run of cable carries as much as its narrowest one, not the sum of them. From 0 to 1000000000. |
| No limit | On: energy cross this block as fast as the blocks at both ends can give and take. The number above is ignored. |

### Connections

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Faces | Which of the six faces connect, and to what. Open the Connections tab to set them. |
| What arrives | A cable or a pipe passes it on and holds nothing. A machine, a tank or a battery keeps it. Choose one of: It keeps it, It passes it on. |
| Served before others | When several blocks want the same thing and there is not enough, the higher number is filled first. Equal numbers take turns. From -64 to 64. |
| Serves first | Whom what leaves it goes to first, for items, fluids and every stock: shared by priority, each block in turn, or the nearest along the pipes. Choose one of: By priority, Each in turn, The nearest. |
| Faces have colours | A coloured face joins only faces of its colour. Off, faces ignore colour. |
| Dyes a face steps through | How many of the sixteen dyes a channel can be set to. From 1 to 16. |
| Face modes | What pressing a face goes through, in order. Empty keeps Off, In, Out, Both. Each row has: Name, Colour, Does. |
| Players set each face | A player right-clicks a face with an empty hand and sets what it does on that placed block alone. The table is where every placed block starts. |
| Face screen | The screen a player opens by right-clicking a face of the placed block, laid out on the Face screen tab. Until it is changed there, the product draws its own rows. |
| Items a face filters | How many items a player can mark on a face, to let only those through or to keep them out. A mark is not the item: nothing is taken from the player. From 0 to 9. |
| Filter of your own | A piece of your own code that answers yes or no for each item, asked on every face beside the marks, for what the marks cannot say: damage, data, a stock level. |
| Speed upgrade | An item a player puts into a face's upgrade slot on its screen. Each one moves that face's rate again, eight at most; they drop when the block is broken. |
| Reserve room for items | An item riding through this pipe holds its place in the chest or machine it is going to, so two stacks never fight for one slot and nothing has to turn round. Turn it off and a stack just goes to the nearest place with room right now. |
| Item to link a chest | Pick an item and this block becomes a node that reaches a chest or machine without a cable. A player right-clicks the chest with the item, then right-clicks this block with it, and the network uses that chest as if it stood against the top of this block. Sneak and right-click the block to cut the link. Leave empty for a plain block. |
| How far a link reaches | The most blocks between this node and the chest it is linked to, in the same dimension. 0 means any distance. From 0 to 1024 blocks. |
| When it is broken | A block that carries more than one thing (items and fluid and energy, say) can come apart one thing at a time: mining it takes off the one added last and leaves the rest standing. Sneaking while you mine breaks the whole block. Choose one of: The whole block goes, One piece at a time. |
| Item for the items piece | What drops when the items part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the fluid piece | What drops when the fluid part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Item for the energy piece | What drops when the energy part is taken off, and what a player uses on the block to put it back. Leave empty and a part taken off is gone. |
| Holds parts | Face parts go on its faces, one a face and one in the middle, and covers take another block's look. A face with no part joins only blocks of this mod, never a chest. |
| Moves by itself | Its out sides push into the blocks beside them and its in sides pull from them, with no pipe between: a machine filling the chest next to it, a block emptying a cart in front of it. Works for items, fluids, energy and your own stocks. Choose one of: No, Pushes out, Pulls in, Pushes and pulls. |
| How much a second | How much it moves each second through each side: items, or the units of a fluid, energy or stock. From 1 to 100000 perSecond. |
| Holds a cart | Stops the cart that rolls up beside it while it works, so the cart stays until the block has moved all it can, or until a rule lets it go. Needs Moves by itself. Choose one of: No, Until it has nothing more to move, Until a rule lets it go. |
| Longest it holds | The most seconds it holds one cart, so a cart is never kept for good. 0 holds as long as it takes. From 0 to 86400 seconds. |
| Destroys what none take | What no other block on its pipes takes is destroyed here, after every other block had its turn. Marks on its sides say what it destroys; with none, everything. |
| Fills a block | Whether its sides fill a block whenever it has room, or only while it holds none of what comes (one stack in each furnace, never two). Choose one of: Whenever it has room, Only when it holds none. |
| Stands in for a far block | Linked to a far chest or machine with the linking item, this block is that chest to hoppers, pipes and other mods: what goes in here goes there, and what is taken from here comes from there. |
| Joins without a seam | Where an arm of this block meets one of these, neither draws the end of its arm, so a run of them reads as one tube. A machine or a chest it meets keeps its end and its plate. Choose one of: As its pictures say, Blocks like it, Every cable or pipe it joins, Nothing. |

### Linked by a channel

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Channel | The name that links it: blocks on the same channel are linked. A player renames a block in an anvil before placing it to put that one on another channel. |
| On its channel it | Sends: what it holds, and the redstone reaching it, go out on the channel, and its faces take in. Receives: it gets what is sent, gives out the channel's signal, and its faces give out. Shares: it holds what every sharing block on the channel holds, one chest or one tank in many places, in every world, kept by the world even while none of them is loaded. Choose one of: sends, receives, shares, jams. |
| Carries a redstone signal | A sending block sends the redstone that reaches it; a receiving block gives out the strongest signal on its channel. |
| Reaches | How far the link reaches, in blocks. 0 reaches anywhere, in every world. From 0 to 100000 blocks. |
| Only its owner's | The channel belongs to the player who placed it: another player's block on a channel of the same name is not linked to it. |

Every block also has the settings on the [Block](editor-block.md) page.

## What it becomes in the game

It is added to the game, so a player needs your mod to see it.

It comes with these abilities already on: Energy, Connections, Linked by a channel.

## What it works with

It points at: [Model](editor-model.md), [Sound](editor-sound.md), [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Item](editor-item.md), [Code](editor-code.md).

Other things that open the same editor: [Block](thing-block.md), [Machine](thing-machine.md), [Generator](thing-generator.md), [Cable](thing-cable.md), [Pipe](thing-pipe.md), [Item pipe](thing-itemPipe.md), [Tank](thing-tank.md), [Transmitter](thing-wirelessTransmitter.md), [Receiver](thing-wirelessReceiver.md), [Shared chest](thing-sharedChest.md), [Shared tank](thing-sharedTank.md), [Chest](thing-chest.md), [Drawer](thing-drawer.md), [Storage crate](thing-crate.md), [Mailbox](thing-mailbox.md), [Trade station](thing-tradeStation.md), [Asking chest](thing-askingChest.md), [Terminal](thing-terminal.md), [Storage cell](thing-storageCell.md), [Storage cable](thing-storageCable.md), [Drive](thing-drive.md), [Network heart](thing-networkHeart.md), [Dense cable](thing-denseCable.md), [Link](thing-storeLink.md), [Access point](thing-accessPoint.md), [Crafter](thing-crafter.md), [Pattern table](thing-patternTable.md), [Matter tank](thing-matterTank.md), [Altar](thing-altar.md), [Pedestal](thing-pedestal.md), [Formed machine](thing-formedMachine.md), [Machine casing](thing-machineCasing.md), [Waypoint](thing-waypointBlock.md), [Aiming block](thing-aimingBlock.md), [Berry bush](thing-berryBush.md), [Matter pipe](thing-matterPipe.md), [Assembly station](thing-assemblyStation.md), [Carved block](thing-carvedBlock.md), [Ore](thing-ore.md), [Crop](thing-crop.md), [Plant](thing-plant.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-ownWord

# Word of your own

A few lines you name once and use in any rule as one line: it is given as many things as it needs, and it can give back an answer.

## How to add it

- New thing > Logic and code > Word of your own


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [Word of your own](editor-ownWord.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | What the word is called where a rule uses it, such as Greet or Bonus for. |
| First thing it is given | A name for something the rule that uses this word hands it, such as who or how much. Leave its kind at Nothing to hand it nothing. |
| Which is | What kind of thing it is given here. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no, A player, A mob, A place, An item. |
| Second thing it is given | A name for something the rule that uses this word hands it, such as who or how much. Leave its kind at Nothing to hand it nothing. |
| Which is | What kind of thing it is given here. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no, A player, A mob, A place, An item. |
| More things it is given | As many more things as the word needs, each with a name and what it is. The rule that uses the word fills each one. Each row has: Called, Which is. |
| It gives back | What the rule that uses this word gets back from it: nothing, or a number, words, or yes or no, set by a Give back line. Choose one of: Nothing, A number, Words, Yes or no. |

## What it becomes in the game

It is not part of the game itself: it describes another mod or a file, so it has no side to choose.

## What it works with

It does not point at other things.

# https://modryos.com/docs/thing-worldEvent

# World event

Something that happens to a whole dimension for a while: a blood sky, a fog bank, an aurora, a rift. When it starts, how long it lasts, what the players see and what it does round them. Rules start it, end it and ask whether it is on.

## How to add it

- New thing > Blocks and items > World event


## What you can set

The main settings are below. The [World event](editor-worldEvent.md) editor lists every setting.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name of the event, as you and your players know it. |
| Game name | The event's name inside the game files. Lower case letters, numbers and underscores. |
| Starts by itself | When the game rolls the chance below: at nightfall, midnight, sunrise or noon each day, or every minute. Never leaves it to your rules. Choose one of: At nightfall, At midnight, At sunrise, At noon, Every minute, Only when a rule starts it. |
| Chance each time | How likely it is to start each time the game rolls for it. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| In dimensions | The dimensions where it can start by itself. Empty means every dimension. Each row has: Dimension. |
| Lasts | How many seconds it lasts. A rule can start it for another length. From 1 to 86400 seconds. |
| Sky tint | The colour laid over the sky half of every screen in the dimension while it lasts. |
| Sky tint strength | How strong the tint is at its fullest, strongest at the top. Nought leaves the sky alone. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Fog colour | The colour laid over the whole screen while it lasts. |
| Fog thickness | How thick the fog is at its fullest. Nought brings no fog. It fades in the last five seconds. From 0 to 100 percent. |
| Particles round each player | Particles thrown round every player in the dimension each second while it lasts: ash, spores, rain of sparks. Each row has: Particle, Each second, Spread over. |
| Pushes area values | An area value it adds to each second at every player's place while it lasts: a corruption rising, a rift charging. Each row has: Area value, Each second. |
| Calls mobs | Mobs that appear near each player while it lasts, so a night brings its own creatures. Each row has: Mob, Chance each second, No more than, Appears. |

## What it becomes in the game

It runs on the player's side of the game.

## What it works with

It points at: [Particle](editor-particle.md), [Area value](editor-areaValue.md), [Mob](editor-creature.md).

# https://modryos.com/docs/templates-and-samples

# Templates and samples

A template adds a thing that already works. A sample is a small finished mod you copy and change. Your copy goes in its own folder and the sample stays as it is.

## Templates

Add one with New thing > the category shown > its name.

| Template | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Crafting station (Machines and networks) | A block with a 3x3 grid and a result, like a crafting table. |
| Powered machine (Machines and networks) | A machine with a recipe that uses energy and time. |
| Generator with fuel (Machines and networks) | A generator that burns coal into energy, ready to run. |
| Electric furnace (Machines and networks) | A machine that cooks sand into glass using energy. |
| Fluid tank (Machines and networks) | A tank that holds 8000 mB and opens its own screen. |
| Ore with a pickaxe (Blocks and items) | An ore that needs an iron pickaxe, its ingot and a pickaxe. |
| Set (Blocks and items) | Makes an ore, its ingot, tools and armor, with recipes. |

## Samples

Start screen > Samples > pick one > Make my copy.

### Ruby Gear

Ruby ore to mine, and a katana and a pickaxe made from rubies.

**What is inside:** 3 items, 1 block, 3 recipes.

**In the game, try:**

- Open the creative inventory and search Ruby.
- Mine Ruby Ore with an iron pickaxe: it drops a Ruby. Three rubies and two sticks make a Ruby Pickaxe.

### Ember Ore

A glowing ore that drops Ember Ingots, and a chest that holds more.

**What is inside:** 1 item, 2 blocks, 1 recipe.

**In the game, try:**

- Search Ember in the creative inventory.
- Break Ember Ore with a pickaxe: it drops Ember Ingots.

### Frost Magic

A frost wand, a frost blade, a chilly enchantment and a potion of frost.

**What is inside:** 3 items, 1 block, 1 potion, 1 effect, 1 enchantment, 1 painting.

**In the game, try:**

- Search Frost in the creative inventory.
- Hit a mob with the Frost Blade and watch it freeze.

### Wyrm

A flying wyrm with a boss bar that drops dragon scales when it falls.

**What is inside:** 1 item, 1 creature.

**In the game, try:**

- Take the Wyrm spawn egg from the creative inventory and use it.
- Defeat it to get Dragon scales.

### Ember Fox

A fiery fox you tame with sweet berries. It follows you around.

**What is inside:** 1 creature.

**In the game, try:**

- Use the Ember Fox spawn egg from the creative inventory.
- Feed it sweet berries until hearts show: now it follows you.

### Trail Quests

A quest book that walks you from your first log to the Nether.

**What is inside:** 1 item, 1 quest book.

**In the game, try:**

- You get the Trailhead Book when you join a world. Open it.
- Chop a log to finish the first quest.

### Hearthwood

An adventure and cooking mod: pies, a bestiary, an ember altar, a longbow and two armour sets.

**What is inside:** 4 foods and a cookbook, a bestiary book, a skill tree with 6 skills, an altar and 4 pedestals with carved models, a longbow and 2 armour sets, a magnet with a charge bar, 3 HUD gauges.

**In the game, try:**

- Craft a Golden Cookie from gold nuggets and a cookie.
- Open the Hearth Cookbook and the Wild Things book.
- Build the Ember Altar inside a ring of Stone Pedestals.

### Hidden Stats

Shows what the game hides: saturation, tool wear and armour toughness.

**What is inside:** 3 HUD meters.

**In the game, try:**

- Eat something and watch the saturation above your hunger bar.
- Hold a pickaxe to see how much wear it has left, or wear diamond armour to see its toughness.

### Garden Blocks

Brick stairs and walls, a wooden fence, gate and door, flowers and tomatoes.

**What is inside:** 11 blocks.

**In the game, try:**

- Search Garden in the creative inventory.
- Build a little garden with the fence, the gate and the bluebells.

### Carved Helm

A carved helm to wear on your head and a power chest on your back.

**What is inside:** 2 items, 1 block.

**In the game, try:**

- Search Carved Helm in the creative inventory.
- Put it on and press F5 to see it.

### Brass Works

Brass dust, ingots, rods, plates and gears, each made from the last.

**What is inside:** 5 items, 5 recipes.

**In the game, try:**

- Open a crafting table and search Brass in the recipe book.
- Turn Brass Dust into an Ingot, then into a Gear.

# https://modryos.com/docs/versions-and-loaders

# Versions and loaders

A [loader](glossary.md#loader) is the program that runs mods in Minecraft. Modryos makes mods for NeoForge and Fabric.

## What the studio makes mods for

Minecraft numbers its newer versions by year: 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3 are versions from 2026, newer than 1.21.11. One project makes a mod for every version and loader you tick.

| Target | Loader |
| --- | --- |
| NeoForge 1.21.1 | NeoForge |
| Fabric 1.21.1 | Fabric |
| NeoForge 26.3 | NeoForge |
| Fabric 26.3 | Fabric |
| NeoForge 26.2 | NeoForge |
| Fabric 26.2 | Fabric |
| NeoForge 1.21.11 | NeoForge |
| Fabric 1.21.11 | Fabric |
| NeoForge 26.1.2 | NeoForge |
| Fabric 26.1.2 | Fabric |

Minecraft 1.20.1 comes after version 1.0. Packs only 1.21.1.

## Where you pick them

- **New project:** the **Works with** line lists the loaders. At least one stays ticked.
- **Later, any time:** open **Mod details** and use **Made for** to add or remove a loader and version.
- **Which one Play opens:** the toolbar's **Play on** picker. It only lists what **Made for** has.

## Which jar your friend needs

Ask your friend two things: which loader they use (NeoForge or Fabric) and which Minecraft version. Give them the [jar](glossary.md#jar) made for that pair. A Fabric friend also needs [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) in their mods folder. The jars are in your project's release folder, see [Export](export.md).

## Many versions in one project

One project can list many [targets](glossary.md#target). You build the thing once; [Cook](glossary.md#cook) makes one jar for each target you pick and puts them side by side in the project's release folder. Before it makes anything, Cook shows what will not carry over to each version. [Play](glossary.md#play) opens the target you choose under "Play on".

## Related pages

- [Glossary](glossary.md)
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

---

# https://modryos.com/docs/publishing

# Publish on Modrinth and CurseForge

Modryos does not upload anything for you. It writes the texts and files each site asks for, so you can paste them.

## The store files

When you [make the mod file](export.md), Modryos also writes a `stores` folder inside `release/<version>/`:

- `stores/modrinth/` and `stores/curseforge/` hold one file per [jar](glossary.md#jar) and one page file for the project.
- `stores/README.txt` says what to paste where, and what to check by hand.
- `MADE_WITH_AI.md` is the note about AI help, with a ready text for each site.

Nothing in them is sent anywhere. If something is missing, such as a description, a logo or a licence link, Modryos tells you in the README.

## Your store ids

Make your mod's page on the store first. Then open **Mod details** and fill in **Modrinth project id** and **CurseForge project id**. Every cook then puts them in the store files, ready to paste. A CurseForge id is a number shown on the project's page.

## The AI note

Each site has its own rule about AI-made content. The short version: say so if an AI made part of your mod.

A sentence to copy when nothing was AI-made (the beta): "No AI was used to make this mod." Only write it if it is true, also for pictures and code made outside the studio.

A sentence to copy when an AI helped: "Part of this mod was made with help from an AI tool."

Modryos records what an AI agent made in the studio. `MADE_WITH_AI.md` turns that into a short text. While Modryos AI is closed in the beta, the record says no AI help was recorded in the studio. If you used an outside tool, the studio cannot see it, so tell the site yourself.

`MADE_WITH_AI.md` starts with a summary such as "No AI help was recorded in the studio for this project". Then it has one text for Modrinth, one for CurseForge and one for Nexus Mods. When an agent helped, it says how much of your project the agent changed.

On Modrinth the file also says whether to switch on **Contains AI-generated content**.

## Upload

Each site has its own upload page. Use the files above for the descriptions and versions. Then check the site's game version names, because Modryos does not check those.
